Depicting Goodridge's bared breasts surrounded by white cloth, the portrait miniature is painted on a piece of ivory . It was originally backed with paper and is now in a modern frame. Goodridge presented the breasts as youthful and individualized, employing a frontal view that showed the area from the collarbone to just underneath the breasts. She gave the portrait to statesman Daniel Webster , who was a frequent subject and possible lover, following the death of his wife; she may have intended to provoke him into marrying her. Although Webster married someone else, his family held onto the portrait until the 1980s, when it was auctioned at Christie's and purchased by Gloria and Richard Manney. The painting was acquired by the Metropolitan Museum of Art in 2006. It has been read as a work of erotica , as well as an expression of Goodridge's confident sexuality. Four commands were raised in 1940, early in World War II, to oversee operations, training and maintenance within their geographical boundaries. In 1941–42 the structure was revised to make a total of five commands, along with four functional groups that assumed the training and maintenance roles. The area commands focused on operations until the end of hostilities. A new area command covering RAAF units in New Guinea existed from 1944 to 1947. By the early 1950s, the area command structure was no longer considered appropriate, and in 1953 it was transformed into Home Command (controlling operations), Training Command , and Maintenance Command . The area commands ceded their authority to these functional commands in 1954, and were disbanded by the end of 1956. ( This article is part of a featured topic : RAAF area commands .) Adele wrote the song with its producer, Greg Kurstin . Columbia Records released it as the album's lead single on 15 October 2021. A torch ballad , "Easy on Me" places emphasis on Adele's vocals over piano instrumentation. In the song, she addresses her divorce and pleads for forgiveness and understanding. It received positive reviews from music critics, who praised her vocals and the lyrics. "Easy on Me" won the Grammy Award for Best Pop Solo Performance and the Brit Award for Song of the Year . The song reached number one on the charts in several countries. Xavier Dolan directed the music video, which references previous Adele videos and depicts her moving out of the house featured in the " Hello " music video. She performed it at the NRJ Music Awards , on her television specials, and at the concert residency Weekends with Adele . Many artists sang cover versions of it. It was inspired by The Hunger , a 1983 erotic vampire horror film. Typically for early-career McQueen, the designs emphasised female sexuality and sharp tailoring, and it was his first collection to include menswear. The runway show was staged at London's Natural History Museum on 23 October 1995. Imagery of sexuality, violence, and death predominated, most notably in a corset of translucent plastic with real worms encased inside. Models bared their breasts and flashed obscene gestures on the runway, and the show concluded with McQueen mooning the audience. Critical reception was mixed, with some seeing McQueen's work as immature or misogynistic. Retrospective analysis has focused on the cinematic inspiration behind the collection and the gothic imagery of the worm corset. Garments from The Hunger appeared in the retrospective Alexander McQueen: Savage Beauty . Launched on 17 October 1891, she was an ironclad battleship with a main battery of heavy guns mounted on the centerline and the first use of Belleville boilers. She formed the basis for subsequent designs, beginning with Charles Martel . When completed in 1893, Brennus was very top-heavy and had to be rebuilt over the next three years before she was ready to enter service. She spent the majority of her service in the Mediterranean Squadron and she served as its flagship early in her career. As newer battleships were commissioned into the fleet, Brennus was relegated to the Reserve Squadron in the early 1900s and then served as a training ship . The ship was decommissioned before the First World War began in August 1914 and disarmed in 1915. She served as a source of spare parts and equipment for other ships during the war. Her hulk was stricken from the naval register in 1919 and was scrapped three years later. Producer A. H. Woods staged it on Broadway ; it premiered on October 18, 1921, and was one of the most successful plays of the season. The play is a bedroom farce about former couple Gloria Graham and Wally Deane, both movie actors, whose marriage was so brief that the press speculated about Gloria's virginity. Because it contained suggestive dialog and the female cast wore revealing clothes, the production was considered highly risqué at the time. The script alluded to a contemporary scandal involving actor Roscoe Arbuckle . Reviewers panned the play as unfunny and vulgar. A magistrate ruled the play was obscene, and obscenity charges were brought against Woods, but a grand jury declined to indict him. Woods promoted the controversy to increase ticket sales. The play had no long-term literary impact and was never published, but it stimulated arguments over censorship of theatrical performances. There are no known texts written in Cappadocian, although classical Greek writers identified Cappadocian as distinct from Greek, and a few Greek words were attributed to a Cappadocian origin. The language also influenced the pronunciation of Greek spoken by Cappadocians, whose accent was infamous among classical authors. Although Cappadocian does not have a secure linguistic classification, it likely belonged to the Anatolian branch of the Indo-European languages , probably as a relative or descendant of Luwian . Prior to the modern understanding of Anatolian languages in the twentieth century, Cappadocian was variously considered part of the Semitic family, part of other known branches of Indo-European, or part of an Anatolian language family unrelated to any other known languages. The Monster's modus operandi was to abuse women verbally with lewd and suggestive comments, then attack them with a knife (cartoon pictured) . The philanthropist John Julius Angerstein arranged a reward of 100 guineas (equivalent to £13,000 in 2025) for the capture and conviction of the Monster. More than 30 men were taken to Bow Street Magistrates' Court with their accusers hoping to claim the reward; all were released. Renwick Williams was arrested when one of the attacked women claimed to recognise him as the attacker. He was found guilty, despite having an alibi for at least one of the attacks. There is doubt among some historians whether he was the attacker as no hard or forensic evidence was ever found. It is likely that copycat attacks took place, particularly as some of the assaults were recorded as being committed by a group of men. Born into a peasant family in Anhui , Zhu grew up amid famine, epidemics, and unrest under the Mongol-led Yuan dynasty . Orphaned at 16, he briefly lived as a novice monk before joining the Red Turban rebels in 1352. Rising rapidly, he captured Nanjing in 1356, established a regional regime, and defeated rival rebels. In 1368, he proclaimed the Ming dynasty , adopted the era name Hongwu , and expelled the Yuan from China proper . During his 30-year reign, he restored stability after decades of war, strengthened state institutions, promoted agriculture, and maintained a disciplined army while seeking to limit civilian suffering. He died in 1398 and was succeeded by his grandson, the Jianwen Emperor , who was overthrown in 1402 by Zhu Di , later known as the Yongle Emperor. During the British colonial era, thuggee came to be represented and popularised as a secret pan-Indian fraternity of ritual stranglers with ancient origins, motivated by fanaticism and bloodlust. In the 1830s, colonial administrator William Henry Sleeman led a policing campaign against thuggee, supported by legal developments that facilitated convictions. The success of the 1839 novel Confessions of a Thug inspired a number of depictions in literature and film, among them Indiana Jones and the Temple of Doom (1984). Historians have since revised the 19th-century portrayal, generally viewing the Thugs as more or less ordinary criminals, or thuggee as a type of banditry . Control of the area gave either combatant access to southwestern German states and Rhine crossings. On 20 October, the French army under Jean-Victor Moreau retreated from Freiburg im Breisgau and established his army along a ridge of hills. The Austrian army led by Archduke Charles attacked the French flanks directly, and in force, which increased casualties for both sides. The French withdrew from the battlefield in good order and several days later crossed the Rhine at Huningue . Confusion in Vienna wasted any strategic advantage that Charles might have obtained and locked the Habsburg force into two sieges on the Rhine, when the troops were badly needed in northern Italy. The battle is commemorated on a monument in Vienna and on the Arc de Triomphe in Paris. Their original line-up comprised brothers Ray Davies and Dave Davies , Pete Quaife and Mick Avory . Emerging during the height of British rhythm and blues and Merseybeat , " You Really Got Me " (1964), their breakthrough third single written by Ray Davies, became an international hit, topping the charts in the United Kingdom and reaching the top 10 in the United States. They were part of the British Invasion until their 1965 American tour led to them being banned from touring there for a number of years. The Kinks are regarded as one of the most influential rock bands of the 1960s. They had seventeen top-20 singles and five top-10 albums in the UK, and five singles reached the top 10 on the US Billboard Hot 100 . The band has sold more than 50 million records worldwide. Among the first Chinese literary magazines marketed towards women, and the first to be edited mainly by women, it was founded by Gao Jianhua and Xu Xiaotian, her husband and cousin. The magazine often ran romance stories aimed at women, but contained sexually explicit depictions of women in its advertising, covers, and pictures, some sourced from European erotic postcards . Unlike its contemporaries, Eyebrow Talk ' s romances often centered on the desires of their female protagonists, frequently including love triangles between the protagonists and multiple men. Its libertine content ran afoul of a government advisory committee, who unanimously voted to ban it in 1916, making it the first Chinese magazine to be banned under charges of obscenity . Its association with lowbrow " Mandarin Duck and Butterfly " fiction prevented scholarly research for much of the 20th century. The 1986 New York Mets season began on April 8, 1986. It concluded on October 27 with a Mets victory in Game 7 of the 1986 World Series , for their second and most recent World Series title. The Mets had narrowly missed winning the NL East in 1985, but in 1986 were not seriously challenged, winning the division by 21½ games. They defeated the Houston Astros in six games in the NLCS , with the Mets erasing a three run ninth-inning deficit and winning Game 6 in sixteen innings. They played the Boston Red Sox in the World Series, and in Game 6 of that series, trailing three games to two, they rallied from two runs down with two outs and none on base in the tenth inning. They won that game on an error by Bill Buckner , winning Game 7 two days later. The 1986 Mets have been described as one of the best teams in MLB history, but their failure to sustain their success has marred the team's legacy. Many team members drank heavily and the 1986 Mets became known for their lifestyle off the field. In September 1864, the Confederates launched Price's Raid , an attempt to create a popular uprising against Union control of Missouri . After being forced to retreat, the Confederates halted to rest near Newtonia. On the afternoon of the 28th, Union pursuers caught up and surprised the Confederates. The main Confederate army withdrew, leaving a rear guard under Brigadier General Joseph O. Shelby . Shelby initially had a numerical advantage, and used it to outflank Blunt's shorter line. Blunt was considering a retreat shortly before sundown when reinforcements arrived in the form of Brigadier General John B. Sanborn and his brigade. Sanborn joined Blunt's line, and the Union troops counterattacked . Shelby ordered a retreat and was not pursued until October 30. Modern historians credit the Union with a victory at Newtonia. Located on the base of the Quimper Peninsula , the main stem originates from springs and ponds in the forested hills south of Discovery Bay . It flows south from its source, then turns east, then north, taking in tributaries before entering Chimacum Valley. It enters a ravine where it meets the sea in Port Hadlock-Irondale , creating a small estuary and an area of intertidal wetland as it enters Port Townsend Bay . The topography of the watershed was shaped by the Cordilleran ice sheet during the Last Glacial Maximum , which deposited large amounts of glacial outwash and sedimentary material. The area was the traditional lands of the Chemakum people , who were devastated by disease and massacres before the 1850s. The watershed was dredged and channelized during the early 20th century, turning the creek into a relatively straight channel. Environmental restoration projects help protect the spawning runs of coho salmon . He was a Province of Massachusetts Bay delegate to the Second Continental Congress and the leading advocate for American independence from Britain. After seconding the Lee Resolution , Adams served on the Committee of Five which drafted the United States Declaration of Independence . A dedicated diarist, Adams corresponded with his wife Abigail during this time, recording historical information on the era. In 1783 Adams was part of the American delegation that negotiated the Treaty of Paris , which formally ended the American Revolutionary War . Adams was the primary author of the 1780 Massachusetts Constitution , which influenced the 1789 United States Constitution , and he became the new nation's first vice president and second president. After his presidency, Adams returned to Peacefield , his Massachusetts home and farm. The zombie kills the teens, whose deaths are investigated by the police. The film was written to star mostly black actors but, at the request of investors, the characters' names were changed to more typically white names. While Jack Bravman was credited as director, John Fasano directed most of the film, causing problems with the production crew, who believed Fasano was the assistant director and ignored his directions. Zombie Nightmare was released direct-to-video by New World Video . It grossed C$ 1.5 million against a budget of $180,000. title: Sea balls - Wikipedia
text: Sea balls - Wikipedia Jump to content Search Search Sea balls 6 languages العربية Deutsch Français Igbo Italiano 中文 Edit links From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia Group of aquatic phenomena Not to be confused with Beach ball . "Aegagropiles" redirects here; not to be confused with Aegagropila . A Neptune ball on a sandy beach Sea balls are a group of aquatic phenomena. They form through the movement of discarded plant debris by water, which rolls up fibre into compact spheres. The most well-known examples, found on the coasts of the Mediterranean Sea , are formed from decayed leaf fibres of the seagrass species Posidonia oceanica , though other variants worldwide are made of different organic materials; Mediterranean sea balls are typically referred to as Neptune balls . Some researchers say that sea balls also encompass living plants such as Aegagropila . Neptune balls, and particularly fibres obtained from them, have been used for millennia, such as for making shoes, ancient medicine, or to caulk ships, though the balls' formation process and composition has only become clear since the late 19th century. Potential modern applications make use of the properties of Neptune balls which are rare in nature; for example, Neptune balls have been shown to be a good soundproofing material. Neptune balls would also be a more environmentally-friendly substitute for some synthetic materials. A study in 2018 and 2019 found that plastic waste , especially microplastics , has been captured in the process of Neptune ball formation; studies and people have found plastic in many Neptune balls in the Mediterranean. Consequently, Neptune balls have been suggested as an indicator of plastic pollution in the sea, which results have shown as a valid indicator as of 2026. Description [ edit ] Names and definitions [ edit ] Sea balls formed in the Mediterranean Sea are known by a variety of names. The term aegagropilae derives from the Ancient Greek αἴγαγρος ( aígagros , ' wild goat ' ) and πῖλος ( pîlos , ' felt, fur ' ), by analogy with the felted hairballs ( trichobezoars ) found in the stomachs of ruminants. [ 1 ] In English and scientific literature, they are also referred to as aegagropiles , Neptune balls , [ 2 ] [ 3 ] égagropiles , [ 4 ] egagropili , [ 5 ] Posidonia oceanica spheroids , [ 6 ] and by the Latin terms pilae stagnales , pilae marinae , pili marini , sphaerae marinae , globuli marini , and sphaerae thalassiae . [ 7 ] Historical Arabic sources recorded them as أُكَر الْبَحْر ( ʾukar al-baḥr or okr elbahr , ' balls of the sea ' ) and النَّبَاتِيّ ( an-nabātiyy or annabati , ' the botanical [one] ' ). [ 7 ] [ 8 ] Equivalent vernacular names include pelotes marines or pelotes-de-mer in French, [ 7 ] [ 9 ] [ a ] zeeballen in Dutch, motolini in Italian, and Seebälle in German. [ 7 ] [ b ] Historically, sea balls was used synonymously with Neptune balls and its equivalents, [ 12 ] though more recent literature applies the term more broadly to encompass Neptune balls, [ 5 ] other spheroids of marine material, [ 13 ] and fossilized specimens. [ 8 ] The German phycologist and botanist Bruno Schröder [ de ] distinguished between two categories: non-living sea balls, [ c ] such as Neptune balls, which are aggregates of detached plant debris rolled together by wave action; and living sea balls, [ d ] such as those of the algal genus Aegagropila , which develop through radial spherical growth. [ 7 ] The Canadian botanist W. F. Ganong drew a similar distinction between algal balls and wave-formed plant aggregations. [ 14 ] Formation [ edit ] Posidonia oceanica growing on the sea floor Neptune balls are formed out of the remains of Posidonia oceanica , a seagrass species endemic to the Mediterranean Sea. [ 1 ] In autumn, Posidonia oceanica loses its leaves . [ 15 ] When leaves shed, its leaf sheaths are buried by sedimentation in an accumulation of dead rhizomes and roots. [ 15 ] [ 16 ] As they are buried, the lignin -rich leaf sheaths are eroded, leaving fibres behind. [ 2 ] [ 15 ] The sea rolls the fibres into a spherical shape, creating Neptune balls. [ 1 ] [ e ] Then, ocean currents can dislodge Neptune balls from the sea floor; some drift into deeper waters and some are washed ashore. [ 2 ] [ 15 ] Though details on where they travel during their relocation are not known, Neptune balls wash up on beaches especially frequently during storms. [ 3 ] Appearance, properties, and applications [ edit ] Dry Neptune balls are light brown. [ 7 ] Neptune balls usually have a radius less than 8 centimetres (3.1 in) long; a study found that the mean radius is between 1.14 cm (0.45 in) and 2.68 cm (1.06 in) . [ 1 ] [ f ] The study also found that the average mass of Neptune balls is 0.212 g (0.0075 oz) . [ 1 ] [ g ] Another study described Neptune balls as having radii from 10 millimetres (0.39 in) up to 10 centimetres (3.9 in) . [ 5 ] Neptune balls can be spherical or ellipsoidal . [ 17 ] Their fibres are relatively smooth, except for places in which salt crystals form following sea water evaporation. [ 1 ] Fibres on the outside of Neptune balls are often broken into a disordered bundle of smaller fibres because of the transport to the shore, though this is unlikely to impact the formation process. [ 1 ] Posidonia oceanica ' s lignin and cell fibres ensure that Neptune balls are stiff; [ 15 ] they are composed of 32% lignin, whereas Posidonia oceanica has 19% lignin. [ 17 ] Neptune balls are also stiff because of their high density. [ 1 ] Neptune balls that wash up on shores are typically considered waste, although if collected as a resource they may have a variety of uses. [ 17 ] : 45 Neptune balls have been suggested as a soundproofing material, as they have similar absorption to that of mineral wool and polyester fibre . [ 18 ] Extracted lignin from Neptune balls has been suggested as a material for reinforcement. [ 17 ] The poor flammability and good thermal insulation of Neptune balls make them excellent for building insulation ; [ 5 ] [ 19 ] consequently, they have been sold as a building insulation material. [ 1 ] Neptune balls would have less of an environmental impact because Posidonia oceanica absorbs carbon dioxide, [ 18 ] and they would replace plastic fibres, which are unsustainable as they require oil extraction. [ 17 ] This would also reduce energy use and organic waste. [ 17 ] Procuring Neptune balls for insulation uses up to thirty times less energy than procuring mineral wool, rock wool, or petroleum-based foams. [ 19 ] However, Anna Sanchez-Vidal, a researcher at the University of Barcelona , argues against removing Neptune balls from beaches as they are part of beach ecosystems. [ 2 ] They bring humidity to beaches, [ 2 ] protect beaches against erosion, provide nutrients for dune plants, and feed beach arthropods . [ 15 ] Distribution [ edit ] In the Mediterranean Sea [ edit ] Neptune balls formed from Posidonia oceanica can only be found on coasts of the Mediterranean Sea as Posidonia oceanica is endemic to there. [ 1 ] Posidonia oceanica Neptune balls have been found on the coasts of Spain, Algeria, Tunisia, and Turkey. [ 17 ] Worldwide [ edit ] On the east coast of Africa and on the coast of Australia, non-living sea balls made of Posidonia australis have been found. [ 7 ] Despite conservation efforts, Posidonia australis is also in decline. [ 2 ] In 1996 and 2006, non-living sea balls made of marram grass were reported at Dingle Bay , Ireland. [ 13 ] These varied in shape; some were spherical and had a radius 3.5 cm (1.4 in) , whereas others were elliptical and over 25 cm (9.8 in) long. [ 13 ] Non-living sea balls made of fragments of marsh plant stems, rhizomes, and roots have been reported in Florida , United States. [ 20 ] Non-living sea balls have also been found in lakes and on the coast of Nova Scotia , Canada, the coast of New England , United States, [ 11 ] as well as on coasts of the North Sea . [ 7 ] Canadian botanist W. F. Ganong speculated that non-living sea balls occur "all over the globe". [ 11 ] History [ edit ] The earliest known use of Neptune balls was in ancient Egypt, where they were used to make footwear. [ 21 ] The earliest known dated description of Neptune balls was in 1216 in Andalusia , Spain, where they were known as annabdti . Abul Abbas, a Moorish scholar, mentioned them in his book of travel, Kitab ar-rihlat , for supposedly having medicinal properties. [ 7 ] [ 8 ] An Arabic pharmacologist , Ibu el Baither, called Neptune balls okr elbahr in his book Kitab al-Dschamie al-Kabir , believing that they have medicinal properties in dentistry . [ 7 ] [ 8 ] The Encyclopédie , published between 1751 and 1772, defined Neptune balls as "a substance usually an oblong, rounded or spherical ball shape, [and] fist-sized". [ 12 ] The Encyclopédie stated that Neptune balls are formed from fibrous plant substances. [ 12 ] Henry David Thoreau mentioned aquatic spheroids in his 1854 book Walden . [ 14 ] Botanists in France have known that Neptune balls are formed from Posidonia oceanica remains since at least 1872, though theories that they are formed from the remains of pine cones existed in the 19th century. [ 11 ] In 1877, Hugh Algernon Weddell reported that Neptune balls found on beaches around Hyères , France, are made of Posidonia caulini , [ 10 ] [ 11 ] another name for Posidonia oceanica . [ 22 ] He disproved the theory that Neptune balls are made of algae ; thus they were removed from the algae genus Aegagropila . [ 11 ] In 1897, Génau de Lamarlière stated that Neptune balls found on the coast of Spain are made of Posidonia oceanica , though other variants can be made of algae or pine needles. [ 23 ] Plastic waste and climate [ edit ] From 2018 to 2019, a study led by Anna Sanchez-Vidal, a researcher at the University of Barcelona , investigated the role of Neptune balls in trapping marine plastic and carrying it to the shore. [ 2 ] [ 15 ] The study examined Neptune balls collected on different beaches on Mallorca , Spain, chosen for its extensive underwater meadows of Posidonia oceanica and its large accumulations of plastic waste. The study found that half the samples contained plastic debris, mainly fragments, pellets and foams . The average plastic size was 9.08 mm (0.357 in) . [ 15 ] The polymers were identified by spectroscopy and included polyethylene (50.57%) followed by polypropylene (32.18%) and polyvinyl chloride (6.90%). [ 15 ] After the paper was published, Sanchez-Vidal received pictures of Neptune balls filled with plastic from many people. In an interview with the BBC , she said that these examples contained larger plastics like "sanitary towels, tampons, [and] wet wipes". She stated that the Neptune balls return waste "that was never meant to be on the seafloor". However, according to Sanchez-Vidal, Neptune balls are not a solution for plastic waste problems, as removing them to reduce pollution would disrupt the beach ecosystem, and they would not work as a plastic filter. [ 2 ] Neptune balls may collect up to 900 million pieces of plastic from the ocean every year. As of 2021, it is unclear whether the plastic damages the seagrass. [ 3 ] A 2024 study by the Spanish Institute of Oceanography [ es ] found that Neptune balls are an effective indicator for marine plastic pollution on the seafloor, especially microplastics , which were present in 62% of collected Neptune balls containing plastic. However, the study suggested that more research is needed to discover what proportion of plastics in Neptune balls are fibres, in order to assess differences between plastics found on beaches compared to on the sea floor. Additionally, the study found that Neptune balls may facilitate the movement of plastic from the seafloor to the surface, which could lead to increased consumption of plastic by sea life. The study concluded that the number of plastic items trapped in Neptune balls is dependent on the number of plastic items in the area rather than the size of the balls. [ 4 ] A 2026 study suggested that Neptune balls offer "promising opportunities for large-scale [plastic pollution] monitoring programs", although the method is still "in an early stage" and "[f]urther research is required" to standardise Neptune balls as an indicator of marine plastic pollution. The study analysed 1300 Neptune balls collected on 13 beaches of the Latium coast in Italy, and found that more than one-third contained plastic, with microplastics being the most common type. text: Kurt Gloor - Wikipedia Jump to content Search Search Kurt Gloor 9 languages مصرى Català Deutsch Español Français Bahasa Indonesia Malagasy Polski اردو Edit links From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia Swiss film director (1942–1997) Kurt Gloor Gloor in 1972 Born ( 1942-11-08 ) 8 November 1942 Zurich , Switzerland Died 20 September 1997 (1997-09-20) (aged 54) Zurich, Switzerland Occupations Film director , screenwriter , film producer Years active 1969–1997 Grave of Kurt Gloor at Manegg Cemetery, Zurich Kurt Gloor (8 November 1942 – 20 September 1997) was a Swiss film director , screenwriter and producer associated with the New Swiss Cinema. His work explored social conditions and the lives of people on the margins of society. His first feature film, Die plötzliche Einsamkeit des Konrad Steiner (1976), brought him wider recognition, and in the 1990s he shifted his focus to documentaries for Swiss television. Biography [ edit ] Kurt Gloor was born on 8 November 1942 in Zurich . [ 1 ] [ 2 ] He studied at Zurich's Kunstgewerbeschule and completed training in graphic design. [ 1 ] [ 3 ] After his training, he worked as a graphic designer in Vienna and Zurich. [ 4 ] He later gained experience as a camera assistant on advertising films. [ 1 ] [ 4 ] In 1969, he became an independent filmmaker and producer and established his own film production company. [ 1 ] [ 4 ] Screenwriting was also part of his work from that year. [ 3 ] In 1990, Gloor began contributing to Swiss television's documentary unit as both a journalist and director. [ 3 ] From 1993, he concentrated entirely on documentary productions for Swiss television, after several major projects had failed to come to fruition and he had suffered financial losses. [ 1 ] [ 5 ] Gloor also wrote as a journalist for the Neue Zürcher Zeitung and Weltwoche . [ 1 ] In 1977, he received the Film Prize of the City of Zurich . [ 1 ] Gloor died by suicide in Zurich on 20 September 1997. [ 2 ] [ 4 ] [ 5 ] Work [ edit ] Gloor became part of the New Swiss Cinema generation, making documentaries that addressed social issues. [ 1 ] His films sought to draw attention to people who were oppressed, marginalised or dependent. [ 1 ] He researched his subjects closely and used local dialect in his films. [ 2 ] Die Landschaftsgärtner (1969) portrayed Swiss mountain farmers, while EX (1970) addressed alcoholism in Switzerland. [ 4 ] In Die Landschaftsgärtner , Gloor challenged idealised images of Swiss farming through his depiction of rural working life. [ 2 ] The film won the FIPRESCI Award at Oberhausen . [ 2 ] Die grünen Kinder (1971) examined modern housing developments, specifically the negative effects of life in the Swiss countryside on people relocated there. A controversy followed it when an award decision in Zurich was reversed by the Swiss Parliament and the jury subsequently resigned. Die besten Jahre (1973–1974) focused on married women, arguing that emancipation cannot be achieved without a favourable political and cultural climate. [ 4 ] [ 2 ] Gloor's first feature film, Die plötzliche Einsamkeit des Konrad Steiner , brought him wider attention in 1976. [ 1 ] [ 4 ] He wrote the leading role specifically for Sigfrit Steiner . [ 6 ] In developing the film, he carried out research in institutions for older people and spoke extensively with elderly people. [ 6 ] The film linked the experience of ageing with the decline of small urban businesses. [ 6 ] For Der Erfinder (1981), Gloor drew on a stage play by Hansjörg Schneider . [ 7 ] The film was nominated for the Golden Bear at the Berlin International Film Festival and the Gold Hugo at the Chicago International Film Festival , and won the OCIC Award at the San Sebastián International Film Festival . [ 8 ] He wrote the leading role specifically for Bruno Ganz . [ 7 ] For Mann ohne Gedächtnis (1984), Gloor drew on the case of an unidentified man found in the Bernese Jura in 1980 who neither spoke nor carried identification. [ 9 ] The film reworked the case as a modern Kaspar Hauser story. [ 9 ] Michael König played the central character without speaking a word. [ 9 ] As part of his preparation, Gloor completed a placement at the Waldau psychiatric clinic . [ 9 ] Gloor's last film, Trekking am Limit (1997), documented a week-long trek through the Jura involving 15 inmates from Witzwil prison and 10 people with disabilities. [ 2 ] [ 10 ] [ 11 ] Gloor accompanied the journey with a film crew, recording participants travelling on foot, by wheelchair, kayak and horse-drawn wagon. [ 11 ] Selected filmography [ edit ] A selection of Gloor's films as director includes: Mondo Karies (1969) [ 3 ] Die Landschaftsgärtner (1969) [ 3 ] EX (1970) [ 4 ] Die grünen Kinder (1971) [ 4 ] Die besten Jahre (1973–1974) [ 4 ] Die plötzliche Einsamkeit des Konrad Steiner (1976) [ 3 ] Der Chinese (1978) [ 3 ] Der Erfinder (1981) [ 3 ] Mann ohne Gedächtnis (1984) [ 9 ] Jessica – Die ersten Tage im Leben eines Methadonbabys (1992) [ 3 ] Leben unter Riesen (1995) [ 3 ] Mit einem Fuss im Jenseits (1996) [ 3 ] Trekking am Limit (1997) [ 2 ] Legacy [ edit ] In October 1998, 3sat presented a retrospective to Gloor comprising twelve of his documentary films and the feature film Der Erfinder . text: Via Mansuerisca - Wikipedia Jump to content Search Search Via Mansuerisca 3 languages Deutsch Français Nederlands Edit links From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia Ancient Belgian road Map of the Via Mansuerisca The Via Mansuerisca or Pavé Charlemagne is a paved ancient road in the High Fens in Belgium. It was discovered in 1768. The precise age of the road has been a matter of debate; a detailed study made in 2005 indicated two periods of construction: one dating from around 300 AD, and a later from sometime around the year 460 AD. The purpose of constructing the road is unknown. Parts of the road have been excavated on several occasions, the first time in 1932. The identified course of the road is approximately 6 kilometres (3.7 mi) long. History [ edit ] During the late 18th century, the High Fens was a border region where the borders of five sovereign territories converged: the Duchy of Limburg , the Duchy of Luxembourg , the Duchy of Jülich , the Princely Abbey of Stavelot-Malmedy , and possessions belonging to the Prince-Bishopric of Liège . The different territories imposed different taxes and levies on goods traded over their borders, making trade in the region cumbersome and expensive. The establishment of new roads and the repair of old ones were considered a practical solution to the conundrum; by establishing roads that avoided unnecessary border crossings, tariffs could be reduced and trade increased. Authorities in the Austrian Netherlands strove to establish a new network of routes connecting the harbour in Ostend with Germany and France. While surveying the High Fens for possible routes for new roads (in a project that was eventually abandoned), the remains of an ancient paved road were discovered in 1768. [ 1 ] The discovery was formally reported in a document dated 7 September 1768. [ 2 ] While the authorities had been unaware of the existence of the road, it is possible that its existence had been known to the local population. [ 3 ] The precise age of the road has been a matter of debate. Initially it was believed to be a Roman road , but at least since the 1980s it has also been proposed that the road was instead built during the Merovingian dynasty . [ 4 ] [ 5 ] The latter hypothesis has been supported by some radiocarbon dating and pollen analyses, indicating a post-Roman date. [ 6 ] Furthermore, a written record from the Merovingian period (dated 670) mentions a road called the Via Mansuerisca , noting that it marked the border of the territory of the Abbey of Stavelot-Malmedy. [ 7 ] [ 8 ] A detailed analysis made in 2005 indicated the road appears to have had two building periods: one dating from around 300 AD, and a later from sometime around the year 460 AD. [ 9 ] The purpose of the construction of the road is unknown. It may have been constructed as part of a remodelled Roman defensive system during the Migration Period , or perhaps for economic reasons, facilitating the movement of goods and minerals between Trier and areas further north. [ 9 ] Parts of the road have been excavated by archaeologists on several occasions, the first in 1932. [ 10 ] Following the widespread wildfires in the High Fens in summer 2026, parts of the road were exposed as covering peat and vegetation was consumed by fire. [ 11 ] [ 12 ] Description [ edit ] The identified course of the road is approximately 6 kilometres (3.7 mi) long. [ 13 ] It crosses the High Fens , and runs in a relatively straight line from Hestreux in the north-west to the Rasquin peat bog to the south-east, just east of Baraque Michel . It crosses the Hill stream or Helle. [ 7 ] A detailed mapping of the course of the road was made in 1998. [ 14 ] The local population traditionally calls the road the Pavé Charlemagne (" Charlemagne street"). Whether or not the road is actually identical with the Via Mansuerisca identified in the Merovingian document is unknown, but Via Mansuerisca has been used to refer to the road since 1871 and has become an accepted and established name for the road. Thirty Years of Virginity Can Make You a Wizard?! Tower of God Bocchi the Rock! Koisenu Futari The Tiger and Her Wings Children 1 Awards Kuniko Mukōda Award [ ja ] (2022) Erika Yoshida ( 吉田 恵里香 , Yoshida Erika ; born 21 November 1987) is a Japanese screenwriter and novelist affiliated with Queen-B. [ 1 ] Becoming an assistant to Masafumi Nishida [ ja ] as a student, she began serving as head writer for several television series, including Boys Over Flowers Season 2 (2017), Cherry Magic! Thirty Years of Virginity Can Make You a Wizard?! (2020), Tower of God (2020-2024), Bocchi the Rock! (2022), I Will Be Your Bloom (2023), and the asadora drama The Tiger and Her Wings (2024). She also won the Kuniko Mukōda Award [ ja ] as screenwriter for Koisenu Futari (2022). Biography [ edit ] Early life and education [ edit ] Erika Yoshida, a native of Kanagawa Prefecture , was born on 21 November 1987. [ 1 ] She graduated from both Nihon University Senior & Junior High School [ ja ] and the Nihon University College of Art (Nichigei)'s Department of Literature. [ 2 ] Yoshida originally planned to be a mangaka while in junior high school , and with that aspiration in mind even chose a school with an arts department , but eventually decided against it. [ 3 ] Her next aspiration was to become a novelist , [ 4 ] and she picked Nichigei's Department of Literature to receive guidance on that career path. [ 5 ] During her student years, she learned that Masafumi Nishida was looking for an assistant, and began her career as a screenwriter under that position. [ 4 ] Screenwriting career [ edit ] Yoshida wrote the screenplay for Koisuru Eve [ ja ] , an NTV drama special which aired on Christmas Eve 2013; [ 6 ] this was her debut as a drama screenwriter. [ 7 ] She subsequently wrote screenplays for several dramas, namely Dansui! [ ja ] (2017), Boys Over Flowers Season 2 (2017), Heaven? [ ja ] (2019), Dasada (2020), Cherry Magic! Thirty Years of Virginity Can Make You a Wizard?! (2020), and Koeharu! (2021). [ 8 ] Yoshida was writer for the 2022 drama Koisenu Futari , [ 9 ] for which she won the 40th Kuniko Mukōda Award [ ja ] . [ 10 ] [ 11 ] She wrote the screenplays for Double and I Will Be Your Bloom , which both aired that same year, [ 8 ] and she was screenwriter for the 2023 NHK special drama Menstrual Uncle and His Daughter [ ja ] . [ 12 ] She served as screenwriter for the 2024 asadora drama The Tiger and Her Wings , [ 12 ] as well as its 2026 special drama spinoff Yamada Todoroki Hōritsu Jimusho . [ 13 ] In September 2026, it was announced that she would be the screenwriter for Amazon Prime Video 's live-action adaptation of The Apothecary Diaries . [ 14 ] Yoshida's first anime work was in the 2011 television series Tiger & Bunny . [ 3 ] She subsequently was the head writer for Trickster (2016), Namu Amida Butsu! Rendai Utena [ ja ] (2019), and the first season of Tower of God (2020). [ 15 ] [ 16 ] [ 17 ] She later became the 2022 anime adaptation for the manga Bocchi the Rock! ; she won the 9th Anime Trending Anime of the Year Award for Best in Adapted Screenplay for her work on the anime. [ 18 ] [ 19 ] She later returned to work for Tower of God as the second season's series composition writer, a position she later held for the 2025 anime Maebashi Witches ; [ 20 ] [ 21 ] Reiichi Naruma of Real Sound called the latter an example of a growing trend of drama screenwriters providing series composition for original anime. [ 22 ] Yoshida is also a film screenwriter, with her work including No Longer Heroine (2015), Love and Lies (2017), Leon [ ja ] (2018), Even: Song for You [ ja ] (2018), Sensei Kunshu (2018), Oz Land [ ja ] (2018), xxxHolic (2022), and Otonanajimi (2023). [ 8 ] Novels, manga, and other works [ edit ] Yoshida is also a novelist, with such work originally written for teenage audiences. [ 23 ] She wrote a novelization of Reruriri [ ja ] 's Vocaloid song " Nou Shou Sakuretsu Girl "; [ 24 ] she had landed the job after having a class where Hatsune Miku was discussed. [ 5 ] She was also the writer for the song's film and manga adaptations. [ 8 ] [ 25 ] Her novels also include adaptations of the NHK drama Jikken Kenji Totori [ ja ] and of Koisenu Futari . [ 26 ] [ 27 ] Following her writing of the Koisenu Futari novelization, she has announced plans to write another novel. [ 4 ] In May 2020, she wrote Okaeri , a one-shot romance manga in Weekly Young Jump illustrated by Masakazu Katsura . [ 28 ] She also wrote both Tiger & Bunny: The Comic and Tiger & Bunny 2: The Comic . [ 29 ] Yoshida served as a guest judge at the 75th NHK Kōhaku Uta Gassen in December 2024. [ 30 ] In 2025, she received a Kanagawa Cultural Award for the Future [ ja ] for her work in novels and screenwriting, [ 31 ] as well as the 19th Nichigei Prize. [ 32 ] Themes and personal life [ edit ] According to Naruma, Yoshida is "skilled at weaving social themes into her stories". [ 22 ] In an interview, Yoshida said that she was approached by NHK to work on Koisenu Futari , which is about an aromantic/asexual couple, after depicting a similar character in the Cherry Magic! drama. [ 27 ] When asked about whether she finds novels or screenplays an easier medium to write on, she replied: "Neither comes easily (laughs). I love writing stories, but I struggle and agonize over both forms." [ 4 ] She cites Kuniko Mukōda and Hiromi Kawakami as inspirations, and cites Yoshikazu Okada [ ja ] , Yuji Sakamoto , and Aya Watanabe [ ja ] as screenwriters she admires. [ 33 ] Yoshida has been affiliated with Queen-B since she was in university. [ 5 ] She has a Japanese language teacher's license. [ 1 ] She has a son who was born in 2019 or 2020. "Brain Fluid Explosion Girl") is a 2012 song by written by Japanese Vocaloid producer Rerulili [ ja ] . It has been adapted into a light novel, manga, and live-action film, all of which were written by screenwriter Erika Yoshida . Background and release [ edit ] Rerulili, as explained in an interview with Mynavi News , conceived the idea behind "Nou Shou Sakuretsu Girl" when, having hit a creative wall while focusing on pop and ballads, he researched current trends and noticed that young people were gravitating toward high-volume tracks featuring rapid-fire vocal delivery; he decided to take on the challenge despite it being outside his comfort zone. [ 2 ] He also mentioned that he had intentionally written the lyrics somewhat haphazardly to stimulate the listeners' imaginations, and was surprised to find people speculating that the song contained a critique of AKB48 . [ 2 ] "Nou Shou Sakuretsu Girl" was uploaded to Nico Nico Douga by Rerulili in October 2012. [ 2 ] It was his first song to reach one million views, doing so in January 2013. [ 3 ] surpassed 1.5 million views within five months. [ 2 ] Its popularity endured, eventually achieving "Hall of Fame" status (10 million views on Nico Nico Douga) in 2023. [ 2 ] Another self-cover version of "Nou Shou Sakuretsu Girl" featuring Kagamine Rin and Megurine Luka was released to commemorate the one-million view milestone. [ 3 ] A live-action music video commemorating the two-million view milestone was released in July 2013. [ 3 ] In 2015, a self-remake named "Nou Shou Bakuretsu Girl 2015 Ver" was released. [ 4 ] A sequel of this song was also released, titled "Isshoku Sokuhatsu Zen Girl" ( 一触即発 禅ガール ) . [ 3 ] "Nou Shou Sakuretsu Girl" was the first song of the album of the same name, released on 28 December 2012. [ 1 ] Contents [ edit ] "Nou Shou Bakuretsu Girl" is characterized by rapid-fire lyrics and an up-tempo beat. [ 2 ] Its lyrics and music were written by Rerulili [ ja ] , and Hatsune Miku and Megpoid are the vocalists. [ 3 ] A diverse range of genres appear in "Nou Shou Sakuretsu Girl", including electronic music, jazz, and traditional Japanese musical instruments ; Animate Times stated that the song's rapid changes in style is a "key charm" of the song. [ 4 ] UtaTen remarks that the lyrics indicate "a song about the daily life of a girl with a masochistic streak". [ 3 ] Other media [ edit ] Light novel [ edit ] A novelization of "Nou Shou Sakuretsu Girl" was written by Erika Yoshida ; [ 5 ] she had landed the job after having a class where Hatsune Miku was discussed. [ 6 ] It is about high school students Hana Ichii and Hana Inazawa appearing in a cell phone survival game. Kadokawa Beans Bunko released six volumes of the light novel. [ 7 ] Volumes [ edit ] No. Original release date Original ISBN English release date English ISBN 1 1 December 2013 [ 8 ] 978-40-4-101105-8 — — 2 1 March 2014 [ 9 ] 978-40-4-101263-5 — — 3 1 August 2014 [ 10 ] 978-40-4-101716-6 — — 4 1 December 2014 [ 11 ] 978-40-4-101717-3 — — 5 1 May 2015 [ 12 ] 978-40-4-102730-1 — — 6 1 August 2015 [ 13 ] 978-40-4-102729-5 — — Manga [ edit ] A self-titled manga adaptation of the song began serialization in Young Ace ' s May 2015 issue; it was illustrated by Kudan Natsuka and written by Erika Yoshida. [ 14 ] [ 3 ] It centers on schoolboy Inase Ukiha ( 浮葉いなせ , Ukiha Inase ) being attacked by a brain-eating monster. [ 14 ] Volumes [ edit ] No. Original release date Original ISBN English release date English ISBN 1 25 July 2015 [ 15 ] 978-4-04-103451-4 — — 2 4 March 2016 [ 16 ] 978-4-04-103865-9 — — 3 4 November 2016 [ 17 ] 978-4-04-104859-7 — — Live-action film [ edit ] "Nou Shou Sakuretsu Girl" was adapted into a live-action film, directed by Yūichi Abe [ ja ] , written by Erika Yoshida and starring Hinata Kashiwagi and Seika Taketomi [ ja ] . [ 18 ] The theme song is a cover version of the titular song by Shiritsu Ebisu Chugaku . [ 19 ] It was also the first live-action adaptation of a Vocaloid song. [ 20 ] [ 5 ] Nou Shou Sakuretsu Girl was released on 25 July 2015 by Kadokawa Corporation , [ 18 ] and was screened at a premium Nico Nico Live stream. [ 3 ] It made ¥18 million in the box office. [ 21 ] Critic Kazufumi Iida [ ja ] described the film as part of a trend of successful "Vocaloid novels" following up on the popularity of the Kagerou Project multimedia project. [ 22 ] It was scheduled for a theatrical release in Taiwan, but it was canceled due to declining sales which a lawsuit attributed to a fast movie [ ja ] by YouTuber AmoGood [ zh ] . [ 23 ] Stage adaptations [ edit ] There have been two stage adaptations of "Nou Shou Sakuretsu Girl": Nōshō Sakuretsu Girl: Ningen Dōbutsuen ( 脳漿炸裂ガール ～人間動物園～ , Nōshō Sakuretsu Gāru ~Ningen Dōbutsuen~ ) , performed in 2019, and the latter, Nōshō Sakuretsu Gāru 2: Zokubutsu Kikō/Anarchy in the Journey ( 脳漿炸裂ガール2 〜俗物奇行〜 Anarchy in the Journey , Nōshō Sakuretsu Gāru 2 ~ Zokubutsu Kikō ~ Anarchy in the Journey ) , performed at Rikkoukai [ ja ] Hall from 2 to 6 June 2021. text: Beauty and the Beast (Kanye West song) - Wikipedia Jump to content Search Search Beauty and the Beast (Kanye West song) Add languages Add links From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia 2025 promotional single by Kanye West "Beauty and the Beast" Promotional single by Kanye West from the album Bully Released February 9, 2025 ( 2025-02-09 ) Recorded 2021 2024–2026 Genre Downtempo Length 1 : 45 Label YZY Gamma Songwriters Ye Caleb Toliver Producer Ye " Beauty and the Beast " (stylized in all caps ) is a song by American rapper Kanye West from his twelfth studio album, Bully (2026). It was released as a promotional single on February 9, 2025, exclusively through West's Yeezy website, and was later released to music streaming services along with " Preacher Man " and "Damn" on June 20, 2025, via a 3-track extended play (EP). Prior to its release, a visual preview was posted by West on Instagram in October 2024. A downtempo song, it samples "Don't Have to Shop Around" by R&B vocal group the Mad Lads . West solely produced the track himself and wrote it alongside Don Toliver . Lyrically, "Beauty and the Beast" focuses on West's emotional state and place in the music industry, reflecting on how his career has changed. West initially recorded "Beauty and the Beast" in 2021, later reworking the song in 2024 in his hotel room in Tokyo. It was previewed multiple times prior to its release, first being played at West and Ty Dolla Sign 's September 2024 concert at the Wuyuan River Stadium in Haikou , China, where West first officially announced Bully . It was the second song previewed for the album, along with the track "Preacher Man". The song was later included as a track on West's March 2025 visual album Bully V1 . Following its debut at Haikou, "Beauty and the Beast" received positive reviews from music critics , who often praised its production and writing as more relaxed than West's recent releases. Commercially, the track appeared on the Billboard Hot 100 , US Hot R&B/Hip-Hop Songs chart, Canadian Hot 100 , and New Zealand Hot Singles chart. Background and recording [ edit ] "Beauty and the Beast" was first played during Kanye West 's September 28, 2024, show at Haikou 's Wuyuan River Stadium , a destination on his and Ty Dolla Sign 's Vultures 2 Listening Experience tour. [ 1 ] [ 2 ] This was the second time West had debuted a new song during the tour, as he had previously played the song " Preacher Man " (2025) at a September 15 concert. [ 3 ] Towards the end of the song, West announced that he had "a new album coming out", revealing the album's title, Bully , and the song "Beauty and the Beast". [ 2 ] He previewed an updated version in full via Instagram on October 16, alongside an accompanying visual from the Haikou show. [ 4 ] [ 5 ] According to the post's caption, West had made adjustments to the song since its debut while staying in Tokyo , Japan, recording it in his hotel room. [ 5 ] [ 6 ] Former collaborator and record producer Mike Dean later affirmed that the track was first conceived during sessions for West's tenth studio album, Donda (2021). [ 7 ] Composition and lyrics [ edit ] "Beauty and the Beast" "Beauty and the Beast" is a downtempo song that shows West's reflective nature and sample-based production. Problems playing this file? See media help . Musically, "Beauty and the Beast" is a downtempo song. [ 4 ] Unlike most of West's work, his vocals are entirely sung rather than rapped. [ 8 ] It was produced using the keyboard Ensoniq ASR-10 and the sampler machine SP-1200 . [ 9 ] It uses a prominent sample of "Don't Have to Shop Around" by R&B vocal group the Mad Lads . [ 10 ] [ 9 ] The sample-based production and used equipment led critics to draw comparisons to West's earlier work, [ 8 ] [ 6 ] [ 11 ] with HotNewHipHop writer Zachary Horvath considering the song's production style to resemble a blend of West's prior albums The College Dropout (2004), 808s & Heartbreak (2008), My Beautiful Dark Twisted Fantasy (2010), and The Life of Pablo (2016). [ 8 ] Like the majority of Bully , West served as the primary producer of "Beauty and the Beast". [ 12 ] [ 6 ] Lyrically, West sings about having "fresh new tires" and admits his attempts to managing his emotions better, reflecting on his status and rekindled career following the Vultures albums. [ 4 ] He acknowledges his fans' expectations for him and his music, singing on the song's chorus , "Think about it every night and day / To try to stay away, to keep my audience / So don't take this as disrespect, I'm sitting here tryna redirect." [ 4 ] The relaxed nature of "Beauty and the Beast" is reflective of West's time spent in Tokyo. Music journalist Touré , who was in correspondence with West, stated that his China tour dates were intentionally picked so he could retreat to Japan. Touré also claimed that West was producing the album "pretty much by himself", noting that his music was usually a combination of multiple people's input. He referred to it as a "fresh chapter" in West's life, "because in Tokyo he can be who he wants to be." [ 4 ] Release and reception [ edit ] "Beauty and the Beast" was released as a promotional single on West's Yeezy website on February 9, 2025, for streaming. [ 13 ] [ 14 ] [ 15 ] As it was released during the Super Bowl LIX halftime show , publications saw it as a sign that West was jealous of halftime show performer and fellow rapper Kendrick Lamar . [ 13 ] The song was removed from his website shortly after, as all items were replaced with a swastika T-shirt. [ 14 ] [ 16 ] It later appeared on the short film Bully V1 . [ 17 ] On June 20, 2025, West released a 3-track extended play (EP) as promotion for the album, including the song alongside the tracks "Preacher Man" and "Damn". [ 18 ] Bully was released on March 28, 2026, through distribution from Gamma , which includes "Beauty and the Beast". [ 19 ] [ 20 ] The song was also provided with a different visual on West's YouTube channel. [ 21 ] "Beauty and the Beast" has received positive reviews. Commenting on its initial preview, iHeart Radio ' s Tony Centeno described West's vocals as "soothing" with an instrumental similar to his earlier works. [ 11 ] Armon Sadler of Vibe felt the track's downtempo production was a departure from West's recent albums– Vultures 1 and 2 in particular–making it "the ideal canvas for [him] to be more vulnerable." [ 4 ] Similarly, Complex ' s Miki Hellerbach noted its writing as "the most meditative we've heard [West's] lyrics in quite some time, as he ponders rather than asserts." [ 22 ] As a promotional single, "Beauty and the Beast", peaked at number 19 on the New Zealand Hot Singles chart. [ 23 ] Following the release of Bully , it peaked at number 85 on the Billboard Hot 100 , [ 24 ] number 23 on the Hot R&B/Hip-Hop Songs chart, [ 25 ] and number 93 on the Canadian Hot 100 . text: Jessie Waddell - Wikipedia Jump to content Search Search Jessie Waddell Add languages Add links From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia Founder of the New York City West Indian Day Carnival (1892–1975) Jessie Waddell soon after her arrival in New York. Jessie Waddell (1892–1975) was a Trinidadian-American musician and performer. She was the founder of New York City's West Indian Day Parade , a celebration of West Indian culture held annually in Brooklyn. Early life [ edit ] Waddell was born in Tunapuna , Trinidad and Tobago , the oldest of seven children. She was a musician from a young age, playing dance music as well as the organ at a local Anglican church. After the death of her father in 1907, she left school to work at the Arima Roman Catholic School. [ 1 ] She immigrated to New York City sometime in 1923 or 1924. [ 1 ] [ 2 ] West Indian Day Parade [ edit ] In New York, Waddell sought to provide a cultural link for Harlem's Caribbean community by hosting Carnival festivities in the form of masquerade balls. From 1924 to 1944, she promoted some of the biggest masquerades at the Renaissance Ballroom . She also led a 10-piece orchestra, the "Nu-Tones", who performed at many of these dances. [ 2 ] [ 3 ] In 1946, Waddell wrote to mayor William O'Dwyer about hosting the Carnival parade outdoors on Labor Day , along Seventh Avenue in Harlem. She was the chair of the Trinidad Carnival Pageant Committee of New York, the forerunner of the West Indian American Day Carnival Association, which sponsored the parade. Originally, the event was planned to be exclusively Trinidadian, but pressure from other Caribbean civic organizations and businesses caused Waddell to shift the event to a broader "West Indian Day" celebration. The first Carnival parade took place on September 1, 1947, attended by over 50,000 people and featuring a variety of floats, calypso bands and orchestras, and intricately costumed performers. [ 4 ] Waddell continued to be an important figure in organizing the annual parades and recruiting performers until the Harlem parade permit was revoked in 1964. [ 5 ] When the parade was resumed in 1969 along Eastern Parkway in Brooklyn, it was under the leadership of Carlos Lezama . [ 6 ] Personal life [ edit ] After moving to the US, Waddell married Smithy Young and had two sons. The younger, Courtenay, was killed on Labor Day weekend, 1945, when he fell off the roof of their apartment building. Following her son's death, Waddell became deeply depressed. According to her niece and nephew, Waddell's friends and associates pushed her to host the West Indian Day parade as a means of escaping that depression, and for that reason she decided the parade would fall on Labor Day, the anniversary of Courtenay's death. [ 1 ] [ 2 ] Waddell returned to Trinidad in 1972, and remained there until her death in 1975. [ 3 ] References [ edit ] 1 2 3 Pidduck, Angela (March 22, 1999). text: West Indian Day Parade - Wikipedia Jump to content Search Search West Indian Day Parade 1 language العربية Edit links From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia Parade in New York City Labor Day Carnival The West Indian Day Parade marching by the Brooklyn Museum Dates Labor Day Years active 1930s–present Website https://wiadcacarnival.org/ The West Indian Day Parade Carnival is an annual celebration of West Indian culture, held on or around the first Monday of September in the Crown Heights neighborhood of Brooklyn in New York City. It is organized by the West Indian American Day Carnival Association (WIADCA). The main event is the West Indian Day Parade (also known as simply the Labor Day Parade ), which attracts between one and three million participants. [ 1 ] The spectators and participators watch and follow the parade on its route along Eastern Parkway . Some of the West Indian or Caribbean islands represented in the parade include Trinidad and Tobago , Haiti , Barbados , Dominica , Saint Lucia , Jamaica , Saint Vincent and Grenada , along with some Afro-Panamanians . Mainland Caribbean countries such as Guyana , Suriname , and Belize also participate as well. History [ edit ] This section needs more citations . Please help improve this section by adding citations to reliable sources . Unsourced material may be challenged and removed . Find sources: "West Indian Day Parade" – news · newspapers · books · scholar · JSTOR ( January 2017 ) ( Learn how and when to remove this message ) Start in Harlem [ edit ] Woman in costume in the 2009 New York City parade. David Dubinsky , Nelson Rockefeller , and Robert F. Wagner Jr. watch the 1959 Labor Day Parade Jessie Waddell and some of her West Indian friends started the Carnival in Harlem in Upper Manhattan , New York City, in the 1930s by staging costume parties in large, enclosed places such as the Savoy , Renaissance and Audubon Ballrooms due to the cold wintry weather of February. [ 2 ] This is the usual time for the pre- Lenten celebrations of the Trinidad and Tobago Carnival and other related celebrations around the world. However, because of the very nature of Carnival, and the need to parade in costume to music, indoor confinement did not work well. [ 3 ] The earliest known Carnival street parade was held on September 1, 1947. The Trinidad Carnival Pageant Committee was the founding force behind the parade, which was held in Harlem. The parade route was along Seventh Avenue , starting at 110th St. The first Carnival Queen was Dorothy Godfrey . The Committee raised money to finance the parade. They sold advertisement space and boosters, that were printed in a Souvenir Journal for West Indies Day, a booklet which is a memento of that first parade. Jessie Waddell Compton is presented in the journal as the person "whose inspiration and enterprise" was owed to the formation of this committee. The committee consisted of Waddell Compton (Chairman), Ivan H. Daniel (Vice Chairman), Conrad Matthews (Treasurer), Roy Huggins (Secretary), and Robert J. Welsh (Assistant Secretary). Each member of the committee contributed in helping to organize the parade. The after-parade party, which the Trinidad Carnival Pageant Committee held at the Golden Gate Ballroom , was arranged by James M. Green , another figure who helped make the first Carnival Parade in Harlem successful. Move to Crown Heights [ edit ] The permit for the Harlem parade was revoked in 1964. Five years later, a committee headed by Carlos Lezama, which eventually became the West Indian-American Day Carnival Association, obtained approval for the parade to be established on Eastern Parkway in Brooklyn, where it remains today. [ 4 ] [ 5 ] [ 6 ] Throughout the 1970s groups of colorfully clad masqueraders (“mas bands”) “wined” (danced) down the Parkway to the music of Trinidad-style steel bands ( steelpan ). Those steel bands were eventually replaced by powerful, truck-mounted sound systems that played a variety of Caribbean musics including calypso , soca (soul/calypso), reggae, and compas . [ 7 ] In 2020, the parade was cancelled due to COVID-19 by order of Mayor of New York Bill de Blasio , who canceled all permits for large-scale events through September 2020. The parade was replaced by a virtual event . [ 8 ] [ 9 ] While the parade did plan to return for 2021, on August 18 that year the WIADCA announced that the parade itself would once again be cancelled due to COVID-19 uncertainties, but that it would still hold a mix of in-person and streaming events, including several being held at the Brooklyn Museum . [ 10 ] [ 8 ] In popular culture [ edit ] Many calypso and soca songs from Trinidad make reference to the Labor Day Carnival, including "Gun Play in de Parkway" by Calypso Rose , "Melee (on the Eastern Parkway)" by Maestro, Labor Day Jam by the Guyanese superstar, Slingshot, and "Labor Day in Brooklyn" by the Mighty Sparrow . Jay-Z mentions the Labor Day Carnival on his hit song " Empire State of Mind " (2009), when he says "3 dice Cee-lo, 3 card monte, Labor Day Parade, rest in peace Bob Marley". There are also popular Haitian bands with their powerful méringue - compas music on the parkway, such as T-Vice , Tabou Combo , Konpa Kreyol/Kreyol La, Sweet Micky , Phantoms, Carimi, Djakout, D.P. Express and many more popular bands. [ citation needed ] Incidents [ edit ] Main article: Crime in New York City A string of fatal and non-fatal shootings and stabbings has occurred on and near the parade route in recent years, both during and following the parade. [ 11 ] [ 12 ] In 2003, a man was fatally shot and another was stabbed in the neck. [ 13 ] [ 14 ] In 2005, one man was shot and killed along the parade route. In 2006, one man was shot and another was stabbed. At the 2007 parade, there was only one official report of violence, when a man was shot twice in the leg. [ 15 ] [ 16 ] However, a different man (named Nathaniel Smith) was shot and killed in the 2007 parade. [ 17 ] In 2011 pre-dawn marches took a violent turn with the murder of one person, five instances of gunshot victims and three instances of stabbings coupled with sporadic shooting at crowds of people. [ 18 ] Following the 2011 parade, Yolanda Lezama-Clark, The President of the West Indian American Day Carnival Association (WIADCA) and other New York City officials condemned the one or two incidents that took place at the parade. [ 19 ] Additionally during the 2011 West Indian Day Parade in Brooklyn, New York City councilman Jumaane Williams along with a few others were arrested for walking along a closed-off sidewalk, after stating he had received permission to do so from other officers. [ 20 ] Several violent incidents took place after the official end of the 2012 parade. In separate incidents, two people were fatally stabbed, and two others were shot. [ 21 ] In 2013, two men were murdered and a further three individuals were wounded in several shootings. [ 22 ] On September 7, 2015, a pre-parade J'ouvert celebration was marred by violence when, at 3:41 a.m., gunfire hit lawyer Carey Gabay in the head. Gabay was an aide to New York Governor Andrew Cuomo and first deputy counsel at Empire State Development Corporation . Gabay died nine days later. The shooting was one of several violent episodes, including a fatal stabbing, in the hours before the parade. [ 23 ] [ 24 ] [ 25 ] On September 5, 2016, during pre-parade celebrations, two people were shot and killed and five others wounded in attacks. The attacks occurred despite the NYPD doubling the number of officers patrolling the neighborhood, installing 42 new security cameras and erecting 200 light towers. Police also distributed fliers, in conjunction with community groups, with a blunt message: "This community will no longer tolerate this violence. Do not shoot anyone. Do not stab anyone." [ 26 ] On September 4, 2023, one male accidentally shot himself at Eastern Parkway and Franklin Avenue. In another incident, one male was shot and two stabbed and slashed during a fight at 1187 Eastern Parkway. [ 27 ] [ 28 ] On September 2, 2024, a mass shooting occurred when a lone gunman jumped onto a street divider and fired into the crowd, striking four women and a man. The victims were aged between 16-69 years old. A 25-year-old later died from their injuries, and two others were critically injured. [ 29 ] [ 30 ] [ 31 ] On September 1, 2025, six people were shot and injured in separate incidents across four locations in Crown Heights . The first incident was reported around 5:30 p.m. while there was still large crowds in the street after the parade was over. A woman was grazed and a man was shot. The second incident was reported at 6:46 p.m. with two men being shot. Both were listed in stable condition. Minutes later at around 6:55 p.m., a 53-year-old man was shot in the neck and leg and a 40-year-old woman was shot in the ankle outside Yard Pot Restaurant and Bakery. The man was critically injured while the woman was reported to be in stable condition. A person of interest was taken into custody. A man was also injured in a slashing and sustained multiple injuries but refused medical attention and was uncooperative with investigators. text: Neottia confusa - Wikipedia Jump to content Search Search Neottia confusa 1 language Cebuano Edit links From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia Species of orchid Neottia confusa Conservation status Critically Endangered ( IUCN 3.1 ) [ 1 ] Scientific classification Kingdom: Plantae Clade : Tracheophytes Clade : Angiosperms Clade : Monocots Order: Asparagales Family: Orchidaceae Subfamily: Epidendroideae Genus: Neottia Species: N. confusa Binomial name Neottia confusa Bhaumik [ 2 ] Neottia confusa is a critically endangered species of orchid endemic to northeastern India. It was found in three small clusters in temperate and subalpine forests in the Dihang-Dibang Biosphere Reserve . Discovered in 2010 and described in 2012, it was named for its small, undivided lip, atypical among other species. Description [ edit ] Neottia confusa is a terrestrial orchid found on the forest floor. It reaches a height of 12–15.5 centimetres (5–6 in) , with less variation in height as compared to other Neottia species. The stem is ridged, with a pair of oppositely arranged cauline leaves toward its base. The leaves are sessile (attached without stalks) and oval shaped with rounded apices, measuring 8–12 millimetres (0.3–0.5 in) long and 6–11 millimetres (0.2–0.4 in) wide. [ 3 ] Flowering and fruiting occur from July to August. Between 15 and 20 flowers are arranged in a raceme at the end of the stem. These flowers are greenish and 3–4 millimetres (0.12–0.16 in) long. The peduncle , a stalk supporting the inflorescence, is 5–22 millimetres (0.2–0.9 in) in length, circular in cross-section, and covered in glandular hairs. Each individual flower is borne on a pedicel subtended by two to three acuminate (narrow-ended) bracts , although these are sometimes absent. Their pedicels and ovaries are smooth and together about 2–3 millimetres (0.08–0.1 in) in length. [ 3 ] As with other orchids, the flowers of N. confusa have three sepals and three petals, with the median petal called the labellum or lip. The lateral petals are oblong to elliptical, with a rounded apex, 2.2 by 1 millimetre (0.09 in × 0.04 in) . The lip is simple and triangular, measuring around 1.2–1.5 by 1 millimetre (0.05 in–0.06 in × 0.04 in) . The lip has a very small claw (the stalklike base of the lip) with the mesochile (middle portion of the lip) narrowing into an undivided epichile (the labellum tip). The sepals are similar in shape to the lateral petals but vary in size: the dorsal sepal is 2–2.5 by 0.8–1.3 millimetres (0.08 in–0.1 in × 0.03 in–0.05 in) , while the lateral sepals are slightly smaller, at 1.8–2 by 0.6–1 millimetre (0.07 in–0.08 in × 0.02 in–0.04 in) . Like with other orchids, the reproductive parts of the flower are fused, forming a structure called the column . In N. confusa , the column is straight and 0.8–1 millimetre (0.03–0.04 in) long. [ 3 ] Taxonomy [ edit ] Neottia confusa was first collected in July and August 2010 during a botanical survey in the Dihang-Dibang Biosphere Reserve . The collector, Indian botanist M. Bhaumik, later compared collections of Neottia from the survey with species descriptions and determined that the type specimens of N. confusa and N. dihangensis represented new species, which he described in 2012. The epithet confusa refers to the flower's unusual lip morphology, which differs from the bilobed or heavily emarginate (with a long central notch) lip shapes characteristic of most other members of the genus. [ 3 ] N. confusa belongs to the genus Neottia , which contains both autotrophic and myco-heterotrophic plants. N. confusa is autotrophic, and also has smaller lips than other species in the genus. Since the 1990s, Neottia has been combined with Listera , which for much of the 19th and 20th centuries was considered a separate genus. N. confusa has been described as intermediate between the species originally classified as Listera and Neottia . It bears the closest similarities to Neottia taizanensis , although the small lips and undivided epichile most closely resemble Neottia acuminata and Neottia taibaishanensis . [ 3 ] [ 4 ] Distribution and conservation [ edit ] Neottia confusa is known only from the type locality , a region occupying 4 square kilometres (1.5 sq mi) in the Dihang-Dibang Biosphere Reserve in the Upper Siang district of Arunachal Pradesh . The area has an elevation of 3,200–3,800 metres (10,500–12,500 ft) and is located within the temperate to subalpine biome. It grows in moist moss on the forest floor alongside other herbaceous plants, including Neottia acuminata and Juncus , with an canopy dominated by Rhododendron and Abies . [ 3 ] [ 1 ] When N. confusa was first discovered in 2010, three groups of 10–15 mature individuals were observed; no subsequent populations have been documented. [ 3 ] [ 1 ] The IUCN has estimated the global population as consisting of 40–50 plants but recognises that research is needed in order to establish a more accurate estimate of the population size and population trends. [ 1 ] Because the plant's known range is contained entirely in a remote protected area, Bhaumik proposed assessing its conservation status as least concern in his 2012 description of the species. [ 3 ] While no immediate threats to the conservation of N. confusa have been identified, the small number of known occurrences of the plant led to its classification as critically endangered under Criterion D by the IUCN. As with all other orchids, its trade is regulated under the CITES treaty. [ 1 ] References [ edit ] 1 2 3 4 5 Adit, A. (2022). " Neottia confusa " . text: Chew Hock Leong - Wikipedia Jump to content Search Search Chew Hock Leong Add languages Add links From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia Singaporean banker (1897–1967) In this Chinese name , the family name is Chew . Chew Hock Leong JP Chew in 1949 Chairman of the Public Service Commission In office 29 January 1957 ( 1957-01-29 ) – 16 July 1959 ( 1959-07-16 ) Preceded by W. L. Blythe Succeeded by Yusof Ishak Personal details Born 1897 ( 1897 ) Singapore, Straits Settlements Died 19 May 1967 (1967-05-19) (aged 70) Singapore Spouse Goh Seng Neo Children 5 Chinese name Chinese 周福隆 Transcriptions Standard Mandarin Hanyu Pinyin Zhōu Fúlóng IPA [ʈʂo ́ ʊ.fu ̌ .lʊ ̌ ŋ] Chew Hock Leong [ a ] JP ( c. 1897 – 19 May 1967) was a Singaporean banker who served as chairman of the Public Service Commission from 1957 to 1959. A prominent figure in Singapore's early financial sector, he served as the general manager of the Oversea-Chinese Banking Corporation . In 1930, when he sold his patent to Eastman Kodak , he was believed to be the first local Chinese inventor to create and sell "an important invention" to a multi-national company. Early life and education [ edit ] In 1897, Chew was born. He was the eldest son, and had seven brothers and four sisters. His father, Chew Boon Lay , was from Changchow , China, and bought huge plots land in Jurong for farming. [ 1 ] Boon Lay is named after him. [ 2 ] [ 3 ] His mother, Ong Cheng Neo, was a Peranakan from Malacca . [ 4 ] Chew attended Raffles Institution . [ 5 ] [ 6 ] In 1915, he obtained a Senior Cambridge . [ 7 ] Career [ edit ] Chew began his career as a clerk in the high courts. One of his father's friends felt that Chew was "wasted in the high courts", and introduced him to the Chinese Commercial Bank , as its secretary. [ 8 ] [ 9 ] In 1930, Chew invented a device to maintain flat the portion of the exposed film to form a sharp image. The invention was later sold to Eastman Kodak . He was believed to be the first local Chinese to create and sell "an important invention" to a multi-national company. [ 10 ] [ 11 ] Chew was later the manager of the Chinese Commercial Bank, and the Oversea-Chinese Banking Corporation (OCBC). [ 12 ] [ 13 ] In July 1940, in response to the Government implementing a remittance quota, Chew felt that a quota will be "objectionable" and "give rise to an undesirable racket", as many workers need to remit money back to support their family. [ 14 ] [ 15 ] In January 1947, Chew was appointed as a justice of the peace . [ 16 ] In January 1948, he was appointed as a member of the Malayan Board of Income Tax . [ 17 ] [ 18 ] In January 1949, Chew resigned in protest as a member of the Singapore Improvement Trust , after the lowest tender of a project in Balestier Road was rejected. [ 19 ] [ 20 ] In May 1949, Chew left for United Kingdom on RMS Carthage . [ 21 ] He represented the Singapore Chinese Chamber of Commerce as a delegate, to discuss trade with the British Government . [ 22 ] [ 23 ] In September 1952, Chew was appointed as a trustee of the Silver Jubilee Fund. [ 24 ] In April 1955, he was appointed as a board member of Singapore Polytechnic (SP), replacing Lin Yutang . [ 25 ] [ 26 ] In September 1956, Chew retired as general manager of OCBC, and joined the Public Service Commission (PSC) as a board member. [ 27 ] In October 1956, due to his appointment to PSC, Chew resigned from SP, adding that it was "impossible to serve on the Polytechnic Board in his present state of health". [ 28 ] On 29 January 1957, Chew succeeded W. L. Blythe as chairman of PSC. [ 29 ] [ 30 ] In February 1957, the 1st Legislative Assembly approved his monthly salary of $2,300. [ 31 ] On 16 July 1959, Chew stepped down as chairman of PSC, and he was succeeded by Yusof Ishak . [ 32 ] In November 1959, Chew became chairman of the Malayan Rubber Export Registration Board, with a monthly salary of $2,000. [ 33 ] [ 34 ] Personal life [ edit ] Chew was a Christian , [ 35 ] and he was the president of the Straits Chinese Epworth League. In 1927, the league donated new year gifts to various hospitals for the poor. [ 36 ] He was also a trustee of the Straits Chinese Methodist Episcopal Church . [ 37 ] [ 38 ] Chew was married to Goh Seng Neo ( c. 1904 –2 September 1983), [ 39 ] and they had five children. In March 1937, his daughter, Renee Chew Bee Neo, [ 40 ] made headlines as she was the first prize winner in an essay competition, against all school children in the British Empire who took part. [ 11 ] On 12 September 1960, during a rubber conference at Victoria Memorial Hall , Chew suffered a myocardial infarction , and he was sent to a private clinic and then to the General Hospital . It was revealed that he suffered from two similar attacks recently. [ 41 ] [ 42 ] Chew died on 19 May 1967. text: Wendy (coyote) - Wikipedia Jump to content Search Search Wendy (coyote) Add languages Add links From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia Wild coyote in Los Angeles (died 2026) Wendy Other name Sunshine Species Coyote ( Canis latrans ) Sex Female Born c. 2023 Died ( 2026-09-08 ) September 8, 2026 Simi Valley, California , US Cause of death Euthanasia following severe infection caused by a gunshot to the head Residence Studio City, California , US Wendy , also known as Sunshine , [ 1 ] was a wild coyote who lived in Studio City, California , United States. She was known for her deformed face, caused by a gunshot wound, and was euthanized on September 8, 2026. History [ edit ] Around 2023 or 2024, residents of the Los Angeles neighborhood of Studio City began to notice a wild coyote frequenting the area, and they first noticed swelling on her face in 2025. [ 2 ] [ 3 ] Rescuers originally thought her deformity might be a tumor , then the result of a wildlife–vehicle collision after a resident reported that the coyote had been involved in one around the time the deformity was first noticed. [ 3 ] Rescuers also determined the coyote, by now named Wendy, was traversing an inconsistent 2.5-mile (4.0 km) route in the area while most likely being fed by locals. [ 4 ] On July 14, animal-care organization Wildlife Care of Southern California from Simi Valley, California , began tracking the coyote online; Urban Rescue and Southern California Pit Bull Rescue also assisted. The organizations began tracking the animal in person on August 7 and captured her on August 31, 2026. [ 4 ] Wendy was estimated to be three years old when she was captured. [ 5 ] [ 6 ] An examination revealed two pellets lodged in her head, indicating that at some point she had been shot by a pellet gun ; [ 2 ] [ 5 ] they also found that a severe infection had destroyed her upper left jaw bone. Rescuers fed her soft foods and treated her with antibiotics and anti-inflammatory medication, then euthanized her on September 8, 2026, after determining that no treatment or surgery could restore her normal function. [ 5 ] [ 6 ] The organization explained that she would require a soft food diet for the rest of her life, meaning she could not return to the wild nor would she experience freedom in a captive environment, and that "keeping her alive under those circumstances would not be humane." [ 7 ] The day after her death, Southern California Pit Bull Rescue announced a $10,000 reward for information leading to the arrest and conviction of her shooter. [ 8 ] On September 16, the reward was increased to $21,000.
