[[Kolkata]] has a long-established tradition of sweet shops selling [[Bengali cuisine|Bengali]] sweets such as [[Sandesh (confectionery)|{{transliteration|bn|sandesh}}]], as well as seasonal preparations such as [[Pitha|{{transliteration|bn|pithe}}]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Explore Mathura's Delicious Food Scene |url=https://www.incredibleindia.gov.in/en/uttar-pradesh/mathura/enjoy-a-taste-of-mathura |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20261022024818/https://www.incredibleindia.gov.in/en/uttar-pradesh/mathura/enjoy-a-taste-of-mathura |archive-date=22 October 2026 |access-date=22 October 2026 |website=Incredible India}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Winter delicacies that you must try in Kolkata |url=https://www.incredibleindia.gov.in/en/west-bengal/kolkata/winter-delicacies-that-you-should-try-in-kolkata |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20261022025430/https://www.incredibleindia.gov.in/en/west-bengal/kolkata/winter-delicacies-that-you-should-try-in-kolkata |archive-date=22 October 2026 |access-date=22 October 2026 |website=Incredible India}}</ref> ==== Japan ==== In the [[Edo period]], confectionery stores bore the symbol of [[paulownia]] and swirling patterns, and often had an image of Kawaguchiya, one of the two main candy brands in the [[An'ei|An'ei era]]. Small-scale shops had umbrellas to protect candies from melting or getting wet. To increase sales, some vendors wore women's clothing or displayed [[Karakuri puppet|{{transliteration|ja|karakuri}} puppets]]. A vendor sang along with a [[Shamisen|{{transliteration|ja|shamisen}}]] and was rewarded with clothing bearing the [[Onoe Kikugorō V]] family's crest.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Part 1 – Kaleidoscope of Books |url=https://www.ndl.go.jp/kaleido/e/entry/25/1.html |access-date=20 October 2026 |website=Wagashi – Kaleidoscope of Books |language=ja |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250430204625/https://www.ndl.go.jp/kaleido/e/entry/25/1.html |archive-date=30 April 2025 |url-status=live}}</ref> In a 1777{{nbsp}}listing, there were 28 confectionery stores in [[Edo]] (now [[Tokyo]]). Several of them called themselves "{{transliteration|ja|kudarikyogashiya}}" to benefit from an association with "{{transliteration|ja|kudarimono}}", prized goods from the region of [[Kamigata]]. {{transliteration|ja|Kyoto meibutsu mizu no fukiyose}} had confectionery reviews, judging their specialities, product colour, degree of steaming for steamed confectionery and even the confectionery's container.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Part 2 – Kaleidoscope of Books |url=https://www.ndl.go.jp/kaleido/e/entry/25/2.html |access-date=20 October 2026 |website=Wagashi – Kaleidoscope of Books |language=ja |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260119002736/https://www.ndl.go.jp/kaleido/e/entry/25/2.html |archive-date=19 January 2026 |url-status=live}}</ref> Cafés began to appear in the [[Meiji era]], serving Western sweets and coffee; they developed further during the [[Taishō era]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Part 3 – Kaleidoscope of Books |url=https://www.ndl.go.jp/kaleido/e/entry/25/3.html |access-date=20 October 2026 |website=Wagashi – Kaleidoscope of Books |language=ja |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260314202638/https://www.ndl.go.jp/kaleido/e/entry/25/3.html |archive-date=14 March 2026 |url-status=live}}</ref> [[File:A Riot of Shapes and Colors (22664782712).jpg|thumb|Recreation of a {{transliteration|ja|dagashiya}} at Ōme Akasuka Fujio Kaikan Museum (Retro Museum of Packaging from the Showa Era, 1926–1989)]] Prior to the 1980s, the Japanese custom for purchasing candy took place at a [[Dagashiya|{{transliteration|ja|dagashiya}}]] ({{lang|ja|駄菓子屋}}), also known as a "trivial sweets shop". When [[Convenience store|{{transliteration|ja|konbini}}]] stores began to take root in the late 1980s, the smaller, less-stocked {{transliteration|ja|dagashiya}} market began to face steady competition.<ref name="Ehrenreich">{{Cite web |last=Ehrenreich |title=Trivial sweets shops offer interesting gateway to retro Japan |url=https://japan.stripes.com/food-drink/trivial-sweets-shops-offer-interesting-gateway-to-retro-japan.html1 |access-date=19 October 2026 |website=Stripes Japan |first=Alex |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260117213251/https://japan.stripes.com/food-drink/trivial-sweets-shops-offer-interesting-gateway-to-retro-japan.html1 |archive-date=17 January 2026}}</ref> Despite this competition, a number of {{transliteration|ja|dagashiya}} chains managed to survive. One notable example is Okashi no Machioka, known for selling both Western items such as potato chips and chocolate bars, alongside traditional snacks such as [[Yōkan|{{transliteration|ja|yōkan}}]] ({{lang|ja|羊羹}}) and [[Umaibō|{{transliteration|ja|umaibō}}]] ({{lang|ja|うまい棒}}). Some {{transliteration|ja|dagashiya}} stores have been in the same location for centuries. One example is Kami-kawaguchiya, which was established in [[Zōshigaya]] and, as of 2026, remained open for over 200 years.<ref name="Ehrenreich" /> Notable candies sold at Japanese confectioneries include plum-flavoured snacks, jellies, jams, mints, nuts and crackers. [[Senbei|{{transliteration|ja|Senbei}}]] ({{lang|ja|煎餅}}), a type of [[rice cracker]], can also be regularly spotted in shops like these. Seafood is also a very common offering in these shops; {{transliteration|ja|iwashi}} (dried sardines) and {{transliteration|ja|ika}} (dried squid) are very popular snacks.<ref name="Ehrenreich" /> ==== Korea ==== During the [[Joseon]] dynasty, honey and [[Yeot|{{transliteration|ko|yeot}}]] were used to sweeten food while sugar imported in small quantities from China was used primarily as a medicinal ingredient for the royal court and upper classes. In the 1890s, stores in [[Jongno District]] began selling candies made from imported sugar.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Kim |first=Mihye |date=2023-08-12 |title=꿀보다 달콤한 설탕, 조선인 입맛·체형까지 바꾸다 |trans-title=Sugar, Sweeter Than Honey, Transformed Koreans' Taste and Even Their Body Shape |url=https://www.joongang.co.kr/article/25184239 |work=[[Joongang Ilbo]] |language=ko}}</ref> ==== Malaysia ==== During the early 20th century, traditional coffee shops known as ''[[kopitiam]]'' became established in British Malaya. Many were operated by Hainanese Chinese immigrants and served coffee alongside local foods and baked goods. Dedicated confectionery businesses subsequently developed, including King's Confectionery, which grew from a family bakery established in the 1960s, and Chiap Tong, a biscuit and candy shop founded in Kuala Lumpur in 1942.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Yew |first=John Lee Kean |date=2016-12-23 |title=King’s Confectionery: Transferring Tacit Knowledge from Malaysia to Bangladesh |url=https://doi.org/10.1177/2277977916665984 |journal=South Asian Journal of Business and Management Cases |language=EN |publisher=SAGE Publications |volume=5 |issue=2 |pages=198–208 |doi=10.1177/2277977916665984 |issn=2277-9779}}</ref> ==== Turkey ==== Confectioneries in [[Konya]] from the 13th century are mentioned in the writings of Sufi poet [[Rumi|Mevlânâ]]. Sweets were sold in shops and street stands and occasionally advertised and sold on [[Float (parade)|floats]] in street processions, as depicted in 16th-century [[Ottoman miniature]]s. [[Parrot]]s were sometimes associated with sweets through verses of mystic poetry in which they desired sweets and would become eloquent, or "sweet-tongued", after consuming sugar.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Işın |first=Priscilla Mary |url=http://archive.org/details/sherbetspicecomp0000isnp |title=Sherbet & spice : the complete story of Turkish sweets and desserts |date=2013 |publisher=New York : I.B. Tauris |others=Internet Archive |isbn=978-1-84885-898-5}}</ref>[[File:Ali Muhiddin Hacı Bekir (1777).jpg|thumb|The Hacı Bekir shop in [[Istanbul]]]] Turkey, and especially its [[Fatih|Historical Peninsula]], is home to several confectioneries. These stores have been operating since the 18th and 19th centuries. These confectioneries catered to the cosmopolitan upper-middle class who then inhabited the area. These shops can be seen as a result of the Islamic hospitality culture present in Anatolia, where feeding guests and such is seen as a command of the [[Muhammad|Prophet Muhammad]].<ref>Sahih al-Bukhari 6135</ref>{{better source needed|date=October 2026}} Some of the oldest surviving confectioneries from this era are Şekerci Cafer Erol, Ali Muhittin Hacı Bekir and Hicipoğlu Şekerleme, which reportedly is the oldest confectionery in Istanbul and has been in operation since 1752.<ref>{{Cite web |title=T.C. İstanbul Valiliği - İstanbul'da Nostalji: Tarihi Şekerciler |url=https://istanbul.gov.tr/istanbulda-nostalji-tarihi-sekerciler |access-date=2026-10-22 |website=istanbul.gov.tr |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260120000408/https://www.istanbul.gov.tr/istanbulda-nostalji-tarihi-sekerciler |archive-date=20 January 2026 |url-status=live}}</ref> The Hacı Bekir shop in Istanbul, which opened in 1777, claims to have created the modern [[Turkish delight]] ({{lang|tr|lokum}}). The shop is one of the 100 oldest companies in the world.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/travel/article/20181003-the-secret-story-behind-turkish-delight|title=The secret story behind Turkish delight |first=Demetrios |last=Ioannou |website=Bbc.com |date=4 October 2018 |access-date=19 October 2026|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260403023855/https://www.bbc.com/travel/article/20181003-the-secret-story-behind-turkish-delight|archive-date=3 April 2026|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://cnaluxury.channelnewsasia.com/remarkableliving/turkish-delight-heritage-shop-istanbul-173781|title=The story of a 240-year-old sweet shop that makes Turkish Delights fit for a king|website=CNA Luxury|access-date=19 October 2026|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20261009155411/https://cnaluxury.channelnewsasia.com/remarkableliving/turkish-delight-heritage-shop-istanbul-173781|archive-date=9 October 2026|url-status=live|date=2 February 2020|last=Alimin|first=Jasmine}}</ref> === Europe === ==== France ==== [[File:À la Mère de Famille in 2021.jpg|thumb|À la Mère de Famille, one of France's oldest confectionery stores]] One of France's oldest {{lang|fr|confiseries}}, À la Mère de Famille, was founded by Pierre-Jean Bernard and opened in 1761. Candy had been consumed in the country since the [[Middle Ages]], when a man named Regnaut-Barbon founded a guild of confectioners, but it was only eaten by the aristocracy and royalty and used in religious ceremonies.<ref name="parisunlocked2" /> ==== Germany ==== [[File:Konditorei Fester.jpg|thumb|Traditional Konditorei Fester, {{abbr|est.|established}} 1926 in Spandau, Berlin, Germany|alt=A bright storefront reading "Konditorei Fester." Various golden decorations and candy shelves are visible through the front window.]] In Germany, the traditional high-end confectionery shop and café is known as a [[Konditorei|{{lang|de|Konditorei|nocat=yes}}]]. Unlike a standard retail sweet shop or a bread [[bakery]] ({{lang|de|Bäckerei}}), a {{lang|de|Konditorei}} specialises in fine baked goods, elaborate tortes, pastries and artisanal chocolates, frequently operating alongside an integrated sit-down café.<ref>{{cite web |title=German Coffee and Cake Culture Explained |date=9 March 2026 |url=https://nomadepicureans.com/europe/german-coffee-and-cake-culture-explained-a-complete-guide-for-every-visitor/ |publisher=Nomad Epicureans |access-date=19 October 2026}}</ref> Master confectioners ({{lang|de|Konditormeister}}) undergo rigorous, regulated vocational training, maintaining a distinction between scratch-made artisanal confections and mass-produced commercial snacks.<ref>{{Cite web |title=KondAusbV 2003 – Verordnung über die Berufsausbildung zum Konditor/zur Konditorin |url=https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/kondausbv_2003/BJNR079000003.html#:~:text=%C2%A7%201%20Staatliche%20Anerkennung%20des%20Ausbildungsberufes.%20Der,der%20Anlage%20A%20der%20Handwerksordnung%20staatlich%20anerkannt. |access-date=19 October 2026 |website=Gesetze-im-internet.de |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250820215352/https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/kondausbv_2003/BJNR079000003.html#:~:text=%C2%A7%201%20Staatliche%20Anerkennung%20des%20Ausbildungsberufes.%20Der,der%20Anlage%20A%20der%20Handwerksordnung%20staatlich%20anerkannt. |archive-date=20 August 2025 |url-status=live}}</ref> The trade's roots stretch deep into the mediaeval [[Guilds in medieval Europe|European guild system]]. This is the second time my name has been spelt wrong: first time it was "Watts." It was misspelled by my mentor who also added a truly bizarre sentence about me being "associated with the term " I guess "Performance Poetry." All of it so weird that it was removed as too badly written and an obvious attempt to "namedrop" Marty Watt. All I did was write poems to be performed from memory for a live audience, I did perform a LOT in the 1970s and 1980s. LOTS of reviews in mainstream press - all documented ready to be sources. page numbers, dates . . . . Very few if any others were doing "Performance Poetry" in the '70s - Patti Smith did briefly after seeing me but then went into punk rock stardom. By the late 70s there was Rap / Hip Hop etc - and a long time after that something called SLAM. Much documentation about "Performance Poetry" is confusing because later writers - academic journals use term loosely "Performance Poets" about people in the Fifties , Sixties that, when checked into, nothing like that can be found. Energetic poets, some made and played tapes of themselves chanting or something. I can't seem to get myself in the list of "Performance Poets" either. I think there's a link to that on the "Performance Poetry" article. The big three, there are MANY more . And all the stuff I have documented of the term "Performance Poetry" being used throughout the Seventies. Wikipedia is made up of volunteers: I have restructured the page to make it easier so that others can come to it in the future and edit it. What can you do? Wait. People will edit the page if they're interested. That's how Wikipedia works. We're not a company. I can't think of another encyclopedia where you can demand changes to articles. Your primary interest also appears to be what that page says about you and you'll find that's the opposite motivation for most volunteers who you're relying on to fix the page. Shortcuts WP:AFI WP:AFI WP:TWAFI WP:TWAFI We identify and facilitate collaboration at underdeveloped articles that require improvement . Our primary goal is to use these articles as starting-points for newcomers to make their first edits. [ a ] So far, we have improved hundreds of articles; some have even been promoted to good or featured article status! See if there's suggestions for improvement you could make or a newcomer you could help at the current article for improvement, or join the project today ! Archive Nominate an article Check out the project's Articles for improvement page. Just start editing and help newcomers while improving our selected articles! You can nominate an article to be worked on. You may join the project by adding your name to the members list , and can sign up for weekly notices . If you have any questions, please feel free to ask at our talk page , and also at the Teahouse or Help desk . If you are new to Wikipedia, you may find Wikipedia's tutorial useful – it covers the basics of Wikipedia in under an hour. Be bold! Articles here can be edited at any time by all users, regardless of project membership status. Goals The project's four main tasks are to: Coordinate and collaborate to engage newcomers and improve articles. Identify candidate articles. Select the order they appear on the community portal in the Articles for improvement section. Assess and track our accomplishments. Since its inception, the 'Articles for Improvement' project has successfully enhanced hundreds of articles, with several achieving 'Good Article' or 'Featured Article' status, demonstrating the impact of collaborative editing efforts. Upcoming articles See also: Wikipedia:Articles for improvement/Schedule Want to help with future articles? Look for sources and add them on the talk pages using the { { Refideas } } template to help newcomers! Successful nominations are listed on the articles list . Articles on that page can be improved at any time . One article is randomly selected from the list of articles each week, which is placed in the schedule . A few weeks later, it's that article's turn to be the week's selected AFI article! Members The project member list is located at the Members page. Assessment Our assessment criteria and procedure are explained on the Assessment page. Like many other WikiProjects, AFI assesses the articles it is involved with. Unlike other projects, we only assess the article's state before and immediately after its week of collaborative editing – that improvement is one (but not the only) measure of our success. Automation and tools AFI makes use of various templates . See the Automation page for details, including banners, talk page messages, user and project maintenance templates. The project's bot tasks are also listed here, currently undertaken by MusikBot . Their existence was publicly announced on 20 October 2026. [ 4 ] An emergency patch for versions 8.2, 8.3, 8.4 and 8.5 and details about the vulnerabilities were released the following day, with numerous websites temporarily taken offline to apply the patches before exploits could be used. [ 5 ] PHP is a popular programming language that many website and web application codebases are built upon. The vulnerabilities are estimated to affect nearly 70% of websites . Discovery [ edit ] The vulnerabilities were independently discovered by two parties: Ryan Austin, a researcher at the California -based security firm Calif, [ 6 ] as part of the OpenAI "Patch the Planet" project in August 2026, and the Israeli–American cloud security company Wiz , a subsidiary of Alphabet Inc. and a part of Google Cloud . [ 7.1 ] Austin used OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Sol model to assist with finding the vulnerability. [ 7.1 ] Wiz researchers used the large language models Gemini 4 Argon and GPT-5.6 Sol, as well as their own tool, Wiz Atlas, to help with their research. [ 8 ] Wiz coined the name "PHP2Shell" indicating that PHP exploits would enable execution of shell commands on affected servers. [ 9 ] PHP versions as early as 5.4 (released in 2012) [ 10 ] were affected by these vulnerabilities, and while concerns around memory safety bugs had been raised decades before, no action was taken at the time because it was not thought that developing a working exploit could be feasible. [ 11 ] [ 7.2 ] A PHP core developer discovered the out-of-memory error behind one of the vulnerabilities during an audit in 2024, but the bug was never fixed; the development team could not reach consensus on how to do so and a specific exploit had not yet been discovered, so the issue was not prioritized. [ 12 ] [ 13 ] The vulnerability was rated 9.2 (critical) out of 10 under CVSS v4.0 by PHP developers, [ 14 ] while security firm watchTowr rated it a full 10.0. [ 15 ] Patches [ edit ] The maintainers of PHP released patched versions of PHP 8.2, 8.3, 8.4, and 8.5 (8.2.35, 8.3.36, 8.4.27, and 8.5.12). [ 5 ] Source code patches were released for version 7.4, 8.0, and 8.1, but no official updated binaries for those versions were released as they are considered end of life . [ 5 ] Temporary mitigations were also published, but the maintainers said there were no complete mitigations and that updating was the only safe choice. [ 5 ] Both vulnerabilities were published through GitHub security advisories on 21 October 2026 at 13:34 UTC, [ 16 ] [ 17 ] 26 minutes before the announced release time, with the PHP website updated shortly thereafter. [ 18 ] cPanel and CloudLinux released backports in their ecosystems. [ 19 ] [ 20 ] Volunteer maintainer Ondřej Surý, who was given advance access to the fixes by the PHP project, prepared installable packages for old versions from the patched source code so that server administrators could automate deployments without compiling PHP themselves. [ 21 ] In response to claims on X that unpatched older PHP releases left one-third of the internet permanently vulnerable, Surý stated that there were ways to patch and update the older versions as well. [ 22 ] The PHP maintainers announced the update early and before release, after news of the vulnerabilities leaked on 20 October on the Hacker News forums, [ 23 ] in a post on X (formerly Twitter) by cybersecurity company watchTowr labs, and in a proof-of-concept exploit video mistakenly released by Calif. [ 7.3 ] [ 12 ] The early notice on PHP.net encouraged users to prepare and update as soon as the patch was released. [ 5 ] One security firm, Sansec, expected "mass attacks to start within 15 minutes of the release". [ 24 ] Proof-of-concept exploits, write-ups, and partial mitigations started circulating on the Internet before the end of the embargo, after development platform Chainguard released patched versions of the software early; this allowed attackers to determine what code had been changed. [ 15 ] [ 12 ] Amazon Threat Intelligence identified a PHP2Shell exploitation attempt dating back to 17 October 2026, in MadPot telemetry, four days before public disclosure. [ 25 ] Cloudflare reported signs of early exploitation prior to public patch release, and deployed temporary web application firewall rules as an attempted stopgap mitigation against the vulnerability. [ 26 ] [ 27 ] [ 28 ] Security firm watchTowr said it had observed exploitation in the wild by 21 October through its honeypot network, [ 29 ] while the US Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency said it had not observed exploitation as of the same day. [ 30 ] Impact [ edit ] Warning posted on the English Wikipedia about community-owned tools being offline due to the PHP2Shell incident. The potential impacts of the vulnerability were widespread. Approximately 69% of websites whose server-side programming language is known by W3Techs use PHP, including those that use content management systems such as Drupal , Joomla , and WordPress . [ 30.1 ] [ 31 ] PHP is also bundled with vendor appliances, web host control panels such as cPanel and Plesk , and some Windows applications. [ 32 ] Following advice from CERT -EU and the British National Cyber Security Centre (NCSC), many organizations across Europe took their websites offline as a precaution while the patches were pending, including the Dutch government portal Overheid.nl, the Danish national school communication platform, all Finnish government public-facing web services, and all websites of the French Interior Ministry . [ 8 ] [ 31 ] [ 33 ] [ 34 ] Some Canadian government websites were temporarily taken down as a precaution as taken following guidance from the Canadian Centre for Cyber Security . [ 35 ] The US National Security Agency recommended that websites go offline if unable to update immediately. [ 11 ] [ 36 ] The NCSC released a similar warning, urging organizations to be wary of backdoors . [ 37 ] The Japanese National Cybersecurity Office advised PHP users to immediately update their systems. [ 38 ] The Singaporean Cyber Security Agency has also urged organizations in Singapore to fix the security flaws. [ 39 ] [ 40 ] The Wikimedia Foundation shut down many of their supporting services, and forum sites such as 4chan and Something Awful went offline. [ 30 ] [ 41 ] [ 11 ] Several Japanese websites and applications also went offline, including games such as Umamusume: Pretty Derby , Granblue Fantasy , Princess Connect! Re:Dive , and numerous e-commerce sites. [ 38 ] [ 41 ] The Internet Archive briefly shut down to fix the issue. [ 42 ] Analysis [ edit ] Researchers at Wiz stated that the issue was on par with Heartbleed , a 2014 vulnerability that affected OpenSSL , an encryption library used by about two-thirds of the web at the time. [ 43 ] Commentary in The Guardian noted that the PHP Foundation , which maintains the PHP language, only had 13 full- and part-time employees, and relied on financial contributions, whereas AI research, which was credited with helping discover the vulnerability, received "billions" in investment. [ 44 ] Coverage in The New York Times said that PHP was "pervasive" and speculated that "everyday users" could have their personal data put at risk. [ 45 ] Czech volunteer Ondřej Surý was credited with playing a crucial role in automating the necessary patches. PHP Paradigm Multi-paradigm : imperative , functional , object-oriented , procedural , reflective Designed by Rasmus Lerdorf Developer The PHP Development Team , Zend Technologies , PHP Foundation First appeared 8 June 1995 ; 31 years ago ( 1995-06-08 ) [ 1 ] [ 2 ] Stable release 8.5.12 [ 3 ] / 21 October 2026 ; 4 days ago ( 21 October 2026 ) Typing discipline Dynamic , weak , gradual [ 4 ] Implementation language C (primarily; some components in C++ ) OS Unix-like , Windows , macOS , IBM i , OpenVMS , IBM Z License Modified BSD License Filename extensions .php , .phar , .phtml , .pht , .phps , .phpt Website www .php .net Major implementations Zend Engine , HHVM , PeachPie , Quercus , Parrot Influenced by Perl , C , C++ , [ 5 ] C# , [ 5 ] [ 6 ] Java , [ 7 ] Kotlin , [ 8 ] Tcl , [ 2 ] JavaScript , [ 9 ] Rust , [ 5 ] [ 10 ] [ 8 ] [ 6 ] Swift [ 8 ] [ 6 ] Influenced Hack , JSP , ASP , React JS PHP Programming at Wikibooks PHP is a general-purpose scripting language geared toward web development . [ 11 ] It was created by Danish-Canadian programmer Rasmus Lerdorf in 1993 and released in 1995. [ 12 ] [ 13 ] The PHP reference implementation is now produced by the PHP Group. [ 14 ] PHP was originally an abbreviation of " Personal Home Page ", but it now stands for the recursive backronym " PHP: Hypertext Preprocessor ". [ 15 ] : 14 PHP code is usually processed on a web server by a PHP interpreter implemented as a module , a daemon , or a Common Gateway Interface (CGI) executable. On a web server, the result of the interpreted and executed PHP code—which may be any type of data, such as generated HTML or binary image data—can form the whole or part of an HTTP response. Various web template systems , web content management systems , and web frameworks can be employed to orchestrate or facilitate the generation of that response. PHP can be used for programming tasks outside the web context, though such use is rare. PHP code can also be directly executed from the command line . The standard PHP interpreter, powered by the Zend Engine , is free software released under the PHP License . PHP has been widely ported and can be deployed on most web servers across various operating systems and platforms. History [ edit ] The PHP language at first evolved without a written formal specification or standard , with the original implementation acting as the de facto standard that other implementations aimed to follow. Rasmus Lerdorf , creator of PHP; and Andi Gutmans and Zeev Suraski , creators of the Zend Engine Origins (1993 to 1997) [ edit ] Rasmus Lerdorf wrote several Common Gateway Interface (CGI) programs in C , [ 16 ] [ 17 ] which he used to maintain his personal homepage . He extended them to work with HTML forms and communicate with databases , and called this implementation "Personal Home Page/Forms Interpreter" or PHP/FI. An example of the early PHP syntax : [ 18 ] <!--include /text/header.html--> <!--getenv HTTP_USER_AGENT--> <!--if substr $exec_result Mozilla--> Hey, you are using Netscape! < p > <!--endif--> <!--sql database select * from table where user='$username'--> <!--ifless $numentries 1--> Sorry, that record does not exist < p > <!--endif exit--> Welcome <!--$user--> ! < p > You have <!--$index:0--> credits left in your account. < p > <!--include /text/footer.html--> PHP/FI could be used to build simple, dynamic web applications . To accelerate bug reporting and improve the code, Lerdorf initially announced the release of PHP/FI as "Personal Home Page Tools (PHP Tools) version 1.0" on the Usenet discussion group comp.infosystems.www.authoring.cgi on 8 June 1995. [ 1 ] [ 19 ] This release included basic functionality such as Perl-like variables , form handling, and the ability to embed HTML . By this point, the syntax had changed to resemble that of Perl , but was simpler, more limited, and less consistent. [ 20 ] [ 14 ] Early PHP was never intended to be a new programming language ; rather, it grew organically. Lerdorf has said: "I don't know how to stop it [...] there was never any intent to write a programming language [...] I have absolutely no idea how to write a programming language [...] I just kept adding the next logical step on the way." [ 21 ] A development team began to form and, after months of work and beta testing, officially released PHP/FI 2 in November 1997. [ 22 ] The fact that PHP was not originally designed, but instead was developed organically has led to inconsistent naming of functions and inconsistent ordering of their parameters. [ 23 ] In some cases, the function names were chosen to match the lower-level libraries PHP was "wrapping", [ 24 ] while in some very early versions of PHP the length of the function names was used internally as a hash function , so names were chosen to improve the distribution of hash values . [ 25 ] PHP 3 and 4 (1998 to 2004) [ edit ] An example of PHP code for the WordPress content management system Zeev Suraski and Andi Gutmans rewrote the parser in 1997 and formed the base of PHP 3, changing the language's name to the recursive acronym PHP: Hypertext Preprocessor . [ 14 ] [ 26 ] Public testing of PHP 3 then began, and the official launch was in June 1998. Suraski and Gutmans then started a new rewrite of PHP's core, producing the Zend Engine in 1999. [ 27 ] They also founded Zend Technologies in Ramat Gan , Israel. [ 14 ] On 22 May 2000, PHP 4.0, powered by the Zend Engine 1.0, was released. [ 14 ] By August 2008, this branch had reached version 4.4.9. PHP 4 is now no longer under development, nor are any security updates planned to be released. [ 28 ] [ 29 ] Early PHP 5 (2004 to 2006) [ edit ] On 1 July 2004, PHP 5.0 was released, powered by the new Zend Engine 2.0. [ 14 ] PHP 5.0 included significant changes to the language, most notably an overhauled approach to object-oriented programming , as well as iterators and exceptions . [ 30 ] PHP 5.1 and PHP 5.2 were released the following years, adding smaller improvements and new features, such as the PHP Data Objects (PDO) extension (which defines a lightweight and consistent interface for accessing databases) In 2008, PHP 5.x became the only stable version under development. Many high-profile open-source projects ceased to support PHP 4 in new code from February 5, 2008, because of the GoPHP5 initiative, [ 31 ] provided by a consortium of PHP developers promoting the transition from PHP 4 to PHP 5. [ 32 ] [ 33 ] PHP 6 and Unicode [ edit ] PHP's native string functions worked only on raw bytes, making use with multibyte character encodings difficult. [ 34 ] [ 35 ] In 2005, a project headed by Andrei Zmievski was initiated to bring native Unicode support throughout PHP, by embedding the International Components for Unicode (ICU) library, and representing text strings as UTF-16 internally. [ 36 ] Since this would cause major changes both to the internals of the language and to user code, it was planned to release this as version 6.0 of the language, along with other major features then in development. [ 37 ] However, a shortage of developers who understood the necessary changes, and performance problems arising from conversion to and from UTF-16, which is rarely used in a web context, led to delays in the project. [ 38 ] As a result, a PHP 5.3 release was created in 2009, and in March 2010, the project in its current form was officially abandoned, and a PHP 5.4 release was prepared to contain most remaining non-Unicode features from PHP 6. [ 39 ] Initial hopes were that a new plan would be formed for Unicode integration, but by 2014 none had been adopted. [ citation needed ] PHP does support using Unicode encodings for source code, but the language still (as of version 8) has no abstract "Unicode string" type. All strings are stored in as 8-bit bytes in a specific byte encoding. There are functions that can distinguish between the number of bytes, Unicode points, and graphemes as needed, or convert to a different encoding. [ 40 ] The Multibye String extension [ 41 ] has been available since at least PHP 4.0.6 [ 42 ] does provide functions that operation more abstractly on Unicode strings, and the byte encoding of its internal representation is configurable. [ 43 ] Later PHP 5 (2009 to 2014) [ edit ] Because it contained features originally intended to be part of 6.0, PHP 5.3 was a significant release, adding support for namespaces , closures , late static binding , [ 44 ] [ 45 ] and many fixes and improvements to standard functions. With the Unicode branch officially abandoned, a new release process was adopted in 2011, planning a yearly release cycle, and a clear distinction between "feature releases" (x.y.z to x.y+1.0) and "major releases" (x.y.z to x+1.0.0). [ 46 ] Remaining features which had been planned for the 6.0 release were included in PHP 5.4, released in March 2012, such as trait support and a new "short array syntax". This was followed by more incremental changes in PHP 5.5 (June 2013) and 5.6 (August 2014). For PHP versions 5.3 and 5.4, the only available Microsoft Windows binary distributions were 32-bit IA-32 builds, [ 47 ] [ 48 ] requiring Windows 32-bit compatibility mode while using Internet Information Services (IIS) on a 64-bit Windows platform. PHP version 5.5 made the 64-bit x86-64 builds available for Microsoft Windows. [ 49 ] Official security support for PHP 5.6 ended on 31 December 2018. [ 50 ] PHP 7.x (2015 to 2019) [ edit ] During 2014 and 2015, a new major PHP version was developed that became PHP 7.0. The numbering of this version involved some debate among internal developers. [ 51 ] While the PHP 6 Unicode experiments had never been released, several articles and book titles referenced the PHP 6 names, which might have caused confusion if a new release were to reuse the name. [ 52 ] After a vote, the name PHP 7 was chosen. [ 53 ] The foundation of PHP 7.0 was a PHP branch that was originally dubbed PHP next generation ( phpng ). It was written by Dmitry Stogov, Xinchen Hui and Nikita Popov, [ 54 ] and aimed to optimize PHP performance by refactoring the Zend Engine while retaining near-complete language compatibility. [ 55 ] By 14 July 2014, WordPress -based benchmarks, which served as the main benchmark suite for the phpng project, showed an almost 100% increase in performance. Changes from phpng make it easier to improve performance in future versions, as more compact data structures and other changes are seen as better suited for a successful migration to a just-in-time (JIT) compiler. [ 56 ] Because of the significant changes, the reworked Zend Engine was called Zend Engine 3 , succeeding Zend Engine 2 used in PHP 5.x. [ 57 ] PHP 7.0 also included changes which were not backward compatible, as allowed for "major versions" under the versioning scheme agreed in 2011. [ 46 ] Changes to the core language included a more consistent handling of variable dereferencing, [ 58 ] a more predictable behavior of the foreach statement , [ 59 ] and platform consistency of bitwise shifts [ 60 ] and floating-point to integer conversion. [ 60 ] [ 61 ] Several unmaintained or deprecated server application programming interfaces (SAPIs) and extensions were removed from the PHP core, most notably the legacy mysql extension. [ 62 ] Other legacy features were also removed, such as ASP-style delimiters < % and % > and < script language="php" > ... < /script > . [ 63 ] PHP 7.0 marked the beginning of an expansion in PHP's type system. In PHP 5.x, only function parameters could have type declarations, but this was extended to function return types in 7.0, [ 64 ] and object properties in 7.4. [ 65 ] The types expressible also expanded, with scalar types (integer, float, string, and boolean) in 7.0; [ 66 ] iterable type, [ 67 ] nullable types, [ 68 ] and void return type , [ 69 ] all in 7.1; and the object type in 7.2. [ 70 ] Other changes in this period aimed to add expressiveness to the language, such as the ?? ( null coalesce ) [ 71 ] and <=> "spaceship" three-way comparison [ 72 ] operators in 7.0; new syntax for array dereferencing [ 73 ] and catching multiple exception types in PHP 7.1; [ 74 ] more flexible Heredoc and Nowdoc syntax [ 75 ] in 7.3; and the null-coalescing assignment operator in 7.4. [ 76 ] PHP 8.x (2020 onwards) [ edit ] PHP 8.0 was released on 26 November 2020, as a major version with breaking changes from previous versions. [ 77 ] [ 78 ] One of the most high-profile changes was the addition of a JIT compiler , which can provide substantial performance improvements for some use cases. [ 79 ] [ 80 ] Substantial improvements were expected more for mathematical-type operations than for common web-development use cases. [ 81 ] Additionally, the performance advantage of the JIT compiler provides the potential to move some code from C to PHP. [ 82 ] A significant addition to the language in 8.0 is attributes , which allow metadata to be added to program elements such as classes, methods, and parameters. [ 77 ] Later versions added built-in attributes which change the behaviour of the language, such as the #[ \SensitiveParameter ] attribute in PHP 8.2, [ 83 ] #[ \Override ] in PHP 8.3, [ 84 ] #[ \Deprecated ] in PHP 8.4, [ 85 ] and the #[ \NoDiscard ] and #[ \DelayedTargetValidation ] attributes in PHP 8.5. [ 86 ] [ 87 ] [ 88 ] A significant extension to the language's type system is the addition of composite types: union types in PHP 8.0 (e.g. int | string meaning "either integer or string"), [ 89 ] intersection types in PHP 8.1 (e.g. Traversable & Countable meaning the value must implement both the Traversable and Countable interfaces), [ 90 ] and disjunctive normal form (DNF) types in PHP 8.2 (unions of intersections, such as array | ( Traversable & Countable ) ). [ 91 ] Additional special type keywords have been added, such as mixed and static in PHP 8.0, [ 77 ] never (a bottom type indicating that a function never returns) in PHP 8.1, [ 92 ] and null , false , and true as stand-alone types in PHP 8.2. [ 93 ] [ 94 ] The addition of a rich type system is part of a general trend towards a stricter language, and PHP 8.0 included breaking changes to the handling of string to number comparisons, [ 95 ] numeric strings, [ 96 ] and incompatible method signatures. [ 97 ] Later versions have introduced deprecation notices for behaviour which is planned as a breaking change in a future major version, such as passing null to non-nullable internal function parameters [ 98 ] and referring to properties which have not been declared on the class. [ 193 ] Preview version: 8.6 19 November 2026 [ 194 ] Legend: Unsupported Supported Latest version Preview version Future version Beginning on 28 June 2011, the PHP Development Team implemented a timeline for the release of new versions of PHP. [ 46 ] Under this system, at least one release should occur every month. Once per year, a minor release should occur which may include new features. Every minor release should at least be supported for two years with security and bug fixes, followed by at least one year of only security fixes, for a total of a three-year release process for every minor release. No new features, unless small and self-contained, are to be introduced into a minor release during the three-year release process. A 2024 RFC extended the length of the security fix only period to two years, fixed all end of life dates to 31 December, and removed the exception that allowed for "small and self-contained" features to be introduced in patch versions. [ 195 ] Prevalence of outdated versions [ edit ] W3Techs reports that as of November 2025 [ update ] (about three years since PHP 7 was discontinued and 23 months after the PHP 8.3 release), unsupported versions such as PHP 7 were still used by well over half of PHP websites , which are outdated and known to be insecure. [ 196 ] [ 197 ] Those included the 9.7% of PHP websites using the even more outdated (discontinued for 7 years) and insecure PHP 5, released over two decades ago. Mascot [ edit ] The elePHPant, PHP's mascot The mascot of the PHP project is the elePHPant , a blue elephant with the PHP logo on its side, designed by Vincent Pontier in 1998. [ 198 ] [ 199 ] "I suddenly noticed that the letters [PHP] were forming the shape of an elephant if viewed in a 'sideways angle [ sic ] ." [ 200 ] The elePHPant is sometimes differently coloured when in plush toy form. [ 201 ] Many variations of this physical mascot have been made over the years. Only the elePHPants based on the original design by Vincent Pontier are considered official by the community. [ 202 ] These are collectable and some of them are extremely rare. [ 203 ] Syntax [ edit ] Main article: PHP syntax and semantics A "Hello, World" application in PHP 7.4 running on its built-in development server The following "Hello, World!" program is written in PHP code embedded in an HTML document: <!DOCTYPE html> < html > < head > < title > PHP "Hello, World!" program </ title > </ head > < body > < p > <? = 'Hello, World!' ?> </ p > </ body > </ html > The PHP interpreter only executes PHP code within its delimiters . Anything outside its delimiters is not processed by PHP, although the non-PHP text can still be subject to control structures described in PHP code. <?php is used to open and ?> to close PHP sections. A shorthand <?= exists, which is a shorthand for <?php echo . [ 15 ] : 22–23, 46 The shortened form <? also exists, which makes script files less portable since support can be disabled in the local PHP configuration. The shortened form is discouraged by the PHP Group for this reason. [ 204 ] [ 205 ] Conversely, there is no recommendation against the echo short tag <?= . [ 206 ] Prior to PHP 5.4.0, the short syntax for echo only works with the short_open_tag configuration setting enabled, while for PHP 5.4.0 and later it is always available. [ 207 ] [ 208 ] [ 204 ] The purpose of delimiters is to separate PHP code from non-PHP content, such as JavaScript code or HTML markup. [ 209 ] The first form of delimiters, <?php and ?> , in XHTML and other XML documents, creates correctly formed XML processing instructions. [ 210 ] This means that the resulting mixture of PHP code and other markup in the server-side file is itself well-formed XML. Variables are prefixed with a dollar symbol , and a type does not need to be specified in advance. PHP 5 introduced type declarations that allow functions to force their parameters to be objects of a specific class, arrays, interfaces or callback functions . Before PHP 7, type declarations could not be used with scalar types such as integers or strings. [ 66 ] Below is an example of how PHP variables are declared and initialized. <?php $name = 'John' ; // variable of string type being declared and initialized $age = 18 ; // variable of integer type being declared and initialized $height = 5.3 ; // variable of double type being declared and initialized echo $name . ' is ' . $height . "m tall \n " ; // concatenating variables and strings echo " $name is $age years old." ; // interpolating variables to string ?> Unlike function and class names, variable names are case-sensitive. Both double-quoted "" and heredoc strings provide the ability to interpolate a variable's value into the string. [ 211 ] PHP treats newlines as whitespace in the manner of a free-form language , and statements are terminated by a semicolon. [ 212 ] PHP has three types of comments : /* */ marks block and inline comments; // or # are used for one-line comments. The echo statement is one of several keywords PHP provides to output text. [ 15 ] : 24–26 In terms of keywords and language syntax, PHP is similar to C-style syntax. if conditions, for and while loops and function returns are similar in syntax to languages such as C, C++, C#, Java and Perl. [ 213 ] [ 214 ] [ 215 ] Data types [ edit ] PHP is loosely typed . It stores integers in a platform-dependent range, either as a 32, 64 or 128-bit signed integer equivalent to the C-language long type . Unsigned integers are converted to signed values in certain situations, which is different behaviour to many other programming languages. [ 216 ] Integer variables can be assigned using decimal (positive and negative), octal , hexadecimal , and binary notations. [ 217 ] Floating-point numbers are also stored in a platform-specific range. They can be specified using floating-point notation, or two forms of scientific notation . [ 218 ] PHP has a native Boolean type that is similar to the native Boolean types in Java and C++ . Using the Boolean type conversion rules, non-zero values are interpreted as true and zero as false, as in Perl and C++. [ 218 ] The null data type represents a variable that has no value; NULL is the only allowed value for this data type. [ 218 ] Variables of the "resource" type represent references to resources from external sources. These are typically created by functions from a particular extension, and can only be processed by functions from the same extension; examples include file, image, and database resources. [ 218 ] Arrays can contain elements of any type that PHP can handle, including resources, objects, and even other arrays. Order is preserved in lists of values and in hashes with both keys and values, and the two can be intermingled. [ 218 ] PHP also supports strings , which can be used with single quotes, double quotes, nowdoc or heredoc syntax. [ 219 ] The Standard PHP Library (SPL) attempts to solve standard problems and implements efficient data access interfaces and classes. [ 220 ] Functions [ edit ] PHP defines a large array of functions in the core language and many are also available in various extensions; these functions are well documented online PHP documentation. [ 221 ] However, the built-in library has a wide variety of naming conventions and associated inconsistencies, as described under history above. Custom functions may be defined by the developer: function myAge ( int $birthYear ) : string { // calculate the age by subtracting the birth year from the current year. $yearsOld = date ( 'Y' ) - $birthYear ; // return the age in a descriptive string. return $yearsOld . ( $yearsOld == 1 ? ' year' : ' years' ); } echo 'I am currently ' . myAge ( 1995 ) . ' old.' ; As of 2026 , the output of the above sample program is "I am currently 31 years old." In lieu of function pointers , functions in PHP can be referenced by a string containing their name. In this manner, normal PHP functions can be used, for example, as callbacks or within function tables . [ 222 ] User-defined functions may be created at any time without being prototyped . [ 221 ] [ 222 ] Functions may be defined inside code blocks, permitting a run-time decision as to whether or not a function should be defined. There is a function_exists function that determines whether a function with a given name has already been defined. Function calls must use parentheses, with the exception of zero-argument class constructor functions called with the PHP operator new , in which case parentheses are optional. [ 223 ] Since PHP 4.0.1 create_function() , a thin wrapper around eval() , allowed normal PHP functions to be created during program execution; it was deprecated in PHP 7.2 and removed in PHP 8.0 [ 224 ] in favor of syntax for anonymous functions or " closures " that can capture variables from the surrounding scope, [ 225 ] which was added in PHP 5.3. Shorthand arrow syntax was added in PHP 7.4: [ 226 ] function getAdder ( $x ) { return fn ( $y ) => $x + $y ; } $adder = getAdder ( 8 ); echo $adder ( 2 ); // prints "10" In the example above, getAdder() function creates a closure using passed argument $x , which takes an additional argument $y , and returns the created closure to the caller. Such a function is a first-class object, meaning that it can be stored in a variable, passed as a parameter to other functions, etc. [ 227 ] Unusually for a dynamically typed language, PHP supports type declarations on function parameters, which are enforced at runtime. This has been supported for classes and interfaces since PHP 5.0, for arrays since PHP 5.1, for "callables" since PHP 5.4, and scalar (integer, float, string and boolean) types since PHP 7.0. [ 66 ] PHP 7.0 also has type declarations for function return types, expressed by placing the type name after the list of parameters, preceded by a colon. [ 64 ] For example, the getAdder function from the earlier example could be annotated with types like so in PHP 7: function getAdder ( int $x ) : Closure { return fn ( int $y ) : int => $x + $y ; } $adder = getAdder ( 8 ); echo $adder ( 2 ); // prints "10" echo $adder ( null ); // throws an exception because an incorrect type was passed $adder = getAdder ([]); // would also throw an exception By default, scalar type declarations follow weak typing principles. So, for example, if a parameter's type is int , PHP would allow not only integers, but also convertible numeric strings, floats or Booleans to be passed to that function, and would convert them. [ 66 ] However, PHP 7 has a "strict typing" mode which, when used, disallows such conversions for function calls and returns within a file. [ 66 ] PHP objects [ edit ] Basic object-oriented programming functionality was added in PHP 3 and improved in PHP 4. [ 14 ] This allowed for PHP to gain further abstraction, making creative tasks easier for programmers using the language. Object handling was completely rewritten for PHP 5, expanding the feature set and enhancing performance. [ 228 ] In previous versions of PHP, objects were handled like value types . [ 228 ] The drawback of this method was that code had to make heavy use of PHP's "reference" variables if it wanted to modify an object it was passed rather than creating a copy of it. In the new approach, objects are referenced by handle , and not by value. [ 229 ] PHP 5 introduced private and protected member variables and methods, along with abstract classes , final classes , abstract methods , and final methods . It also introduced a standard way of declaring constructors and destructors , similar to that of other object-oriented languages such as C++ , and a standard exception handling model. Furthermore, PHP 5 added interfaces and allowed for multiple interfaces to be implemented. There are special interfaces that allow objects to interact with the runtime system. Objects implementing ArrayAccess can be used with array syntax and objects implementing Iterator or IteratorAggregate can be used with the foreach language construct . There is no virtual table feature in the engine, so static variables are bound with a name instead of a reference at compile time. [ 230 ] If the developer creates a copy of an object using the reserved word clone , the Zend engine will check whether a __clone() method has been defined. If not, it will call a default __clone() which will copy the object's properties. If a __clone() method is defined, then it will be responsible for setting the necessary properties in the created object. For convenience, the engine will supply a function that imports the properties of the source object, so the programmer can start with a by-value replica of the source object and only override properties that need to be changed. [ 231 ] The visibility of PHP properties and methods is defined using the keywords public , private , and protected . The default is public, if only var is used; var is a synonym for public . Items declared public can be accessed everywhere. protected limits access to inherited classes (and to the class that defines the item). private limits visibility only to the class that defines the item. [ 232 ] Objects of the same type have access to each other's private and protected members even though they are not the same instance. [ 233 ] Example [ edit ] The following is a basic example of object-oriented programming in PHP 8: <?php abstract class User { protected string $name ; public function __construct ( string $name ) { // make first letter uppercase and the rest lowercase $this -> name = ucfirst ( strtolower ( $name )); } public function greet () : string { return "Hello, my name is " . $this -> name ; } abstract public function job () : string ; } class Student extends User { public function __construct ( string $name , private string $course ) { parent :: __construct ( $name ); } public function job () : string { return "I learn " . $this -> course ; } } class Teacher extends User { public function __construct ( string $name , private array $teachingCourses ) { parent :: __construct ( $name ); } public function job () : string { return "I teach " . implode ( ", " , $this -> teachingCourses ); } } $students = [ new Student ( "Alice" , "Computer Science" ), new Student ( "Bob" , "Computer Science" ), new Student ( "Charlie" , "Business Studies" ), ]; $teachers = [ new Teacher ( "Dan" , [ "Computer Science" , "Information Security" ]), new Teacher ( "Erin" , [ "Computer Science" , "3D Graphics Programming" ]), new Teacher ( "Frankie" , [ "Online Marketing" , "Business Studies" , "E-commerce" ]), ]; foreach ([ $students , $teachers ] as $users ) { echo $users [ 0 ] :: class . "s: \n " ; array_walk ( $users , function ( User $user ) { echo " { $user -> greet () } , { $user -> job () } \n " ; }); } This program outputs the following: Students: Hello, my name is Alice, I learn Computer Science Hello, my name is Bob, I learn Computer Science Hello, my name is Charlie, I learn Business Studies Teachers: Hello, my name is Dan, I teach Computer Science, Information Security Hello, my name is Erin, I teach Computer Science, 3D Graphics Programming Hello, my name is Frankie, I teach Online Marketing, Business Studies, E-commerce Implementations [ edit ] The only complete PHP implementation is the original, known simply as PHP. It is the most widely used and is powered by the Zend Engine . To disambiguate it from other implementations, it is sometimes unofficially called "Zend PHP". The Zend Engine compiles PHP source code on-the-fly into an internal format that it can execute, thus it works as an interpreter . [ 234 ] [ 235 ] It is also the "reference implementation" of PHP, as PHP has no formal specification, and so the semantics of Zend PHP define the semantics of PHP. Due to the complex and nuanced semantics of PHP, defined by how Zend works, it is difficult for competing implementations to offer complete compatibility. [ 236 ] PHP's single-request-per-script-execution model, and the fact that the Zend Engine is an interpreter, leads to inefficiency; as a result, various products have been developed to help improve PHP performance. To speed up execution time and not have to compile the PHP source code every time the web page is accessed, PHP scripts can also be deployed in the PHP engine's internal format by using an opcode cache, which works by caching the compiled form of a PHP script (opcodes) in shared memory to avoid the overhead of parsing and compiling the code every time the script runs. An opcode cache, Zend Opcache , is built into PHP since version 5.5. [ 237 ] Another example of a widely used opcode cache is the Alternative PHP Cache (APC), which is available as a PECL extension. [ 238 ] While Zend PHP is still the most popular implementation, several other implementations have been developed. Some of these are compilers or support JIT compilation , and hence offer performance benefits over Zend PHP at the expense of lacking full PHP compatibility. [ citation needed ] Alternative implementations include the following: HHVM (HipHop Virtual Machine) – developed at Facebook and available as open source, it converts PHP code into a high-level bytecode (commonly known as an intermediate language ), which is then translated into x86-64 machine code dynamically at runtime by a just-in-time (JIT) compiler, resulting in up to 6× performance improvements. [ 239 ] However, since version 7.2 Zend has outperformed HHVM, [ 240 ] and HHVM 3.24 is the last version to officially support PHP. [ 241 ] HipHop – developed at Facebook and available as open source, it transforms the PHP scripts into C++ code and then compiles the resulting code, reducing the server load up to 50%. In early 2013, Facebook deprecated it in favour of HHVM due to multiple reasons, including deployment difficulties and lack of support for the whole PHP language, including the create_function() and eval() constructs. [ 242 ] Parrot – a virtual machine designed to run dynamic languages efficiently; the cross-translator Pipp transforms the PHP source code into the Parrot intermediate representation , which is then translated into the Parrot's bytecode and executed by the virtual machine. PeachPie – a second-generation compiler to . NET Common Intermediate Language (CIL) bytecode, built on the Roslyn platform; successor of Phalanger, sharing several architectural components. Phalanger – compiles PHP into .Net Common Intermediate Language bytecode; predecessor of PeachPie. Quercus – compiles PHP into Java bytecode . Licensing [ edit ] Main article: PHP License PHP is free software released under the PHP License , which is equivalent to the 3-clause BSD license . [ 243 ] Versions prior to 8.6 were released under a more restrictive license, which stipulates that: [ 244 ] Products derived from this software may not be called "PHP", nor may "PHP" appear in their name, without prior written permission from group@php.net. You may indicate that your software works in conjunction with PHP by saying " Foo for PHP" instead of calling it "PHP Foo" or "phpfoo". This restriction on the use of "PHP" made the PHP License incompatible with the GNU General Public License (GPL), while the Zend License was incompatible due to an advertising clause similar to that of the original BSD license . [ 245 ] Development and community [ edit ] See also: List of PHP software and tools PHP includes various free and open-source libraries in its source distribution or uses them in resulting PHP binary builds. PHP is fundamentally an Internet-aware system with built-in modules for accessing File Transfer Protocol (FTP) servers and many database servers, including PostgreSQL , MySQL , Microsoft SQL Server and SQLite (which is an embedded database), LDAP servers, and others. Numerous functions are familiar to C programmers, such as those in the stdio family, are available in standard PHP builds. [ 246 ] PHP allows developers to write extensions in C to add functionality to the PHP language. PHP extensions can be compiled statically into PHP or loaded dynamically at runtime. Numerous extensions have been written to add support for the Windows API , process management on Unix-like operating systems , multibyte strings ( Unicode ), cURL , and several popular compression formats . Other PHP features made available through extensions include integration with Internet Relay Chat (IRC), dynamic generation of images and Adobe Flash content, PHP Data Objects (PDO) as an abstraction layer used for accessing databases, [ 247 ] [ 248 ] [ 249 ] [ 250 ] [ 251 ] [ 252 ] [ 253 ] [ excessive citations ] and even speech synthesis . Some of the language's core functions, such as those dealing with strings and arrays, are also implemented as extensions. [ 254 ] The PHP Extension Community Library (PECL) project is a repository for extensions to the PHP language. [ 255 ] Most of the community focuses on web development, and PHP running server side (though also serving JavaScript for the client side), and some exceptional uses are for e.g. standalone graphical applications (with PHP-GTK unmaintained now for over a decade), [ 256 ] and even drone control. [ 257 ] Some other projects, such as Zephir , provide the ability for PHP extensions to be created in a high-level language and compiled into native PHP extensions. Such an approach, instead of writing PHP extensions directly in C, simplifies the development of extensions and reduces the time required for programming and testing. [ 258 ] By December 2018 the PHP Group consisted of ten people: Thies C. Arntzen , Stig Bakken , Shane Caraveo , Andi Gutmans , Rasmus Lerdorf , Sam Ruby , Sascha Schumann , Zeev Suraski , Jim Winstead , and Andrei Zmievski . [ 259 ] Zend Technologies provides a PHP Certification based on PHP 8 [ 260 ] exam (and previously based on PHP 7 and 5.5) for programmers to become certified PHP developers. The PHP Foundation [ edit ] PHP Formation 22 November 2021 ; 4 years ago ( 2021-11-22 ) Founder Automattic , Laravel , Acquia, Zend , Private Packagist, Symfony , Craft CMS, Tideways, PrestaShop , JetBrains [ 261 ] Website thephp .foundation On 26 November 2021, the JetBrains blog announced the creation of The PHP Foundation, which will sponsor the design and development of PHP. [ 262 ] Year Commits Reviews RFCs 2022 [ 263 ] 683 283 8 2023 [ 264 ] 784 702 17 2024 [ 265 ] 1976 1278 13 The foundation hires "Core Developers" to work on the PHP language's core repository. Roman Pronskiy, a member of the foundation's board, said that they aim to pay "market salaries" to developers. [ 266 ] The response to the foundation has been largely positive. [ 267 ] [ 268 ] Germany's Sovereign Tech Fund provided more than 200,000 Euros to support the PHP Foundation. [ 269 ] As of 2026 [ update ] , the foundation employed 13 full-time and part-time engineers, as reported by The Guardian . [ 270 ] Installation and configuration [ edit ] Example output of the phpinfo() function in PHP 7.1 There are two primary ways for adding support for PHP to a web server—as a native web server module, or as a CGI executable. PHP has a direct module interface called server application programming interface (SAPI), which is supported by many web servers including Apache HTTP Server , Microsoft IIS , Caddy (through FrankenPHP) and iPlanet Web Server . Some other web servers, such as OmniHTTPd, support the Internet Server Application Programming Interface (ISAPI), which is Microsoft 's web server module interface. If PHP has no module support for a web server, it can always be used as a Common Gateway Interface (CGI) or FastCGI processor; in that case, the web server is configured to use PHP's CGI executable to process all requests to PHP files. [ 271 ] PHP-FPM (FastCGI Process Manager) is an alternative FastCGI implementation for PHP, bundled with the official PHP distribution since version 5.3.3. [ 272 ] When compared to the older FastCGI implementation, it contains some additional features, mostly useful for heavily loaded web servers. [ 273 ] When using PHP for command-line scripting, a PHP command-line interface (CLI) executable is needed. PHP supports a CLI server application programming interface (SAPI) since PHP 4.3.0. [ 274 ] The main focus of this SAPI is developing shell applications using PHP. There are quite a few differences between the CLI SAPI and other SAPIs, although they do share many of the same behaviours. [ 275 ] PHP has a direct module interface called SAPI for different web servers; [ 276 ] in case of PHP 5 and Apache 2.0 on Windows, it is provided in form of a DLL file called php5apache2.dll , [ 277 ] which is a module that, among other functions, provides an interface between PHP and the web server, implemented in a form that the server understands. This form is what is known as a SAPI. [ citation needed ] There are different kinds of SAPIs for various web server extensions. For example, in addition to those listed above, other SAPIs for the PHP language include the Common Gateway Interface and command-line interface. [ 276 ] [ 274 ] PHP can also be used for writing desktop graphical user interface (GUI) applications, by using the "PHP Desktop" . GitHub . or discontinued PHP-GTK extension. PHP-GTK is not included in the official PHP distribution, [ 271 ] and as an extension, it can be used only with PHP versions 5.1.0 and newer. The most common way of installing PHP-GTK is by compiling it from the source code. [ 278 ] When PHP is installed and used in cloud environments, software development kits (SDKs) are provided for using cloud-specific features. [ 279 ] For example: Amazon Web Services provides the AWS SDK for PHP. [ 280 ] Microsoft Azure can be used with the Windows Azure SDK for PHP. [ 281 ] Numerous configuration options are supported, affecting both core PHP features and extensions. [ 282 ] [ 283 ] Configuration file php.ini is searched for in different locations, depending on the way PHP is used. [ 284 ] The configuration file is split into various sections, [ 285 ] while some of the configuration options can be also set within the web server configuration. [ 286 ] Use [ edit ] A broad overview of the LAMP software bundle, displayed here together with Squid PHP is a general-purpose scripting language that is especially suited to server-side web development , in which case PHP generally runs on a web server . Any PHP code in a requested file is executed by the PHP runtime, usually to create dynamic web page content or dynamic images used

The strike targeted a fuel depot that was reportedly used by the Rapid Support Forces (RSF), although other parts of the market were also struck, resulting in its complete destruction. A Sudanese official initially said that the strikes targeted fuel tankers that were supplying the RSF, claiming that the casualties were members of the militia and fuel smugglers. The SAF later denied involvement in the attack. Background [ edit ] See also: Abyei status referendum Since April 2023, a civil war has been fought between the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) and the Rapid Support Forces (RSF), in which drones have become increasingly used. A day before the attack, an alleged SAF drone strike killed over 150 people in West Kordofan , while an RSF drone attack near the Khartoum International Airport killed four the following day. [ 2 ] [ 3 ] The Amiet Common Market, which serves the Ngok Dinka and Messiria people , [ 4 ] is located 10 kilometres (6.2 mi) from the town of Abyei . [ 2 ] Ownership of the oil-rich Abyei region, which borders Kordofan , has been disputed by Sudan and South Sudan since the latter's independence in 2011. The United Nations Interim Security Force for Abyei (UNISFA) warned in May 2026 that the RSF was active in Abyei, putting civilians at risk, although the territory's caretaker minister of information has denied the militia's presence. The fuel depot targeted in the strikes has allegedly been used by the RSF in the past. [ 3 ] Airstrike [ edit ] At around 11:30 CAT on 19 October, a fuel depot in the northern part of the Amiet Common Market was struck by seven munitions allegedly launched by SAF drones, according to Abyei interim minister of information Yohana Akol Ngor . [ 4 ] The Abyei Special Administrative Area said that 22 munitions were launched into the crowded market. [ 5 ] The first strike hit a tractor-trailer carrying 26 people, causing many casualties. [ 6 ] Further strikes hit different parts of the market, including its center, south, and its northern gate, igniting a fire and reportedly destroying the entire market and an estimated 500 shops. [ 5 ] [ 7 ] [ 8 ] BBC News verified videos showing major damage in the northeast part of the market, where several buildings were set ablaze; two large fires were also seen rising from buildings in the part of the market near the fuel depot. The fire was still burning the following day. [ 2 ] [ 9 ] [ 3 ] Trucks were also destroyed in the attack, some of which had their tires melted. [ 10 ] [ 11 ] The death toll was initially reported as 73, although Yohana Akol Ngor announced a day later that it had risen to 153. [ 3 ] It was later reported that the death toll was over 220, with 153 victims being buried in one mass grave and 73 in a second. [ 6 ] At least 30 of the deceased had succumbed to their injuries after the attack. [ 12 ] Among the dead were women, children, merchants, Ngor Dinka people, South Sudanese nationals, and Sudanese refugees . [ 13 ] At least four Somalis were also killed. Some of the bodies were burned beyond recognition; [ 7 ] recovery efforts were also hampered by the fire. [ 14 ] The United Nations added that many others were missing, with the death toll expected to rise. [ 15 ] Over 8,000 people were internally displaced in the attack, some of whom sought shelter under trees. [ 6 ] More than 20 wounded victims were treated by Médecins Sans Frontières at Ameth Bek Hospital , where several were in critical condition. [ 9 ] UNISFA dispatched medical teams and firefighting equipment to evacuate the wounded and contain the fire. [ 15 ] On 22 October, UNISFA announced that it had extinguished the fires, while confirming a death toll of at least 80, in addition to 27 others injured. [ 16 ] Aftermath [ edit ] South Sudanese president Salva Kiir condemned the attack, with his government summoning Sudan's ambassador, Isam Mohamed Hassan Karrar , in protest. [ 17 ] [ 18 ] Residents in Abyei participated in mass protests on the streets to condemn the attack, which they blamed on the SAF. [ 19 ] United Nations secretary-general António Guterres and African Union Commission chairman Mahamoud Ali Youssouf condemned the attack. [ 20 ] [ 21 ] The RSF-led Government of Peace and Unity submitted an official complaint to the UN Independent International Fact-Finding Mission on Sudan, claiming that the attack violated international law . [ 22 ] A senior Sudanese official confirmed that strikes by the army targeted fuel tankers that came from South Sudan, claiming that they were being sent to the RSF. He said the casualties were RSF members and fuel smugglers but proferred no evidence. [ 9 ] The SAF later denied involvement in the attack, likening it to attrocities committed by the RSF. The Sudanese foreign ministry offered condolences to the victims' families. [ 23 ] The Abyei Joint Oversight Committee, led by Sudan, called for a UNIFSA investigation into the attack. [ 24 ] The closure of the Amiet market, which served as Abyei's main outlet for food, fuel, and medicine, led to a deterioration in living conditions, with many merchants losing their jobs.
