Penza Oblast mobilisation Drone incursions into the Baltic states and Finland Drone incidents in Romania September 2026 1 September Apartment building in Kyiv after the attack Ukrainian drones attacked and damaged port infrastructure at Ust-Luga . The regional governor confirmed a fire at the port while claiming 38 drones had been shot down. [ 1 ] Overnight Russian strikes killed 12 people, including six Ukrainian Railways employees, and injured 21 others in Kyiv and the surrounding area. [ 2 ] President Zelenskyy warned "airlines, insurers, and foreign governments" to avoid Russian airspace as it "will be de facto closed" by Ukrainian drones. President Putin called such actions "state terrorism". [ 3 ] 2 September The Proton-PM facility near Perm caught fire. [ 4 ] A shootout broke out between units of the SBU and HUR in Kyiv. Three HUR officers were wounded during the firefight, two seriously, between both services involving the deputy head of the Russian Volunteer Corps , Stepan Kaplunov. The HUR accused the SBU of kidnapping Kaplunov, while the SBU accused Kaplunov of working with the FSB. President Zelenskyy subsequently fired SBU official Oleh Khramov , head of the SBU's department for the protection of state secrets. [ 5 ] Some 27 flights to and from Moscow were cancelled by various international airlines due to Ukrainian threats to Russian airspace over the capital. [ 6 ] 3 September The commander of the 22nd Guards Heavy Bomber Aviation Division , Major General Nikolai Varpakhovich, was shot near the village of Probuzhdenie, near Engels-2 air base . Varpakhovich was shot twice, once in the face and once in the torso. [ 7 ] A Moldovan national accused of carrying out the attack was subsequently arrested by the FSB in Astrakhan Oblast . [ 8 ] Ukrainian naval drones attacked Sochi , with explosions and smoke being reported over the port. Nine oil depots were destroyed, while the Russian vessel Nefrit was struck. A Ka-52 and an Mi-28 were destroyed while an Mi-8 was damaged at Sochi International Airport , also damaged were two radars and an S-300 missile system. [ 9 ] [ 10 ] The PETRUS plant in Noginsk was set on fire by Ukrainian drones. [ 11 ] 4 September Headquarters of Security Service of Ukraine after the attack A Russian drone hit the headquarters of the SBU in Kyiv, injuring 12 people. [ 12 ] Zelenskyy said that the attack was aimed at assassinating SBU chief Oleksandr Poklad . [ 13 ] Attacks were also carried out on two vessels in Odesa Oblast . [ 14 ] In Sterlitamak , the Sterlitamak Petrochemical Plant and the Avangard Federal State Enterprise were struck by Ukrainian drones. At least 12 FP-1 drones were used in the attack. Both facilities produce explosives, synthetic rubber and aviation fuel, among other military products. [ 15 ] The HUR struck a K-300P Bastion-P missile system in Crimea that was capable of firing Zircon and Onyx missiles . [ 16 ] 5 September President Zelenskyy ordered a halt to attacks on Moscow from 5 to 8 September to allow U.S. envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner to visit Kyiv and then Moscow for peace talks. Russian attacks killed four people and injured five others in Dnipropetrovsk Oblast . [ 17 ] [ 18 ] [ 19 ] President Putin ordered a halt to attacks on Kyiv, for three days starting from midnight on 6 September to allow US peace envoys to visit Kyiv and Moscow for talks. [ 20 ] An explosion in Simferopol killed Anatoly Chernyshov, a pro-Russian fundraiser. He was posthumously awarded the Order of Courage by President Putin. [ 21 ] 6 September The Lady Maria , a Russian-flagged sanctioned tanker, was struck 12 times near Sicily by Ukrainian drones launched from Libya. The vessel was travelling from Oran to Syria with suspected Iranian weapons on board. [ 22 ] The Ryazan oil refinery was set ablaze by Ukrainian drones, while explosions and firing from air defences were reported in Bataysk . [ 23 ] 7 September Ukrainian drones struck oil refineries in Ryazan and Perm Oblasts and Tatarstan , with smoke and/or fires being at all three locations. [ 24 ] Ukrainian drones struck the Taganrog-Central air base , striking an Mi-35 and an Mi-8 . [ 25 ] Two Russian Su-35Ss collided over Kursk Oblast . One pilot was killed, the second survived. [ 26 ] 8 September Train in Sumy Oblast after drone strike on 8 September Two people were killed in Russian airstrikes on Kyiv. [ 27 ] Ukrainian drones attacked Saratov Oil Refinery, residents reported explosions and a fire. [ 28 ] The EU approved the use of a loan for Ukraine to purchase 1,000 Patriot missiles . [ 29 ] The ISW reported that a Ukrainian brigade commander operating in the Orikhiv direction claimed that the Russians had formed 120 assault groups, totaling "roughly" 150,000 personnel, to support offensive operations against the city. [ 30 ] 9 September Checkpoint on the Ukrainian-Moldovan border in Odesa Oblast after drone strike on 9 September The Romanian Intelligence Service detained a Russian national suspected of trying to sabotage a Ukrainian aircraft in Romania. [ 31 ] Ukrainian drones struck the naval base at Novorossiysk , with fires being reported at the seaport's fuel oil terminal and naval base. [ 32 ] Four people were killed in the attack. [ 33 ] The Russian frigate Admiral Essen was struck by a Neptune missile , starting a fire on the ship’s superstructure. [ 34 ] An Su-33 and an Mi-8 were also destroyed by Ukrainian drones. [ 35 ] [ 36 ] Drones also attacked the Purovsky Gas Condensate Processing Plant, 3,200 km (2,000 mi) from the Ukrainian border, a record for FP-1 drones. Fires were reported at facility along with smoke, to avoid an explosion the plant released excess gas through the flare stacks. [ 37 ] A Ukrainian naval drone struck Sochi , setting fire to the port embankment and injuring eight people. A concert by Tatiana Bulanova was evacuated. [ 38 ] German defence minister Boris Pistorius said that Germany would transfer PAC2 missiles from Bundeswehr stocks to Ukraine. [ 39 ] Norwegian prime minister Jonas Gahr Støre announced that President Zelenskyy’s aircraft was nearly struck by an UAV while taking off from Moldova the day before. [ 40 ] 10 September Aftermath of the attack on Dnipro Five people were killed in a Russian airstrike on a mall in Pavlohrad . [ 41 ] Two people were killed in an attack on an American oil extraction plant in Dnipro . [ 42 ] Ukrainian drones struck Makhachkala , with reports of fires raging near the city’s port with the Caspian Sea . [ 43 ] One person was killed in a separate attack on Borisoglebsk , Voronezh Oblast . [ 44 ] Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney stated that Canada was supplying a $350 Million CAD aid package to Ukraine in order to bolster Ukrainian air defenses. [ 45 ] 11 September Ambulance in Yasnohirka, Donetsk Oblast after Russian drone strike on 11 September A Russian airstrike on Odesa Oblast destroyed the family apartment of tennis player Dayana Yastremska and left 37 injured and two missing across the region. [ 46 ] Ukrainian drones struck an Ozon warehouse and an oil refinery, both in Saratov . The Ozon facility ceased operations due to the resulting fire. [ 47 ] Ukrainian FP-5 Flamingo missiles struck the Volgogradpromproekt in Volgograd . The company has been sanctioned by the US since 2023, and manufactures ferrocene which is "used as a catalyst and combustion-rate modifier for composite solid rocket propellants." [ 48 ] The strike destroyed a 20 m × 15 m (66 ft × 49 ft) section of the plant’s main workshop. [ 49 ] 12 September Apartment building in Odesa after attack on 12 September Ukrainian drones attacked a strategic chemical plant in Tolyatti and an airfield and automobile plant in Taganrog . A tank at the automobile plant in Taganrog caught fire and fires were reported at the airfield. [ 50 ] A Ukrainian naval drone destroyed a Russian naval drone in the Black Sea, which the Ukrainian Navy described as the "This is the first-ever battle between unmanned naval boats". [ 51 ] A Ukrainian aerial drone struck the Russian tanker Armada Leader near Sochi . The vessel was escorted by a helicopter that engaged the drone with gunfire. [ 52 ] According to the ISW, HUR director Lieutenant General Oleh Ivashchenko claimed in an interview that Russian generals have asked President Putin to mobilize 800,000 additional troops after the 2026 Russian legislative election , "likely to sustain and enable Russian offensive operations in the face of enormous Russian casualty rates". He claimed that Russia's daily casualty rate exceeded their recruitment rate, with "about" 60 percent of casualties being killed in action, an "extraordinarily high ratio of killed to wounded when the standard ratio in modern war is 1:3". The ISW assessed that Russia does not currently possess the training and administrative capabilities to fully mobilize 800,000 new recruits, especially if they did so during their semi-annual October conscription cycle. [ 53 ] The Ukrainian Unmanned Systems Force killed Russian Major General Anton Grunis during a raid in Horlivka . [ 54 ] 13 September Ukrainian drones struck the TANECO refinery in Nizhnekamsk and the Slavyansky oil refinery in Slavyansk-on-Kuban . [ 55 ] An unknown object flew from Belarus through Lithuanian airspace before reaching Kaliningrad . [ 56 ] Russian drones attacked a fuel station in Yahodyn , Volyn Oblast , [ 57 ] and a Warsaw -bound train at Yahodyn railway station . [ 58 ] [ 59 ] 14 September A German-Ukrainian woman identified as "Ilona W." was charged by German authorities with providing intelligence to the Russian Embassy in Berlin . According to the case's prosecutor, "Ilona W." had been in contact with the Russian embassy since October 2023 and tried to convince members of the German Ministry of Defense to defect to Russia. [ 60 ] HUR Chief, Lt. General Oleh Ivashchenko, claimed that Russia had recruited over 28,000 foreign mercenaries for the war in an attempt to "offset its battlefield losses". He also claimed that Russia could increase the number of North Korean troops in Kursk Oblast to 50,000, with 8,000 currently deployed there. [ 61 ] 15 September House in Sumy after drone strike on 15 September Russia struck port utilities in Odesa . [ 62 ] Ukrainian drones struck the Syzran Oil Refinery. [ 63 ] The Atlant Aero drone factory in Taganrog was struck by Neptune missiles , resulting in a roof collapse. [ 64 ] The 3rd Army Corps of Ukraine confirmed conducting counteroffensive operations called Operation Vivaldi to clear Russian forces from Dnipropetrovsk Oblast , which includes countering the Russian salient northwest of Lyman in Donetsk oblast. [ 65 ] [ 66 ] Elena Astanina, a Ukrainian woman who was head of a section of the Russian election commission , was killed in a drone strike in Zhovtneve. She is accused of orchestrating “sham” Russian referendums in Donetsk, Luhansk, Zaporizhzhia and Kherson Oblasts. [ 67 ] 16 September Poland closed two airports at Lublin and Rzeszow for 40 minutes and scrambled fighter jets due to a Russian drone attack on Ukraine. [ 68 ] Ukrainian forces retook Serednie, Donetsk Oblast. [ 66 ] 17 September Poland said it would send up to 50 million euros worth of F-16 ammunition for Ukraine to shoot down Russian drones. [ 69 ] Ukrainian drones hit two S-400 launchers in Bryansk Oblast, [ 70 ] an Su-24M at Saky airbase , [ 71 ] the Yaroslavl oil refinery, and a military airfield in Rostov Oblast. [ 72 ] Ukrainian drones attacked an airfield in Rostov , damaging a An-12 , two An-26 , and three more helicopters. Satellite imagery showed the “complete destruction” of two Mi-8 helicopters, another An-12 and a An-26 . [ 73 ] Three medical workers and the head of the medical advisory commission for Ternopil Oblast were arrested on suspicion of accepting bribes, ranging from $6,000 to $12,000, to give some 1,000 Ukrainians medical deferment certificates for military services, between 2024 and 2026. [ 74 ] Ukraine repatriated the remains of some 252 deceased citizens from Russia. [ 75 ] 18 September Administrative building in Odesa after a strike on 18 September Two people were killed in a Russian attack on Zhytomyr Oblast . [ 76 ] Moscow Mayor Sergey Sobyanin claimed that 350 Ukrainian drones were shot down, including 64 on a “terminal approach” to Moscow , while the others were shot down over Moscow Oblast . Vnukovo and Domodedovo airports cancelled flights for several hours. [ 77 ] Two Ukrainian companies completed “combat tests” of drones capable of intercepting Russian jet-powered Shahed drones . [ 78 ] Estonia's intelligence chief, Col. Ants Kiviselg, claimed that Russian losses over the past week were 11,000, averaging 1,600 personnel killed and wounded per day. He also claimed that this was the third consecutive week that Russian troop losses exceeded 10,000. [ 79 ] 19 September Shopping center in Dnipro after a strike on 19 September Three people were killed in a Russian drone attack on Kyiv Oblast. [ 80 ] The Trump administration approved a potential $2.68 billion sale of air defense equipment to Ukraine, adding that the country would finance it using a combination of European contributions and US foreign military financing . [ 81 ] The package includes S-300 Clone missiles, GAM-67 anti-aircraft missiles, plus counter drone weapons such as laser guided rockets, drone detection equipment, spare parts and software. [ 82 ] Russia claimed that it hit a Ukrainian cargo vessel and a tanker in the Black Sea region. [ 81 ] The Russian Defence Ministry claimed to have intercepted some 344 Ukrainian drones over 16 regions of Russia. In Sochi the beaches were closed due to the threat of sea drones, the local airport suspended operations while voting in the city for the 2026 Russian legislative election was suspended for the day. [ 83 ] President Trump signed into law the “ Lindsey O Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026 ”, which in part allows President Trump to impose tariffs, of up to 100 percent, on buyers of Russian oil, including China and India. [ 84 ] The SBU released footage of a new drone interceptor, which its counterintelligence unit developed, downing a Geran-5 . [ 85 ] Ukrainian drones struck targets near Kaspiysk , explosions were reported and helicopters were involved in intercepting drones. The Makhachkala Uytash Airport suspended flights. [ 86 ] Alexander Isaev, commander of the Russian Army’s 8th Artillery Regiment, was killed by a Ukrainian drone strike. He was accused of previous war crimes while serving in Ukraine. [ 87 ] 20 September Ukraine launched at least 1,000 drones towards Russia. [ 88 ] 249 drones were reported shot down over Moscow, with the Moscow Refinery being set ablaze. In total 288 drones were claimed shot down over 12 regions, drones or drone debris killed a woman in Sofyino and injured five others. A man was killed in an unspecified region in a private home. 400 people were evacuated due to a fire at an apartment building in Ramenskoye . [ 89 ] [ 90 ] President Zelenskyy said that FP-5 Flamingo and FP-7 Pelican missiles were used during the attack. [ 91 ] 21 September Biological department of Zaporizhzhia National University after the attack One person was killed in a Russian attack on Sumy and two in attacks on Kharkiv Oblast . One person was killed in Ukrainian attack on Bryansk Oblast . [ 92 ] In the night Russian drones damaged the biological department of Zaporizhzhia National University , housed inside a building built in 1902, [ 93 ] while a separate attack damaged the building of Sumy State University . [ 94 ] 22 September Destructions in Kramatorsk after the bombing on 22 September One person was killed in a Ukrainian drone attack on Samara Oblast . [ 95 ] Seven people were killed and seven injured by a Russian glide bomb attack in Izium , Kharkiv Oblast. [ 96 ] [ 97 ] One person was killed and four injured after FPV drone attacks in Kyivskyi District, Kharkiv . A car dealership and a car were also damaged. [ 98 ] Ukrainian forces struck russian drone command posts near Novoselivka Persha and Dachne, Pokrovsk Raion , both in occupied Donetsk Oblast. A drone storage depot in occupied Volnovakha was also hit. [ 99 ] A fuel depot was hit in Kalininskyi in occupied Luhansk Oblast. Two warehouses were also hit by Hirnyk, Donetsk Oblast and Velyka Shyshovka, both in occupied Donetsk Oblast. [ 99 ] 23 September Russian forces took Markove, Donetsk Oblast. [ 100 ] Ukrainian forces retook Shandryholove, Derylove, and Seredne, all in Donetsk Oblast. [ 100 ] A state of emergency was declared in Krasnodar Krai due to Ukrainian drone attacks on transport and agricultural infrastructure. [ 101 ] President Zelenskyy said that Ukraine had transferred two North Korean prisoners to South Korean custody. They were captured by Ukrainian forces during the Kursk campaign on 11 January 2025. [ 102 ] Five people were killed and four injured in Russian attacks on Oleksandrivka, Donetsk Oblast . An apartment building was destroyed, with another 11 apartment buildings, 42 homes, and a shop being damaged. [ 103 ] [ 104 ] One person was killed and another injured in a Russian FPV drone attack in Druzhkivka . [ 105 ] One person was injured by shelling in Slatyne , [ 97 ] while another was injured in Staryi Saltiv , Kharkiv Oblast. [ 97 ] Houses, cars and apartment buildings were damaged in Izium, Kharkiv Oblast after a russian artillery attack. [ 97 ] A civilian car was damaged in Derhachi . [ 97 ] Private houses were also damaged in Bohodukhiv , as well as an apartment building in Lozova . [ 97 ] A petrol station in Shevchenkove (rural settlement) , Kharkiv Oblast caught fire due to a russian UAV attack. An administrative building in Velykyi Burluk was also damaged. [ 97 ] 24 September Ukrainian air defence intercepted sixty percent of ballistic missiles fire at Kyiv, during three waves, according to President Zelenskyy. Four Zircon missiles and three Iskander missiles were intercepted. Two were killed and eight injured. [ 106 ] The Maternity Hospital No. 2 was partially damaged. [ 107 ] The Holy Intercession Church in Podil , which was built in 1906, was also damaged. [ 108 ] An apartment building in Khmelnytskyi was damaged from falling drone debris, displacing 35 people. [ 109 ] A driver was killed in Kramatorsk when a Russian FPV drone attacked his lorry. [ 110 ] A drone entered Romanian airspace, travelling for 3–4 minutes before crashing near Solca . Two Romanian F-16s and two Spanish F-18s were scrambled, school classes in the area were cancelled and air raid alerts activated. Police later found a “small UAV”. [ 111 ] Six people were killed and 14 injured in a Russian attack on a farm in Stara Hnylytsia in Chuhuiv Raion , Kharkiv Oblast . [ 112 ] [ 113 ] 25 September House in Lozova (Kharkiv Oblast) after the attack on 25 September Ukrainian drones struck the Lukoil refinery in Perm . [ 114 ] The Iskra electronics plant in Ulyanovsk and a synthetic rubber factory in Voronezh was damaged. [ 115 ] The Novoshakhtinsk oil refinery was damaged by Ukrainian drones, with 50 drones being shot down. [ 116 ] Two people were injured and a hospital was damaged in strikes on Zaporizhzhia . [ 117 ] A vehicle operated by two foreign journalists was destroyed in Sloviansk . [ 118 ] A Russian Shahed drone attack hit an apartment building in a residential neighborhood of Kyiv, killing a child. [ 119 ] A hypermarket was attacked by drones in occupied Luhansk , causing a fire. [ 120 ] A Russian radar in occupied Semenivske, Donetsk Oblast was hit by Ukrainian strikes at night. An ammunition depot in Sievierodonetsk was also hit. [ 121 ] 26 September Russian authorities claimed that a Ukrainian drone strike killed three people in Krasnodar. Ukraine said that it struck Ilsky Oil Refinery. [ 122 ] Three lorries were damaged and three people were injured in a Russian attack in Odesa . [ 123 ] Two people were killed and three injured in a Russian guided aerial bomb attack in Sumy . [ 124 ] Ukrainian Neptune missiles , plus Ruta, Palianytsia, and Bars missile drones, struck the Azov Optical-Mechanical Plant in the Rostov region. Strikes on railway cars, carrying fuel and lubricants, were also reported. [ 125 ] President Zelenskyy said that Ukraine had reached an interception rate of fifty-five percent for Russian jet powered drones and ninety percent for piston powered drones. [ 126 ] 27 September Former Commander-in-Chief of Ukrainian Armed Forces General Oleksandr Syrskyi , claimed that Ukraine had developed an active protection system that could intercept 60-80% of fpv drones fired at Ukrainian armoured vehicles. [ 127 ] 28 September Presidium of National Academy of Sciences of Ukraine after the attack A Russian Shahed drone struck the historic building in Kyiv which houses the Presidium of National Academy of Sciences of Ukraine , killing two people and injuring six, including former Secretary of the National Security and Defence Council Volodymyr Horbulin . [ 128 ] [ 129 ] Attacks on the city injured 24 people and damaged a medical center, pharmaceutical plant and other buildings. [ 130 ] Russian strikes also killed three and injured 18 in Dnipro, killed one in Synelnykove , injured 43 in Kharkiv, injured 32 in Zaporizhzhia, and injured three in Odesa. [ 131 ] [ 132 ] Russia said that it struck a cargo ship in the Black Sea and another at port in Chornomorsk . Ukrainian attacks set three facilities ablaze in Krasnodar , while defense plants in Tula and Voronezh Oblast were targeted. [ 132 ] Ukrainian forces took Nove, Ridkodub, Katerynivka, Karpivka, and Novomykhailivka, all in Donetsk Oblast. [ 133 ] [ 134 ] 29 September A Tu-95MS crashed in the Amur region , killing the crew of eight onboard. Three of the dead, Major Andrei Lobanov, Major Andrei Gerasimov and Lieutenant Colonel Fyodor Pavlyukov, were listed by Ukrainian analysts as “participants in or organizers of missile strikes” against Ukraine. [ 135 ] 30 September The Russian Ministry of Defense claimed to have encircled and captured Dobropillya and Marine (east of Sumy). However, independent data from the Institute for the Study of War and the Ukrainian battlefield command confirmed that Ukrainian forces successfully repelled these maneuvers while maintaining firm control over both towns. [ 136 ] Ukrainian forces announced that they struck 8 Russian ballistic missile launchers, including Iskander and S-400 systems, during September. [ 137 ] October 2026 1 October Ukraine claimed 46,320 Russian casualties in September, the highest so far in 2026 and the third consecutive month where their casualties exceeded 40,000. This is a forty-six percent increase from January 2026. The ISW reported that for these losses, "Russian forces likely at best gained no ground". [ 138 ] [ 139 ] An explosion at the Krasnozavodsk Chemical Plant killed at least seven workers and caused the roof of the plant to collapse. The plant was attacked previously by Ukrainian drones on 20 September 2026 as it makes ammunition for Russian Geran drones. [ 140 ] President Zelenskyy announced that Ukraine used a FP-7 tactical ballistic missile in combat for the first time, at an unspecified target, with the next step being production. [ 141 ] A Russian missile shot down a Ukrainian MiG-29 , killing the pilot, Captain Marat Redvanovych Mambetov [ uk ] , over "eastern Ukraine" during a combat mission. At the time he was the flight commander of the 40th Tactical Aviation Brigade . [ 142 ] France started training Ukrainian pilots how to fly the Rafale fighter jet. [ 143 ] A Mi-8 was shot down by a Su-35S , in a friendly fire incident, over Voronezh Oblast killing all three crew onboard. The helicopter was mistaken for a drone. [ 144 ] According to information from the HUR’s I Want to Live program, HUR reported that 45,959 foreign nationals had been recruited into the Russian army as of 1 October 2026. [ 145 ] 2 October Ukrainian drones struck oil refineries in both Volgograd and Samara regions, resulting in fires at both facilities. [ 146 ] A Ukrainian Mirage 2000-5F shot down a S8000 Banderol with its onboard 30 mm DEFA 554 , in a first kill of its kind. [ 147 ] A car bomb killed the driver of a vehicle in Novomoskovsk, Russia , the driver was believed to have be involved in the war in Ukraine. [ 148 ] Spain, Belgium, and Poland have started transferring 20 mm caliber cannon shells for Ukrainian F-16s to shoot down Russian jet powered drones. [ 149 ] 3 October Ukrainian drones struck the windows and balconies of several apartment buildings in Kaluga . [ 150 ] According to Moldovan President , at least five Russian weapons entered and exploded on Moldovan territory, including Banderol missiles and drones. [ 151 ] Ukrainian strikes targeted Iskander missile launch sites in Bryansk Oblast. [ 152 ] Russian Major Alexei Karavaev, Commander of 11th Tank Regiment accused of killing Ukrainian prisoners in 2024 was killed by Ukrainian artillery. [ 153 ] Ukrainian forces took a part of forest northeast of Vovchanski Kuthory, Kharkiv Oblast. [ 154 ] Russia claimed that it took Nesternoi, Rubel Noi, and Vusakaya Yeruga, all in Kharkiv Oblast. The ISW was unable to confirm the advances. [ 155 ] 4 October German Chancellor Friedrich Merz visited Kyiv, promising €1 billion for military aid, along with €350 million for energy repairs. [ 156 ] Ukrainian drones struck the Khanskaya air base , [ 157 ] striking a Su-34, a Su-35 and aircraft refuelling facilities. [ 158 ] Russian forces struck the Pivnichnyi Bridge in Kyiv, injuring two people. [ 159 ] A Russian strike in Sumy 's Kovpakivskyi District [ uk ] killed one person and injured three others, other attacks in Sumy injured 13 people. [ 160 ] A report by the UN Human Rights Office stated that at least 15,280 Ukrainian civilians had been killed or injured during the first eight months of 2026, or 400 every week. This is a 55 percent increase from the same period in 2025. On the frontline, nearly 2,500 civilians were killed or wounded by Russian glide bombs, a 62 percent increase from 2025. [ 161 ] 5 October An automated turret, fitted with a M2 Browning machine gun and using artificial intelligence, shot down a Russian Geran-5 drone for the first time. [ 162 ] Russia tested barrage balloons as an anti-drone defence. [ 163 ] Russian drones sunk the Turkish owned ship Royad Mammadov , in the Black Sea while carrying grain from Ukraine to Italy. The captain was killed, while eleven crew members were rescued. [ 164 ] A Bulgarian tanker taking grain to Romania was also sunk with 18 crew being rescued. [ 165 ] 6 October Ambulances of Kramatorsk city hospital (Donetsk Oblast) after a strike on 6 October The SBU arrested a man accused of being recruited by the FSB, who was alleged to have set up repeater stations in Kyiv, during late September, to help guide Russian Geran-5 drones and ballistic missiles. [ 166 ] Ukraine announced that its 12 civilians escaped the Russian occupation of Oleshky , due to ongoing starvation in the city. [ 167 ] Ukrainian drones attacked the Volodarsk Linear Production and Dispatch Center, located in Konstantinovo , Moscow Oblast. Moscow Mayor Sergei Sobyanin claimed Ukraine launched 650 drones attacked the capital, with air defences intercepting 105 of them. [ 168 ] The AFRAMAX RIO, a Liberian flagged crude oil tanker, was attacked by drones near Sochi , resulting in a fire breaking out. [ 169 ] As of 16 October, the tanker was afloat but had sustained significant damage and was listing to starboard. An oil spill had spread from it, forcing booms to be installed after oil pollution was reported on the coast. [ 170 ] A Russian strike hit ambulances and a multi-storey apartment building in Kramatorsk, killing one woman and injuring four others. [ 171 ] Russia claimed that it took Samoilovka in Zaporizhzhia Oblast. [ 172 ] 7 October Apartment building in Pryluky (Chernihiv Oblast) after the strike on 7 October The Russian Ministry of Defence claimed to have intercepted 311 Ukrainian drones over 17 regions. [ 173 ] According to Ukrainian Prime Minister Serhii Koretskyi , Ukraine received a loan from the EU worth €1.2 Billion as part of the EU's Ukraine Support Loan program. [ 174 ] At least 26 people, including five children were killed in Russian strikes on Ukraine. [ 175 ] A HUR Sargan-3000 USV shot down a " Shahed type attack drone" over the Black Sea with machine guns. [ 176 ] 8 October Bus in Kramatorsk after the attack Gazprom Neftekhim Salavat , in Salavat , was attacked by Ukrainian drones, resulting in a fire. [ 177 ] Russian air defenses were active for 12 hours over 20 locations, with over 400 drones involved, with the Russian Ministry of Defense claiming 399 interceptions or suppression. [ 178 ] A 57-year-old man was killed during a Ukrainian drone attack on Podolsk , a 37-year-old woman was injured, and flights at Vnukovo, Domodedovo, and Zhukovsky airports were suspended. [ 179 ] Ukrainian forces attacked a Yandex data center and a Sasta machine-tool plant in Sasovo . A large fire reportedly caused "major disruptions" to the Yandex Cloud , including internet connection and power supplies. [ 180 ] Ukrainian FP-1 drones attacked the Omsk refinery , which is about 2,500 kilometers (1,550 miles) from occupied Ukraine. The video of the attack showed smoke, explosions, and fire. [ 181 ] At least 33 people are killed in Russian strikes that hit two passenger buses in Kramatorsk . [ 182 ] [ 183 ] South Korea recalled its ambassador to Ukraine after President Zelenskyy revealed that two captured North Korean prisoners had been transferred to South Korea. South Korea claimed it breached a confidential agreement, and while Ukraine offered an apology, it wasn’t the level they expected. [ 184 ] 9 October Redkino Experimental Chemical Plant in Tver was attacked by Ukrainian drones. It produces fuel for Kh-101 and Kh-55 cruise missiles plus other chemicals used in Russia’s aviation, aerospace, and other industrial sectors. [ 185 ] An oil depot in northern Belgorod was set on fire by Ukrainian drones. [ 186 ] The Ukhta oil refinery was also attacked by Ukrainian drones, with black smoke rising from it. [ 187 ] A Yandex data center in Kaluga was damaged by an Ukrainian drone attack. The full extent of the damage is unknown. [ 188 ] Mikhail Zvinchuk was arrested, along with his wife, Valeriya, by the Montenegrin police and the Agency for National Security officers. He founded the pro-Kremlin Rybar telegram channel . [ 189 ] President Putin’s Il-96-300PU , along with several other government Il-96s, was forced to change its flight route due to a Ukrainian drone attack. President Putin’s plane was attempting to land at Vnukovo airport in Moscow, but it was redirected to Pulkovo Airport in St. Petersburg before returning to Vnukovo after flight restrictions were lifted. [ 190 ] 10 October Apartment building in Zaporizhzhia after the strike A Russian strike hit Zaporizhzhia, killing 20 people, including three children. [ 191 ] [ 192 ] Russia claimed to have took Lukashovo and Lobanovka in the Kharkiv Oblast. [ 193 ] Two Russian ships in Azov ’s port were damaged by drones, with officials refusing to release further information. The Novoshakhtinsk Oil Refinery was set ablaze during a drone attack. [ 194 ] [ 195 ] Seven out of 12 oil storage tanks were destroyed, with the fire finally extinguished on 12 October. [ 196 ] Ukrainian drones damaged the tracks on a railway bridge in Vygonichsky District , Bryansk Oblast. Service on the Bryansk–Unecha–Gomel line was disrupted, with trains heading to Moscow either being rerouted or replaced by buses along certain sections. [ 197 ] 11 October An air defence site in Sochi was attacked by Ukrainian drones, with a fire detected on NASA’s FIRMS. [ 198 ] A Yandex data centre in Vladimir Oblast was attacked by Ukrainian drones, resulting in the complete shutdown of the facility and causing some of the company's services to become unavailable. [ 199 ] 12 October Apartment building in Kharkiv after missile strike on 12 October Ukrainian forces shot down a Geran-5 with a new jet interceptor, the second confirmed interception of a Geran-5. [ 200 ] Ukraine fired an FP-7 missile at an undisclosed target in Russia. [ 201 ] The Russians attacked a Roshen factory in Vinnytsia . [ 202 ] Two people were injured in Russian strikes in Hlukhiv , while another attack killed one woman and injured seven in Lozova . [ 203 ] [ 204 ] A Russian Smerch missile hit a house in Cherkaske, Donetsk Oblast , killing three people, including 13-year-old girl and injuring four, while another strike on Sloviansk injured a 77-year-old woman. [ 205 ] [ 206 ] Three people were killed in a Russian drone attack in Ivano-Frankivsk , [ 207 ] and four were killed in a missile attack on Kharkiv . [ 208 ] 13 October The Ukrainian Air Force claimed that up to 85% of Russian jet-powered drones was being intercepted. [ 209 ] Ukrainian forces struck an Iskander-M maintenance base in Kursk Oblast. [ 210 ] A Russian POW escaped Ukrainian custody in Kharkiv Oblast. While on the run, the Russian soldier was accused of killing five Ukrainian soldiers and one civilian. He was recaptured on 15 October. [ 211 ] 14 October Phase four of Operation Vivaldi has concluded, with some 101 square kilometers of territory claimed to have been recaptured by Ukraine and roughly 3,000 Russian losses inflicted. [ 212 ] SpaceX unilaterally restricted speeds on its Starshield terminals to 72 to 161 km/h, [ 213 ] while Starlink connectivity speeds showed signs of being throttled, directly affecting Ukrainian military drone operations. [ 214 ] Ukrainian drones set fire to a “major data centre” for Sberbank in Balakovo . [ 215 ] The trial of Ukrainian citizen Serhii Kuznetsov started in Hamburg . Prosecutors accused him of helping to blow up the Nord Stream 2 pipeline. He was charged with war crimes, attacking civilian infrastructure, and “ordering divers and an explosive expert to attack civilian infrastructure.” Meanwhile, Croatia approved the extradition to Germany of Volodymyr Zhuravlov, a second Ukrainian accused of involvement. [ 216 ] 15 October Ukrainian forces carried out an attack on Borisoglebsk air base in Russia using R-360 Neptune cruise missiles. [ 217 ] Up to six aircraft were claimed destroyed, with later satellite imagery suggesting that at least four Su-34 fighter-bomber aircraft were destroyed. [ 217 ] The Ryazan oil refinery was struck by Ukrainian drones in the first strike after Ukraine observed a three-day ceasefire. [ 218 ] In an interview on Newsmax , President Trump described Ukraine's renewed strikes on Russian energy infrastructure a 'disgrace'. [ 219 ] [ 220 ] Trump further stated that 'Zelensky is not a good guy for us to deal with', that he was 'not a big fan of Zelensky', and accused the Ukrainian president of destroying the country. [ 221 ] [ 222 ] Trump went on to disparagingly compare Zelenskyy to the 19th century American showman P. T. Barnum , and called for elections in the country. [ 223 ] 16 October Moscow, Rostov, and Vladimir regions were attacked by Ukrainian drones. Yandex 's data center in Vladimir Oblast was targeted, with loud explosions reported. The drone strikes resulted in the closure of multiple airports in Moscow, and a fire broke out in the town of Aksay . [ 224 ] About 22 airports were closed due to Ukrainian drone attacks, air defense systems were activated, and explosions were reported in various regions, including Smolensk , Tver , Tula , Ryazan , Lipetsk , Kaluga , and Nizhny Novgorod . [ 225 ] The Surgut Gas Processing Complex, located in the Khanty-Mansi Autonomous Okrug , was attacked by Ukrainian drones, resulting in a fire. [ 226 ] A series of Russian drone strikes took place in Western Ukraine. Kromberg & Schubert, a manufacturer of electrical wiring, announced the suspension of its plant following the attacks by jet-powered drones. [ 227 ] [ 228 ] The agricultural firm Ahrofrukt also reported significant damage to its facilities. [ 229 ] 17 October Two days before the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026 was to take effect, President Trump signed an executive order waiving the sanctions placed under the act against Russia, in order to facilitate a deal for Russian diesel fuel. [ 230 ] [ 231 ] White House spokeswoman Taylor Rogers stated that "Enforcing the sanctions provisions now would impede ongoing U.S. efforts to negotiate a durable and comprehensive peace agreement". [ 232 ] Secretary of state Rubio confirmed the waiver, stating that more time was necessary to analyze the effects of sanctions and tariffs on the global economy, particularly in regards to India and the Middle East. [ 233 ] [ 234 ] Secretary of state Rubio stated that Ukrainian access to SpaceX Starshield was not permitted at the present time, stating: "It's not at this moment available to Ukraine, and that's under conversation". [ 233 ] At the same time, Rubio clarified that Starlink is a commercial product, and regulated as such. At least eight people, including a 71-year-old woman were killed and 60 others were wounded in Russian strikes on Ukraine. Russian strikes on Ukrainian electrical infrastructure were reported to have cut power to more than 1 million people. [ 235 ] Wait times for customs processing at Polish-Ukrainian border crossings were reported to take up to 40 hours due to the threat of air alerts. [ 236 ] A group of drones was detected by the Romanian Air Force heading in the southwest direction approximately 120 km east of Snake Island . Two F-16s from the 53rd Fighter Squadron intercepted two drones as they entered Romanian airspace. [ 237 ] Moscow Mayor Sergey Sobyanin claimed that between 10 and 17 October 2026, some 2,730 Ukrainian drones had been neutralized heading towards the Moscow region, while some 534 drones were neutralized approaching Moscow itself, forcing Vnukovo, Domodedovo, and Zhukovsky airports to suspend operations for two days in a row. Moscow's airports had been forced to restrict operations, to varying degrees, for some six nights in a row, resulting in long passenger queues and hundreds of flight delays. [ 238 ] The Russian Ministry of Defence claimed that some 4,500 drones had been shot down over various Russian regions during the same period of time. [ 239 ] [ 240 ] According to German police, a section of the security fence at Leipzig/Halle Airport was rammed by a vehicle. The destroyed section was close to three Russian An-124 cargo planes that have been grounded by sanctions since 2022. Following the incident, police searched the grounds but did not find a vehicle or any suspects. [ 241 ] 18 October Lublin Rzeszów Juodžionys Panevėžys Polish and Baltic Airspace incidents - 18 October 2026 On the night of 17-18 October, an air alert was raised in Lithuania and Latvia, with drones detected in the vicinity of the Belarusian border moving from Poland towards Latvia, prompting the temporary suspension of flights from Kaunas Airport . [ 242 ] [ 243 ] [ 244 ] The Lithuanian National Crisis Management centre reported that an explosion had occurred, and that drone debris was found near the village of Juodžionys, Pasvalys District Municipality having possibly entered Lithuanian airspace from Poland. [ 245 ] Another drone was reported by residents in the vicinity of the city of Panevėžys . [ 245 ] Possible violations of Polish airspace in Lublin Voivodeship and Podkarpackie Voivodeship were also reported, with sightings of drones reported near the Zemborzycki Reservoir in Lublin city, as well as in Łęczna County . [ 246 ] [ 247 ] Airports in Lublin and Rzeszow were temporarily suspended. [ 248 ] A fire was reported at the oil terminal of the Port of Saint Petersburg following Ukrainian drone strikes. [ 249 ] [ 250 ] Several other facilities in the Saint Petersburg were also reportedly attacked, including a VK datacenter, [ 251 ] [ 252 ] an OZON e-commerce warehouse, [ 253 ] as well as a bridge section of the Western High-Speed Diameter . [ 254 ] Damage to apartment blocks, parked cars and electrical infrastructure was also reported. [ 255 ] [ 256 ] Prime Minister Peter Magyar said that he was prepared to allow Ukraine to transit its grain through Hungary. However, the trains must be sealed and allowed only for transit to a third country. This potentially reverses a ban on the transit of Ukrainian agricultural products put in place by former Prime Minister Viktor Orban . Attempts to ship the grain via the Black Sea have become too dangerous due to Russian drone attacks. [ 257 ] President Zelenskyy said that the United States had started sharing intelligence again with Ukraine. [ 258 ] Lithuania claimed to have foiled an arson attack on a Starlink station in the country, with authorities alleging that Russia was responsible. [ 259 ] 19 October Kyiv was attacked with ballistic missiles. No casualties were reported, but there was damage to metro stations on the left bank of the Dnipro River, railway tracks, and power infrastructure, according to Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko . According to journalists from The Kyiv Independent , unlike the previous night’s attack, a warning was sent to residents before the strike occurred, allowing them to seek shelter. [ 260 ] The Ukrainian telecommunications company DataGroup reported the destruction of its data center in Kyiv, stating that repairs or resumption of operations at the site were impossible. [ 261 ] [ 262 ] The company announced that it would continue limited operations from backup infrastructure. A Russian spacecraft, 'Kosmos 2612,' came within 26 meters of ICEYE-X36 , a US-registered satellite that provides intelligence to the Armed Forces of Ukraine . The reason for the approach is unclear. ICEYE-X36 is fitted with a synthetic aperture radar that provides images of the Earth's surface at a resolution of up to 25 cm. [ 263 ] A Russian strike in a park in Nova Vodolaga killed six people, including three children. [ 264 ] Russian-installed Luhansk governor claimed that three people were killed in a Ukrainian strike in the oblast. [ 265 ] A 41-year-old Ukrainian man was called into the Pechersk Territorial Recruitment Center on suspicion of breaching mobilization laws. He produced a pistol and fired seven times, wounding six people, two of whom are in critical condition. Three of the injured were police officers and three were military personnel. The man has been arrested. [ 266 ] 20 October A Ukrainian soldier was medically evacuated by UAV in what is called the world's first case of a soldier lifted directly from his position by a drone. A modified hexacopter —normally used for dropping cargo or munitions—was deployed because a ground rescue was too dangerous due to Russian drones. [ 267 ] The Wall Street Journal reported that Elon Musk ordered a deliberate speed cap on military-grade Starlink hardware in Ukraine. One person familiar with the matter claimed that Musk consulted with President Donald Trump and other senior administration officials prior to enforcing the restriction, despite some U.S. officials maintaining that Musk acted unilaterally. [ 268 ] Ukrainian drones attacked an oil pumping station near Michurinsk , resulting in a fire. [ 269 ] The GigaCenter datacenter, operating services for the telecommunications, cloud services and cybersecurity for GIGAGROUP, in Kyiv was destroyed following a Russian strike. [ 270 ] [ 271 ] 21 October Ukrainian drones struck energy infrastructure in Chystiakove . Blackouts were reported in Krasnoperekopsk , Crimea, following attacks on the train system. Separately, a telecommunications tower in Luhansk was attacked. [ 272 ] President Putin announced that Stephen Hubbard, a 74-year-old retired American teacher who had been imprisoned by Moscow on charges of serving as a foreign combatant for Ukraine, was released. [ 273 ] According to Ukrainian figures, Russia lost 2,250 troops killed and wounded in a single day—the highest losses for Russian forces since the full-scale war started. [ 274 ] 22 October A Ukrainian infiltration operation near Kupiansk via gas pipelines captured 30 Russians and inflicted 100 casualties. [ 275 ] Ukrainian drones struck the 75th Arsenal in Serpukhov , a facility that maintains Buk and S-300V missile systems. [ 276 ] Ukrainian drones struck Lipetsk ; fire from the drones and air defenses damaged the windows and facades of multiple residential buildings. [ 277 ] The SBU arrested a Ukrainian Navy sailor in the Mykolaiv region who had gone AWOL. Before doing so, he had posted roughly ten geotagged videos of Ukrainian military positions on TikTok. [ 278 ] 23 October Ukrainian drones struck the Federal Taxation Service data centre in Gorodets —one of the two main hubs that store and process data from Russian government registers, including centralized tax databases. [ 279 ] Ukrainian drone and balloon attacks caused the cancellation of some 340 flights in and out of Moscow's four airports: Vnukovo , Domodedovo , Sheremetyevo , and Zhukovsky . Other flights were rerouted after a fixed-wing drone crashed at Sheremetyevo Airport . [ 280 ] Ukrainian missiles, possibly Storm Shadow or Flamingo missiles , struck the Proton plant in Oryol , destroying a production workshop and potentially causing personnel casualties. [ 281 ] Denmark supplied more than 50,000 rounds of 20 mm caliber cannon ammunition to Ukraine, equipping its F-16 aircraft to intercept Russian strike drones. [ 282 ] Ukrainian forces launched a missile strike targeting the Baltimore Military Air Base in Voronezh , hitting an aircraft parking area used by Russian Su-34 bomber aircraft. Somalia On 3 September 2026, the Iran -backed Houthis launched an offensive against the Saudi -backed and UN recognized Presidential Leadership Council (PLC), the internationally recognized government of Yemen , amid the ongoing Yemeni civil war . [ 67 ] [ 44 ] Clashes began in Taiz Governorate , prompting a PLC counter-offensive against the Houthis in the Al-Jawf and Al-Bayda governorates . [ 9 ] [ 67 ] The fighting coincides with the ongoing 2026 Iran war , which has marked the deadliest fighting in Yemen since the collapse of the 2022 ceasefire. [ 68 ] The Yemeni government lost areas around the Bab al-Mandab Strait in Yemen's southwest after a swift battle over Mokha , resulting in a crisis with the entire west coast of Yemen (except for the Midi district ) falling under control of the Houthi movement, who named the operation as Operation Allah is Stronger in Might and More Severe in Punishment . [ f ] [ 69 ] [ 70 ] The counteroffensive of the PLC against the Houthis was named Operation Dawn of Yemen . [ g ] [ 71 ] [ 72 ] Background 2022 ceasefire and the Red Sea crisis Main article: Red Sea crisis The Houthis and the internationally recognized government of Yemen reached a ceasefire agreement in 2022, which largely held until the 2026 campaign. Peace talks stalled in 2023 amidst the Gaza war . [ 73 ] Starting on 19 October 2023, the Houthis began launching missiles and drones at international shipping crossing the Bab al-Mandab Strait in solidarity with Palestinians during the war in Gaza, triggering the Red Sea crisis . In response, a US -led multinational coalition launched Operation Prosperity Guardian in late 2023 to secure shipping through the Red Sea . In early 2024, the United States and the United Kingdom launched a series of airstrikes targeting Houthi missile and drone launch sites across Yemen. [ 74 ] [ 75 ] In March 2025, the United States launched a larger wave of strikes against the Houthis , after which the Houthis agreed to stop attacking U.S. vessels in the Red Sea. [ 76 ] Additionally, Israel previously launched a series of airstrikes on Houthi-controlled Yemen in response to missile attacks by the group, including a July 2024 strike on Tel Aviv that killed one person. [ 77 ] [ 78 ] Following the implementation of the Gaza peace plan in 2025, both parties briefly ceased attacks until March 2026, when the Houthis again launched missiles toward Israel in support of Iran and the Axis of Resistance , all of which were intercepted. [ 79 ] [ 80 ] 2026 Iran war and escalation Main articles: Houthis in the 2026 Iran war and Houthi blockade of Saudi Arabia On 28 February 2026, the United States and Israel launched a large-scale attack on Iran, aimed at regime change . Iran and its allied militias, including Hezbollah and the Iraqi Popular Mobilization Forces , retaliated against U.S., Israeli, and other regional countries' military and energy infrastructure with drone and missile strikes. The Houthis initially refrained from joining the fighting, breaking with the rest of the Axis of Resistance , only joining the war on 28 March. [ 81 ] When the US navy reimposed its naval blockade against Iran on 14 July 2026, the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) of Iran threatened to cut "all other export corridors that benefit the US and its allies", with a senior Houthi official warning that the group was prepared to close the Bab al-Mandab Strait . [ 82 ] On 16 July 2026, Reuters reported that Iran had asked the Houthis to be ready to close the strait should the US strike Iranian power infrastructure. Soon after the Houthis began deploying drones and missiles near the Bab al-Mandeb Strait. [ 83 ] On 13 July 2026, a Mahan Air flight carrying IRGC commanders and weapons attempted to land at Sanaa Airport , in the Houthi-controlled capital. [ 84 ] Yemeni government forces and Saudi Arabia responded by striking the airport's runway to prevent the landing. In retaliation for the strike, the Houthis declared the ceasefire with the Yemeni government and Saudi Arabia over. [ 85 ] On 20 July, the Houthis announced a naval blockade on Saudi Arabia , amid the renewed U.S. naval blockade of Iran. [ 86 ] The Houthis subsequently began striking Saudi oil tankers in the Red Sea. On 24 July, Saudi Arabia retaliated against the earlier Houthi strikes on its oil tankers by bombing Houthi targets in the port city of Hodeidah . In response, the Houthis struck the Jizan oil refinery and the port city of Yanbu in Saudi Arabia two days later. [ 87 ] Starting on 6 August, the Houthis also started striking Yemeni government forces across the country with missiles and drones, killing and injuring dozens of troops. [ 88 ] Timeline 3–9 September On 3 September, the Houthis launched what was described as a "massive offensive" in the Taiz Governorate , attempting to cut the road linking Taiz to Mokha and thus sever Taiz city from the coast and escalate the Siege of Taiz . [ 291 ] The Houthis fired several missiles at Al-Maashiq Palace in Aden while prime minister Shaya al-Zindani and other cabinet members were present; five people were killed and 16 others injured, [ 292 ] although no government officials were harmed. [ 293 ] [ 294 ] PLC forces claimed to have launched airstrikes against Houthi positions in Dhi al-Barah and Jaba'. [ 295 ] On 16 October, PLC forces claimed to have killed sixteen Houthi fighters and wounded others during clashes on the Al-Shaqab front, south of Taiz. [ 296 ] The 35th Armored Brigade reported capturing a Houthi team allegedly responsible for operating drones on the Al-Aqroudh front in the Kahlan area. [ 297 ] PLC forces repelled multiple Houthi attacks on both the Al-Shaqab and Al-Aqroudh fronts, with ongoing clashes reported. Yemeni armed forces conducted several airstrikes on Houthi positions, including at the Al-Hangar checkpoint, Maqbaba and Al-Kamil hills, [ 298 ] and targeted a Houthi tank at Ghorab School. [ 299 ] The Houthis fired two missiles at the Aden International Airport, which landed near its runway while a flight was taking off. [ 300 ] Another missile targeting Yanbu was intercepted, as were two cruise missiles over the Red Sea and three drones targeting southern Saudi Arabia and Riyadh. [ 301 ] The Chief of Staff of the 26th Infantry Brigade, Ahmed Mohammed Bahibah, died after a failed PLC infiltration attempt into the Harib district . [ 302 ] On 17 October, the SPC Ministry of Telecommunications and Information Technology reported that Saudi airstrikes that targeted telecommunications stations, towers and networks across Yemen had put up to 902 telecommunications sites and stations out of service, systematically damaging infrastructure, causing civilian casualties and depriving citizens of essential services. [ 303 ] [ 304 ] Houthi spokesperson Yahya Saree claimed to have shot down a Saudi reconnaissance aircraft in Hajjah Governorate . [ 305 ] The Houthis also said they shot down a Saudi Apache helicopter over Najran Province in Saudi Arabia. [ 306 ] On 18 October, a Saudi airstrike on a house in Sahar district killed nine people and injured 19 others. [ 307 ] Saudi Arabia also announced that an AH-6 helicopter crashed in Najran Province due to a "technical malfunction", killing two officers, while the Houthis claimed to have shot it down. [ 308 ] Clashes occurred near the Old Airport region and Madarat district in western Taiz, while a Houthi offensive against Al-Shaqab region was repelled. Houthi shelling also killed eight civilians and injured six others. [ 309 ] On 19 October, a Houthi missile attack on the PLC's al-Alam military camp in Jardan district killed 73 soldiers, injured 200, and left 14 missing. Local authorities said, three ⁠ballistic missiles hit security forces during training. [ 310 ] On 20 October, the PLC said that it conducted 744 strikes against the Houthis in the past 24 hours, "neutralizing" 200 fighters and hitting 90 combat vehicles. [ 311

Ltd. Racing colours Trainer Yoshito Yahagi Jockey Yasunari Iwata Record 7: 3–2–1 Earnings ¥ 292,056,000 [ 2 ] Major wins Tokyo Sports Hai Nisai Stakes (2011) Japanese Classic Race wins: Tokyo Yushun (2012) Deep Brillante ( Japanese : ディープブリランテ , Hepburn : Dīpu Burirante ) (8 May 2009 – 23 October 2026) was a Japanese Thoroughbred racehorse and sire . He showed very promising form in 2011 when he won both of his races including the Grade 3 Tokyo Sports Hai Nisai Stakes . In the following spring he ran prominently in several major races including the Satsuki Sho before stepping up in distance and winning the Tokyo Yushun (Japanese Derby). He was then sent to Europe where he ran poorly in the King George VI and Queen Elizabeth Stakes . [ 3 ] [ 4 ] He did not race again and was retired to stud in October 2012, where he produced several grade winning racehorses. [ 5 ] Background [ edit ] Deep Brillante was a bay horse standing 16.1 hands high [ 6 ] with two white socks bred in Japan by the Paca Paca Farm. He was from the second crop of foals sired by Deep Impact who was the Japanese Horse of the Year in 2005 and 2006, winning races including the Tokyo Yushun , Tenno Sho , Arima Kinen and Japan Cup . Deep Impact's other progeny include Gentildonna , Harp Star , Kizuna and A Shin Hikari . [ 7 ] Deep Brillante's dam Love and Bubbles was an American-bred, French-trained mare who won the Prix Chloé in 2004. She was a great-granddaughter of Bubble Company, a broodmare whose other descendants have included Bubble Gum Fellow and That's the Plenty ( Kikuka Sho ). [ 8 ] [ 9 ] As a foal Deep Brillante was offered for sale and bought for ¥ 32,550,000 by representatives of Sunday Racing Co. Ltd. He was sent into training with Yoshito Yahagi and was ridden in all of his races by Yasunari Iwata . [ 10 ] Racing career [ edit ] 2011: two-year-old season [ edit ] Deep Brillante made his racecourse debut in a contest for previously unraced horses over 1800 metres at Hanshin Racecourse on 1 October 2011 and won by five lengths from Ebony Knight and ten others. On 19 November the colt was stepped up in class for the Grade 3 Tokyo Sports Hai Nisai Stakes at Tokyo Racecourse and started 7/5 favourite ahead of fourteen opponents headed by Just A Way and Ennead. Deep Brillante took the lead 400 metres from the finish and won "comfortably" by three lengths from the 54/1 outsider Fujimasa Emperor. [ 11 ] In the JRA Awards for 2011 Deep Brillante finished third behind Alfredo and Adam's Peak in the poll to determine the champion Japanese two-year-old colt of 2011. [ 12 ] 2012: three-year-old season [ edit ] Yasunari Iwata, who rode Deep Brillante in all of his races On his 2012 debut Deep Brillante started odds-on favourite for the Grade 3 Kyodo Tsushin Hai over 1800 metres at Tokyo on 12 February. He led for most of the way but was overtaken by Gold Ship 100 metres from the finish and beaten one and three quarter lengths into second. In March he again headed the betting when he contested the Grade 2 Spring Stakes at Nakayama Racecourse . After racing in fourth he took the lead in the straight and went clear of his rivals before faltering in the closing stages and being beaten by Grandezza. Despite consecutive defeats, Yahagi kept his faith in the horse, describing him as having "tremendous potential". [ 13 ] Deep Brillante started third favourite for the Grade 1 Satsuki Sho at Nakayama on 15 April and finished third of the eighteen runners behind Gold Ship and World Ace. [ 14 ] The 79th running of the Tokyo Yushun took place over 2400 metres on firm ground at Tokyo on 27 May. World Ace headed the betting from Gold Ship with Deep Brillante third choice on 7.5/1. The other runners included Grandezza, Just A Way , Alfredo, Fenomeno and Historical ( Mainichi Hai ). In the build-up to the race the colt's groom had praised his attitude and temperament saying "He's so calm usually it's almost frightening. He doesn't need any babysitting whatsoever. He's an intelligent horse, and he always runs his heart out in races". [ 15 ] After tracking the leaders Iwata sent the colt into third approaching the final turn before taking the lead 200 metres out. In an extremely tight finish Deep Brillante held on to win by a nose from Fenomeno, with Tosen Homareboshi, World Ace, Gold Ship and Cosmo Ozora close behind. Less than two lengths covered the first six finishers. [ 16 ] [ 17 ] After the race Iwata, who was winning the race for the first time, said "Praise him not me. It was his guts that won it as he was completely empty at the finish. I have always thought he was the best horse in this generation so we trained him very hard to get a big success. We thought he was the best one and I am proud that we could prove it." [ 18 ] After his win at Tokyo, Deep Brillante's connections took the unusual decision to send the colt to England and match him against older horses in the King George VI and Queen Elizabeth Stakes at Ascot Racecourse on 21 July. He started a 20/1 outsider and was never in contention, finishing eighth of the ten runners behind the German mare Danedream . [ 3 ] Deep Brillante's retirement was announced on 26 October. [ 5 ] Yahagi commented "It's a terrible shame that the fans won't be able to see him race again. The little more than a year that I spent with this horse has been like a dream and for me he was nothing short of a treasure." [ 19 ] Racing form [ edit ] Deep Brillante had won three races in seven starts. [ 20 ] [ 14 ] [ 3 ] [ 21 ] All the races were on turf. text: Hilkka Kinnunen - Wikipedia Jump to content Search Search Hilkka Kinnunen 3 languages Suomi اردو Volapük Edit links From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia Finnish actress (1925–2026) Hilkka Kinnunen Kinnunen and her future husband in 1946 Born Hilkka Terttu Annikki Kinnunen ( 1925-03-19 ) 19 March 1925 Viipuri , Finland Died 19 October 2026 (2026-10-19) (aged 101) Helsinki , Finland Occupations Actress Operetta singer Stage director Theatre director Organizations Operettiteatteri Title Teatterineuvos Spouse Ekke Hämäläinen ​ ​ ( m. 1948 ; div. 1971 ) ​ Children 2 Hilkka Terttu Annikki Kinnunen (19 March 1925 – 19 October 2026) was a Finnish actress, operetta singer, stage director and theatre director. She appeared in musical theatre, dramas, on radio and in film. She founded the Operettiteatteri in Helsinki, focused on operettas , in 1959 and led it until 1996, often taking lead roles and directing. The title role of Lehár's The Gypsy Princess became her signature role. She took the company on tours to Sweden, the United States and Canada. Life and career [ edit ] Kinnunen was born in Viipuri on 19 March 1925. [ 1 ] Her mother, Hilja Puustinen, ran a shop for fabrics and clothings in Vyborg , and her father, Heikki Kinnunen, worked for the State Railways ; she was their only child. [ 1 ] She had ballet lessons from age four, and her mother enrolled her at the local music school at age six, [ 1 ] [ 2 ] where she learned to play violin for six years. [ 1 ] Her family moved to Helsinki during World War II. Relatives of her mother heard her singing and encouraged her to pursue a career as a performer. She began taking voice lessons with Pia Ravenna , studied music at the Music Academy and trained diction with Helinä Svensson-Timari. [ 1 ] She was accepted to the Suomen Teatterikoulu , the Finnish theatre school, when it opened in 1943. [ 1 ] [ 3 ] During her studies, she performed at the Äänislinna War Theatre [ fi ] and appeared on Aunus Radio in the spring of 1944. [ 1 ] [ 4 ] Performer [ edit ] After graduation, Kinnunen became a member of the Workers' Theatre [ fi ] . She played three lead roles in the open-air Vallila theatre. [ 1 ] [ 4 ] In August 1945, she had a great success in the title role of Kálmán's operetta The Circus Princess , followed by her breakthrough that autumn, portraying Sylva Varescu in Lehár's The Gypsy Princess . Reviewers noted her "pure and expressive soprano" and her "confidence and elegance". It became a signature role. [ 1 ] [ 4 ] In 1946, she became engaged to Ekke Hämäläinen [ fi ] , whom she had met at drama school. They both became members of the Kansanteatteri [ fi ] (Peoples' Theatre) in 1947. Besides musical theatre, she performed drama there in plays by Shakespeare and Strindberg , with partners on stage such as Elsa Turakainen , Edvin Laine , and Leo Lähteenmäki [ fi ] . [ 1 ] [ 4 ] Kinnunen performed also in radio plays and music programs, often with Ture Ara [ fi ] and accompanied by the Radio Entertainment Orchestra conducted by George de Godzinsky . In the 1950s, regarded as the golden age of Finnish cinema, she played in films directed by Valentin Vaala and Matti Kassila , such as April's Coming in 1953. She also appeared in television entertainment in the 1960s. [ 1 ] In 1947, Kinnunen studied voice in Rome with Manlio Marcantoni for around a month, supported by a scholarship from the Leo and Regina Wainstein Foundation. On a government grant, she studied directing and singing at the Vienna Academy of Music from 1954 to 1955. She studied directing further in 1972 with Walter Felsenstein at the Komische Oper Berlin . [ 1 ] When Walter Firner [ de ] was a guest director from Vienna at the Kansanteatteri 1955 of the comedy Father Camillo and Peppone , she was his interpreter and assistant. She was then offered to direct and play the lead role in Victoria and Her Hussar in 1956, but focused on directing for production. It was regarded as "inventive and fast-paced". She then often both directed and played, including The Gypsy Princess in 1956 and Countess Maritza in 1959. [ 1 ] Theatre director [ edit ] Kinnunen as Countess Maritza , 1962 Kinnunen founded the Operettiteatteri, focused on operettas , in 1959 and led it to 1996, often taking lead roles. [ 1 ] [ 5 ] The first production was the musical Guys and Dolls at the Kulttuuritalo , a new theatre designed by Alvar Aalto with a hall seating more than 1,500 people. Her company could rent rehearsal and office space in the building. [ 1 ] She invited popular entertainers to perform, such as Georg Ots in Lehár's The Merry Widow . Performers included Tapani Kansa , Katri Helena , Lasse Mårtenson , Anneli Sari [ fi ] and Virpi Miettinen [ fi ] , conductor Mikko von Deringer [ fi ] , and choreographer Elsa Sylvestersson . [ 1 ] They toured Finland's large cities, and from the 1970s also abroad. The first production to tour nine towns in Sweden was The Countess Mariza in 1973, followed in 1974 by tours of the United States and Canada with The Gypsy Princess . They toured to cities with Finnish immigrants until the end of the 1970s. She also toured in concerts to the United States, Canada and Australia until the 1990s. [ 1 ] She was regarded as the prima donna of operetta in Finland. [ 2 ] Personal life [ edit ] From 1948 to 1971, Kinnunen was married to actor Ekke Hämäläinen; they had two children, their son Vesa Hämes [ fi ] became an actor. From 1976 to 1979, Kinnunen was married to the businessman Bill Farrell. [ 1 ] Kinnunen turned 100 on 19 March 2025, [ 6 ] and died in Helsinki on 19 October 2026, at the age of 101. [ 7 ] Legacy and awards [ edit ] On the occasion of her 80th birthday in 2005, Aino Kukkonen [ fi ] published the book Hilkka Kinnunen ― Primadonna , about her life. [ 8 ] [ 9 ] The story of her youth was told in Lotta-Sofia Saahko [ fi ] 's book Kahvia ja karjalanpiirakoita , published in 2021. [ 10 ] In 2010, President Tarja Halonen awarded her the title of teatterineuvos [ fi ] (Theatre Counsellor) for her achievements for the benefit of Finnish musical theatre. The same year, she received the Grand Cross of the Polish Order of Polonia Restituta and became Commander of the Order of Finnish Performing Arts. text: Jacqueline Van Quaille - Wikipedia Jump to content Search Search Jacqueline Van Quaille 1 language Español Edit links From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia Belgian operatic soprano (1936–2026) Jacqueline Van Quaille Van Quaille, in the 1960s Born ( 1936-10-06 ) 6 October 1936 Gentbrugge , Belgium Died 16 October 2026 (2026-10-16) (aged 90) De Panne , Belgium Education Royal Conservatory of Ghent Occupations Operatic soprano Academic teacher Organizations Ghent Opera Opernhaus Wuppertal Graz Opera Royal Conservatory of Ghent Jacqueline Van Quaille (6 October 1936 – 16 October 2026) was a Belgian operatic soprano . Based at the Ghent Opera , Opernhaus Wuppertal and Graz Opera , she appeared on stage for 56 years. [ 1 ] She performed lead roles in European opera houses, with a wide repertoire including contemporary opera and operettas . Pamina in Mozart's Die Zauberflöte and Puccini's Tosca were among her signature roles. She portrayed Isolde in Wagner's Tristan und Isolde in a 1970 television film. Later in her career, she also performed in musicals, taught at the Royal Conservatory of Ghent , and founded an operetta theatre. Life and career [ edit ] Early life [ edit ] Jacqueline Van Quaille was born in Gentbrugge on 6 October 1936. [ 1 ] [ 2 ] [ 3 ] [ 4 ] She studied at the Royal Conservatory of Ghent , voice with M. Teugels and performance with Karel Locufier. [ 1 ] After graduating in 1957, she worked first at the West Flemish Operetta Company in Kortrijk and Roeselare . [ 1 ] Belgium [ edit ] Van Quaille made her debut at the Ghent Opera in 1958 as Pamina in Mozart's Die Zauberflöte , which became one of her signature roles. [ 1 ] [ 2 ] She performed mostly French and Italian operas there. She portrayed the title role of Verdi's La traviata , studying the role with soprano Vina Bovy . She also appeared as Verdi's Desdemona in Otello and Leonora in La forza del destino , and in Puccini's title roles of La fanciulla del west and Tosca . [ 1 ] She performed in operettas such as Lehár's The Land of Smiles and The Merry Widow and The Gypsy Baron by J. Strauss. [ 1 ] Van Quaille also became a regular performer at the Antwerp Opera . [ 3 ] Elsewhere in Europe [ edit ] After Van Quaille won the King Baudouin Prize at the Verviers competition, [ 1 ] [ 3 ] she was invited to the Opernhaus Wuppertal [ 1 ] and was a member of its company from 1961 to 1964. She participated there in the world premiere of Leo Justinus Kauffmann [ de ] 's Das Perlenhemd in 1963. [ 1 ] [ 3 ] The same year, she took part in the French premiere of Busoni's Doktor Faust at the Théâtre des Champs-Élysées in Paris, alongside Mario Del Monaco in the title role. [ 1 ] During that time, she appeared at the Oper Frankfurt as Chrysothemis in Elektra by R. Strauss, alongside Astrid Varnay , and in Nice and Besançon. [ 1 ] Van Quaille worked at the Graz Opera from 1964 to 1968. She appeared as a guest at the Vienna Volksoper , at the Theater am Gärtnerplatz in Munich, [ 1 ] [ 3 ] and the Essen Opera . [ 3 ] She studied again, with Ettore Campogalliani in Mantua, [ 1 ] [ 3 ] who had also coached Renata Tebaldi and Carlo Bergonzi . [ 1 ] [ 3 ] She also auditioned to study at the academy of La Scala in Milan and was accepted, but decided to remain closer to home, where she had three children then. [ 1 ] On a tour through Romania in 1978, she appeared as Amelia in Verdi's Un ballo in maschera and in the title roles of Puccini's Manon Lescaut and Tosca . [ 3 ] She performed more dramatic roles at the Opéra Royal de Wallonie in Liège , again Leonora and Amelia, alongside Nicolae Herlea and Barry Morell , Giordano's Andrea Chénier alongside Alain Vanzo , the title role of Arabella and Lady Macbeth in Verdi's Macbeth . [ 1 ] She portrayed Sieglinde in Wagner's Die Walküre in the 1983 opening of the Vlaamse Opera . [ 3 ] Her operatic repertoire included leading roles in Mozart operas , [ 3 ] the title role in Beethoven's Fidelio , [ 1 ] Matilda in Rossini's Guillaume Tell , [ 2 ] the title role of Zandonai's Francesca da Rimini , Marietta in Korngold's Die tote Stadt , the Marschallin in Der Rosenkavalier by R. Strauss, Giorgietta in Puccini's Il tabarro , Santuzza in Mascagni's Cavalleria rusticana , Ursula in Hindemith's Mathis der Maler . She performed roles in d'Albert's Tiefland , Wagner's Tannhäuser and La Damnation de Faust by Berlioz, [ 1 ] and in works by Gounod , Massenet , and Dvořák . [ 3 ] She also performed in contemporary operas, [ 1 ] [ 3 ] such as Magda Sorel in Menotti’s The Consul . [ 1 ] Van Quaille performed in Ghent and Antwerp regularly until 1988. In Ghent she appeared in Cilea's Adriana Lecouvreur alongside Rita Gorr . [ 1 ] One day in Ghent, she sang in a concert in the morning in the Feestzaal at Vooruit, then in an afternoon premiere of La forza del destino , and again in the evening as Tosca. [ 1 ] She appeared at the Dutch National Opera in 1989 as Leonora in Il trovatore ; Opera Magazine Netherlands reported that she excelled even in a mediocre performance. [ 1 ] She performed at La Monnaie in Brussels as Juno in Offenbach's Orphée aux Enfers in 1997, [ 3 ] and also in Les Troyens by Berlioz, alongside Guy Chauvet , and in Wagner's Der fliegende Holländer . She appeared as Larina in Tchaikovsky’s Eugene Onegin at both the Aix-en-Provence Festival and the Salzburg Festival . In Salzburg she performed in 2000 as Bacchis in Offenbach's La belle Hélène , staged by Herbert Wernicke . [ 1 ] In 2014, she performed at LOD muziektheater [ nl ] in their production of Ghost Road . [ 1 ] Recordings and films [ edit ] Van Quaille appeared in television opera films for RTBF including Manon Lescaut and Verdi's Don Carlos . She portrayed Isolde in Wagner's Tristan und Isolde , alongside Claude Heater as Tristan, filmed in 1968 on the Belgian coast and at the Gravensteen in Ghent, [ 1 ] and released in 1970. She recorded the musicals Kuifje – De Zonnetempel [ 3 ] and The Sound of Music on CD. She also appeared in Orphée aux Enfers on DVD [ 3 ] in 1979 and in Eugene Onegin in 2002. [ 2 ] She also appeared as Bianca Castafiore in the animated film Tintin and the Temple of the Sun . [ 1 ] [ 5 ] [ 6 ] The music critic Ronny de Schepper noted that her vibrato made her unintelligible and there was insufficient acting. [ 7 ] Her final performance was in a short film in Ghent language, Passé . [ 1 ] Concert and teaching [ edit ] Van Quaille was also a noted concert singer. [ 3 ] She founded her own operetta company, Aruna. [ 1 ] [ 2 ] [ 6 ] She taught at the Music Academy of Ghent, [ 2 ] the music school of Veurne , [ 3 ] and privately. [ 2 ] Personal life [ edit ] Van Quaille had three children. [ 1 ] She died in De Panne on 16 October 2026, at the age of 90. text: Juan Francisco Solórzano Foppa - Wikipedia Jump to content Search Search Juan Francisco Solórzano Foppa 3 languages Español Euskara Volapük Edit links From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia Guatemalan attorney and prosecutor (1983–2026) Juan Francisco Solórzano Foppa Head of the Tax Administration Superintendency [ es ] In office 9 March 2016 – 15 January 2018 President Jimmy Morales Preceded by Juan Francisco Rivera Succeeded by Abel Cruz Calderón Personal details Born ( 1983-07-26 ) 26 July 1983 Died 17 October 2026 (2026-10-17) (aged 43) Guatemala City, Guatemala Cause of death Assassination by gunshot Relatives Alaide Foppa (grandmother) Education Rafael Landívar University Juan Francisco Solórzano Foppa [ a ] (26 July 1983 – 17 October 2026) was a Guatemalan prosecutor, anti-corruption activist and politician. He was best known for his work to stop government corruption and organized crime. He served as the head of the Tax Administration Superintendency [ es ] , Guatemala's tax agency, before being removed by the president, and he previously headed criminal investigations at the Attorney General of Guatemala 's office. He ran for mayor of Guatemala City [ es ] in 2023. Life and career [ edit ] Foppa was born on 26 July 1983 in Nicaragua, [ 3 ] according to Silvia Solórzano Foppa, his mother. [ 4 ] He was the grandson of poet and activist Alaíde Foppa , who was forcibly disappeared three years prior. [ 5 ] His father, Carlos Enrique López Arévalo, "Comandante Camilo", was a leftist guerrilla fighter during the Guatemalan Civil War and was killed two weeks after his son's birth. [ 6 ] [ 7 ] His mother was also a guerrilla. [ 2 ] He grew up in Cuba before the family returned to Guatemala following the signing of the Peace Accords in 1996. [ 7 ] Foppa decided to study law and attended Rafael Landívar University . [ 3 ] Foppa began as an assistant prosecutor in the Attorney General of Guatemala 's office, where among other cases, he prosecuted homicides and organized crimes. He then became head of an office for criminal investigations that had been newly created in 2013. As head, he was responsible for the investigation and arrest of President Otto Pérez Molina for allegedly leading the bribery ring known as La Línea . He also investigated the customs tax department and headed the investigation of steel company Aceros de Guatemala. [ 6 ] In March 2016, he was appointed by President Jimmy Morales to head the Tax Administration Superintendency [ es ] as Superintendent, which made him in charge of Guatemala's tax. [ 8 ] Conservative think tanks immediately became alarmed, with one stating that he would "commit fiscal terrorism". [ 9 ] In this position, he continued with Aceros de Guatemala, alleging they owed US$100 million in taxes, fees, and interest. The company denied this, and as such Foppa tried to seize control of the company's finances. Aceros paid the fees, the largest tax fine in Guatemalan history, but has maintained its innocence. He also investigated and extracted US$5.8 million in back taxes, fines, and interest from a company which owned hotels, partially by arresting its owner. [ 6 ] He investigated many similar cases, and by the end of his term extracted US$280 million. However, he later acknowledged his actions were "too aggressive", and detractors stated he "turned administrative cases into criminal cases". He also restructured the agency, removing individuals he alleged were complicit in helping companies perform tax fraud. [ 6 ] He tweeted out names of companies he suspected of committing tax fraud, [ 2 ] and even insisted his mother catch up with her taxes on Mother's Day. [ 6 ] During this time, he was seen as an important member of the anti-corruption wing of the government, along with Attorney General Thelma Aldana and Interior Minister Francisco Rivas Lara . However, he was fired by Morales for missing his goal by 0.3%, which many thought was a mere pretext to remove him for his anti-corruption fight. [ 2 ] In 2021, the government of Guatemala simultaneously dropped the charges against Pérez Molina and pressed charges against Foppa, allegedly for signature fraud as he began to try to start his own political party. [ 10 ] They also charged him with illicit association and conspiracy, both of which were dropped by the case judge. [ 6 ] Around this time, he left the country and lived in Washington, D.C. , for a period. [ 11 ] In 2022, he became defense counsel for José Rubén Zamora , a media executive who had been arrested under charges of money laundering which both international observers and Zamora viewed as manipulated and as part of an effort to prevent Zamora's reporting. He resigned as defense attorney in March 2023 due to his concerns that he might be charged himself for defending Zamora. [ 12 ] [ 13 ] He ran for mayor of Guatemala City in 2023 as the candidate of a coalition led by the Movimiento Semilla . He was polling in second place, but was ultimately unable to complete his campaign as a result of the Supreme Electoral Tribunal revoking his permission: he was arrested for what was alleged to be obstruction of justice stemming from his defense of Zamora. [ 12 ] He pled guilty, [ 14 ] stating he didn't believe he'd receive a fair trial. [ 15 ] Foppa was also a volunteer firefighter , and spent thirteen years with the municipal fire brigade. [ 16 ] [ 17 ] [ 18 ] On 15 October 2026, Foppa alleged that the CIA and the Guatemalan army held an operation which resulted in the deaths of eight people in Huité , department of Zacapa. [ 19 ] Assassination [ edit ] On 17 October 2026, Foppa was killed by four men in athletic clothing who shot him more than 50 times while he was attending a soccer match in Guatemala City 's Zone 5. He was 43 years old. The Guatemalan government described the incident as an "execution-style" attack. His four security guards were just thirty to forty meters away, protecting his 14-year-old son. Democracy Now! and local journalists characterized the killing as an assassination, and President Bernardo Arévalo called for a full investigation. [ 20 ] [ 5 ] [ 21 ] Another person was also killed and five more injured during the shooting. [ 22 ] Two young men in possession of a firearm were arrested in the immediate aftermath but later released by a judge on the grounds of insufficient evidence linking them to the killings.
